offenses.summary: With intent to promote or assist another's suicide, aids or attempts to aid them in committing or attempting suicide.

tiers.when: Conduct causes a suicide, or an attempted suicide that results in serious bodily injury

offenses.heading: AIDING SUICIDE

offenses.group: Title 5. Offenses Against the Person
offenses.name: Tampering with Consumer Product
offenses.summary: Knowingly or intentionally tampers with a consumer product knowing it will be sold or given to the public, or threatens to tamper to cause fear, affect sales, or cause injury.

tiers.when: Tampering, and a person suffers serious bodily injury

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH CONSUMER PRODUCT

offenses.group: Title 5. Offenses Against the Person
offenses.name: Leaving a Child in a Vehicle
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly leaves a child younger than 7 in a motor vehicle for longer than five minutes without someone 14 or older in the vehicle.
offenses.heading: LEAVING A CHILD IN A VEHICLE

offenses.group: Title 5. Offenses Against the Person
offenses.name: Harassment by Persons in Certain Facilities; Harassment of Public Servant
offenses.summary: With intent to assault, harass, or alarm, causes another person to contact blood, semen, saliva, urine, feces, or other fluid: while confined in a correctional or detention facility; while in a civil commitment facility (against staff); or against a public servant lawfully discharging an official duty or in retaliation.
offenses.heading: HARASSMENT BY PERSONS IN CERTAIN FACILITIES; HARASSMENT OF PUBLIC SERVANT

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Bigamy
offenses.summary: A legally married person marries, purports to marry, or lives as married with someone other than their spouse; or a person knowingly does so with someone else's spouse.

tiers.when: The other person is 17 years old
The other person is 16 or younger

offenses.heading: BIGAMY

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Prohibited Sexual Conduct
offenses.summary: Engages in sexual intercourse or deviate sexual intercourse with a person the actor knows is a close relative: ancestor or descendant, current or former stepchild or stepparent, aunt or uncle, sibling, niece or nephew, or first cousin.

tiers.when: With an ancestor or descendant by blood or adoption (a)(1)

offenses.heading: PROHIBITED SEXUAL CONDUCT

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Interference with Child Custody
offenses.summary: Takes or retains a child younger than 18 knowing it violates a custody order, or takes the child out of the court's area while a custody suit is pending; or a noncustodial parent entices the child away from the custodial parent.
offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH CHILD CUSTODY

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Agreement to Abduct from Custody
offenses.summary: Agrees, for payment or the promise of payment, to abduct a child younger than 18 from a person who has custody under a court order, by force, threat, misrepresentation, stealth, or unlawful entry.
offenses.heading: AGREEMENT TO ABDUCT FROM CUSTODY

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Enticing a Child
offenses.summary: With intent to interfere with lawful custody of a child younger than 18, knowingly entices, persuades, or takes the child from a parent or guardian.

tiers.when: Actor intended to commit a felony against the child

offenses.heading: ENTICING A CHILD

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Criminal Nonsupport
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly fails to provide support for the person's child younger than 18, or for a child covered by a court support order.
offenses.heading: CRIMINAL NONSUPPORT

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Harboring Runaway Child
offenses.summary: Knowingly harbors a child, criminally negligent about whether the child is under 18 and has escaped from custody or is a runaway (away from home without parental consent for a substantial time or without intent to return).
offenses.heading: HARBORING RUNAWAY CHILD

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Violation of Certain Court Orders or Conditions of Bond in a Family Violence, Child Abuse or Neglect, Sexual Assault or Abuse, Indecent Assault, Stalking, or Trafficking Case
offenses.summary: Knowingly or intentionally violates a protective order, magistrate's order for emergency protection, or a bond condition in a family violence, sexual assault, indecent assault, stalking, or trafficking case: by committing family violence or certain offenses; communicating with the protected person; going to or near their home, work, school, or child care; possessing a firearm; or removing or tampering with a GPS monitor.

tiers.when: Violated a post-conviction protective order issued for the victim of that offense
Violated the order or bond condition in a listed manner while possessing a deadly weapon
Two or more prior convictions under this section or 25.072 (or one of each)
Violation was committed by an assault or by stalking

offenses.heading: VIOLATION OF CERTAIN COURT ORDERS OR CONDITIONS OF BOND IN A FAMILY VIOLENCE, CHILD ABUSE OR NEGLECT, SEXUAL ASSAULT OR ABUSE, INDECENT ASSAULT, STALKING, OR TRAFFICKING CASE

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Violation of Protective Order Preventing Offense Caused by Bias or Prejudice
offenses.summary: Knowingly or intentionally violates a protective order issued to prevent an offense motivated by bias or prejudice: by committing a bias-motivated offense, communicating with or threatening the protected person, or going to or near their home or workplace.

tiers.when: Two or more prior convictions under this section, or the violation was an assault

offenses.heading: VIOLATION OF PROTECTIVE ORDER PREVENTING OFFENSE CAUSED BY BIAS OR PREJUDICE

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Repeated Violation of Certain Court Orders or Conditions of Bond in Family Violence, Child Abuse or Neglect, Sexual Assault or Abuse, Indecent Assault, Stalking, or Trafficking Case
offenses.summary: During a period of 12 months or less, two or more times engages in conduct that is a violation of a protective order or bond condition under 25.07.

tiers.when: At least one violation was punishable as a state jail felony under 25.07(g)(1)(B) (deadly weapon)

offenses.heading: REPEATED VIOLATION OF CERTAIN COURT ORDERS OR CONDITIONS OF BOND IN FAMILY VIOLENCE, CHILD ABUSE OR NEGLECT, SEXUAL ASSAULT OR ABUSE, INDECENT ASSAULT, STALKING, OR TRAFFICKING CASE

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Sale or Purchase of Child
offenses.summary: Accepts or offers to accept something of value for delivering a child younger than 18 to another for adoption, or gives something of value to acquire a child for adoption (outside permitted adoption fees).

tiers.when: With intent to commit trafficking, child sex offenses, or sexual performance by a child

offenses.heading: SALE OR PURCHASE OF CHILD

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Unregulated Custody Transfer of Adopted Child
offenses.summary: Knowingly conducts, facilitates, or participates in an unregulated custody transfer of an adopted child ("rehoming" without court or agency involvement).

tiers.when: With intent to commit trafficking, child sex offenses, or child pornography offenses

offenses.heading: UNREGULATED CUSTODY TRANSFER OF ADOPTED CHILD

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Advertising for Placement of Child
offenses.summary: Advertises in the public media that the person will place, provide, or obtain a child for adoption or permanent custody (licensed agencies excepted).
offenses.heading: ADVERTISING FOR PLACEMENT OF CHILD

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Interference with Rights of Guardian of the Person
offenses.summary: Takes, retains, or conceals a ward knowing it interferes with a guardian's possessory right.
offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH RIGHTS OF GUARDIAN OF THE PERSON

offenses.group: Title 6. Offenses Against the Family
offenses.name: Continuous Violence Against the Family
offenses.summary: Within 12 months or less, two or more times commits bodily-injury assault (22.01(a)(1)) against persons in a family, household, or dating relationship (Family Code 71.0021(b), 71.003, 71.005).
offenses.notes: The two assaults may be against the same or different family members, and no prior conviction is needed.
offenses.heading: CONTINUOUS VIOLENCE AGAINST THE FAMILY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Arson
offenses.summary: Starts a fire or causes an explosion with intent to destroy or damage vegetation, a fence, or a structure on open-space land, or a building, habitation, or vehicle under listed circumstances (in a city, insured, mortgaged, belonging to another, etc.). Also covers reckless fires while making drugs (a-1) and intentional fires that recklessly damage another's building or injure someone (a-2).

tiers.when: Bodily injury or death suffered by any person
Property targeted was a habitation or a place of assembly or worship
Reckless fire or explosion while manufacturing a controlled substance (a-1)
Same, and bodily injury or death suffered by any person
Intentional fire that recklessly damages another's building or injures someone (a-2)

offenses.heading: ARSON

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Criminal Mischief
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, intentionally or knowingly damages, destroys, or tampers with (causing loss or substantial inconvenience) the owner's tangible property, or makes markings on it.

tiers.when: Pecuniary loss less than $100, or causes substantial inconvenience
$750 to less than $2,500; or impairs or diverts a public water supply

$2,500 to less than $30,000; habitation damaged by firearm or explosive (under $2,500); livestock or game fence (under $2,500); impairs flood control, dam, or public communications, transport, or gas (under $30,000); or vehicle damaged removing a catalytic converter (under $30,000)
$30,000 to less than $150,000; kills cattle, bison, or horses; impairs ATM access; or impairs public power supply (under $150,000)
$150,000 to less than $300,000; or $1,000 to $300,000 to a habitation while committing criminal trespass
Place of worship or burial, public monument, or community center, loss $750 to less than $30,000
School or college, loss $750 to less than $30,000
Livestock infected with mad cow disease or another listed animal disease
Transportation communications equipment, loss less than $150,000
Copper or brass component of a critical infrastructure facility, causing impairment

offenses.heading: CRIMINAL MISCHIEF

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Reckless Damage or Destruction
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, recklessly damages or destroys the owner's property.
offenses.heading: RECKLESS DAMAGE OR DESTRUCTION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Actor's Interest in Property
offenses.summary: Not an offense. It is no defense to a property-damage charge that the actor also has an interest in the property, if another person has an interest the actor may not infringe.
offenses.heading: ACTOR'S INTEREST IN PROPERTY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Amount of Pecuniary Loss
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Explains how pecuniary loss is measured for Chapter 28: fair market value (or replacement cost) if destroyed; repair or restoration cost if damaged; special rules for documents; and if the loss cannot be determined, it is deemed more than $750 but less than $2,500.
offenses.heading: AMOUNT OF PECUNIARY LOSS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Interference with Railroad Property
offenses.summary: Throws an object or shoots at a train or rail work equipment; or without consent enters railroad property, tampers with it, places an obstruction on the track, or causes a derailment.

tiers.when: Throwing or shooting at a train (b)(1)
Throwing or shooting, causing bodily injury
Entering or remaining on railroad property (b)(2)(A)
Tampering, obstruction, or derailment (b)(2)(B)-(D), loss under $100

offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH RAILROAD PROPERTY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Graffiti
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, intentionally or knowingly makes markings (inscriptions, slogans, drawings, paintings) on the owner's property using paint, an indelible marker, or an etching or engraving device.

tiers.when: Marking on a school, college, place of worship or burial, public monument, or community center, loss $750 to less than $30,000

offenses.heading: GRAFFITI

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.chapter: Ch. 28 Arson, Criminal Mischief, and Other Property Damage or Destruction
offenses.name: Damaging Critical Infrastructure Facility
offenses.summary: Without the consent of the owner or operator, intentionally or knowingly damages, destroys, vandalizes, or impairs a critical infrastructure facility and thereby causes an extended power outage.

tiers.when: Pecuniary damage to the facility of $100,000 or more
Actor used a firearm, drone, cyber attack, or explosive weapon

offenses.heading: DAMAGING CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Robbery
offenses.summary: In the course of committing theft and with intent to obtain or keep control of the property, intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causes bodily injury to another, or intentionally or knowingly threatens or places another in fear of imminent bodily injury or death.
offenses.heading: ROBBERY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Aggravated Robbery
offenses.summary: Commits robbery and causes serious bodily injury, uses or exhibits a deadly weapon, or causes bodily injury to (or threatens or places in fear) a person 65 or older or a disabled person.
offenses.heading: AGGRAVATED ROBBERY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Jugging
offenses.summary: With intent to steal another person's money, knowingly follows them from a business or financial institution along the same route while possessing two or more criminal instruments ("jugging").

tiers.when: Actor commits burglary of a vehicle during the offense
Actor commits robbery during the offense

offenses.heading: JUGGING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Burglary
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent: enters a habitation, or a building not then open to the public, with intent to commit a felony, theft, or assault; remains concealed with that intent; or enters and commits or attempts a felony, theft, or assault.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed only "State Jail Felony". The level depends on the type of premises and intent.

tiers.when: Commercial building where controlled substances are stored (pharmacy, clinic, hospital, warehouse), with intent to steal a controlled substance
Building other than a habitation, while committing smuggling of persons under 20.05(a)(2)
Habitation, and a party entered with intent to commit, or committed or attempted, a felony other than felony theft

offenses.heading: BURGLARY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Burglary of Coin-Operated or Coin Collection Machines
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, breaks into or enters a coin-operated or coin collection machine or receptacle with intent to obtain property or services.
offenses.heading: BURGLARY OF COIN-OPERATED OR COIN COLLECTION MACHINES

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Burglary of Vehicles
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, breaks into or enters a vehicle or any part of a vehicle with intent to commit any felony or theft.

tiers.when: One prior conviction under this section
Two or more prior convictions under this section
Vehicle of a wholesale prescription drug distributor, with intent to steal a controlled substance

offenses.heading: BURGLARY OF VEHICLES

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Criminal Trespass
offenses.summary: Enters or remains on or in another's property (land, building, vehicle, RV park, etc.) without effective consent, and had notice that entry was forbidden or received notice to depart and failed to do so. Notice includes oral or written communication, fencing, signs, purple paint marks, or crops under cultivation.

tiers.when: On agricultural land within 100 feet of its boundary, or on residential land within 100 feet of a protected freshwater area
In a habitation or shelter center, on a Superfund site, or in a critical infrastructure facility
On college property, with a prior conviction for trespassing on college property
At a general residential operation operating as a residential treatment center
Only reason entry was forbidden is that the person carried a firearm or other weapon
Same, but after entering the person was personally told weapons were forbidden and failed to depart

offenses.heading: CRIMINAL TRESPASS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Trespass by License Holder with a Concealed Handgun
offenses.summary: A handgun license holder carries a concealed handgun on another's property without effective consent after receiving notice (oral or written, including a 30.06 sign) that concealed carry by license holders is forbidden.

tiers.when: After entering, was personally told orally that concealed carry is forbidden and failed to depart

offenses.heading: TRESPASS BY LICENSE HOLDER WITH A CONCEALED HANDGUN

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Trespass by License Holder with an Openly Carried Handgun
offenses.summary: A handgun license holder openly carries a handgun on another's property without effective consent after receiving notice (oral or written, including a 30.07 sign) that open carry by license holders is forbidden.

tiers.when: After entering, was personally told orally that open carry is forbidden and failed to depart

offenses.heading: TRESPASS BY LICENSE HOLDER WITH AN OPENLY CARRIED HANDGUN

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft
offenses.summary: Unlawfully appropriates property (without the owner's effective consent, or knowing it was stolen by another) with intent to deprive the owner of it. Includes shoplifting and receiving stolen property.

tiers.when: Less than $100, with any prior theft conviction
Property is a driver's license, commercial driver's license, or ID certificate
$2,500 to less than $30,000; or fewer than 10 head of sheep, swine, or goats under $30,000
Any value, taken from the person of another, or from a corpse or grave (including military grave markers)
Less than $2,500, with two or more prior theft convictions
Official election ballot or carrier envelope
Aluminum, bronze, copper, or brass worth less than $20,000
Catalytic converter with replacement cost less than $30,000
Less than $30,000, stolen in a disaster area by a (purported) disaster volunteer

$30,000 to less than $150,000; cattle, horses, or exotic livestock or fowl under $150,000; 10 or more head of sheep, swine, or goats under $150,000; or controlled substance under $150,000 from a pharmacy, clinic, hospital, or drug-distributor vehicle
ATM or its contents or components, less than $300,000

Actor was a public servant or government contractor and got the property through that position; owner was elderly (65+) or a nonprofit; Medicare provider; or actor set off or disabled a fire exit alarm or retail theft detector, or used a shielding device (applies to (e)(1)-(6))
Catalytic converter theft while possessing a firearm (applies to (e)(4)-(6))
Copper or brass taken from a critical infrastructure facility (applies to (e)(4)-(6))

offenses.heading: THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft of Service
offenses.summary: With intent to avoid payment for a service the actor knows requires payment: secures the service by deception, threat, or false token; diverts services; keeps rented property past the rental period without consent; or fails to return or pay for rental property after notice (see the statute for all means).
offenses.heading: THEFT OF SERVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft of Trade Secrets
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent, knowingly steals a trade secret, copies an article representing one, or communicates or transmits one.

tiers.when: Intended to benefit a foreign agent, government, or instrumentality

offenses.heading: THEFT OF TRADE SECRETS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Presumption for Theft by Check or Similar Sight Order
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Writing or passing a check without sufficient funds is prima facie evidence of intent to deprive (theft) or avoid payment (theft of service) if the issuer had no account, or the bank refused payment for insufficient funds (presented within 30 days of issue) and the issuer did not pay in full within 10 days after notice of the refusal (except postdated checks).
offenses.heading: PRESUMPTION FOR THEFT BY CHECK OR SIMILAR SIGHT ORDER

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unauthorized Use of a Vehicle
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly operates another's boat, airplane, or motor-propelled vehicle without the owner's effective consent.
offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF A VEHICLE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Value
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Value for theft is fair market value at the time and place of the offense (or replacement cost if that can't be determined), with special rules for documents and services; if value cannot be determined, it is deemed $750 to less than $2,500.
offenses.heading: VALUE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Aggregation of Amounts Involved in Theft
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Amounts obtained under one scheme or continuing course of conduct, from one or several sources, may be added together to set the grade of the theft offense.
offenses.heading: AGGREGATION OF AMOUNTS INVOLVED IN THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Actor's Interest in Property
offenses.summary: Not an offense. It is no defense to theft that the actor has an interest in the property if another person has the right of exclusive possession.
offenses.heading: ACTOR'S INTEREST IN PROPERTY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Tampering with Identification Numbers
offenses.summary: Knowingly or intentionally removes, alters, or obliterates a serial number or other permanent identification marking on personal property; or possesses or sells property knowing (or when a reasonable person would know) the number was removed or altered.
offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH IDENTIFICATION NUMBERS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft of or Tampering with Multichannel Video or Information Services
offenses.summary: Without the provider's authorization, connects to or tampers with a cable TV or other multichannel video or information services system, or attaches a device, to receive service without paying.

tiers.when: One prior conviction under this section
Committed for remuneration, with two or more prior convictions

offenses.heading: THEFT OF OR TAMPERING WITH MULTICHANNEL VIDEO OR INFORMATION SERVICES

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Manufacture, Distribution, or Advertisement of Multichannel Video or Information Services Device
offenses.summary: For remuneration, makes, modifies, imports, distributes, advertises, or offers for sale a device, kit, or plan designed to decode a cable or other multichannel video signal, intending to aid theft of that service.
offenses.heading: MANUFACTURE, DISTRIBUTION, OR ADVERTISEMENT OF MULTICHANNEL VIDEO OR INFORMATION SERVICES DEVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Sale or Lease of Multichannel Video or Information Services Device
offenses.summary: Sells or leases a device, kit, or plan designed to decode a cable or other multichannel video signal, intending to aid theft of that service.
offenses.heading: SALE OR LEASE OF MULTICHANNEL VIDEO OR INFORMATION SERVICES DEVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Possession, Manufacture, or Distribution of Certain Instruments Used to Commit Retail Theft
offenses.summary: With intent to commit theft, possesses a shielding or deactivation instrument (such as a foil-lined "booster bag" or tag remover), or knowingly makes, sells, or distributes one.
offenses.heading: POSSESSION, MANUFACTURE, OR DISTRIBUTION OF CERTAIN INSTRUMENTS USED TO COMMIT RETAIL THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Organized Retail Theft
offenses.summary: Unlawfully takes merchandise or property from a merchant while acting in concert with others, or on two or more occasions within 180 days; knowingly benefits from such theft by another; or acts with others to overwhelm a merchant's security response or a peace officer (see the statute for related conduct).
offenses.notes: This ladder is one step higher than ordinary theft at each value. A deferred adjudication for this offense counts as a conviction for Chapter 12 repeat-offender enhancement (subsection (e)).
offenses.heading: ORGANIZED RETAIL THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unauthorized Acquisition or Transfer of Certain Financial Information
offenses.summary: Knowing the person is not entitled to it, obtains another's check or payment card information with a device that reads or records it (a "skimmer"), or transfers that information to a third party.

tiers.when: Transferring it to a third party (b)(2)

offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ACQUISITION OR TRANSFER OF CERTAIN FINANCIAL INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Cargo Theft
offenses.summary: Knowingly receives, possesses, conceals, stores, sells, or disposes of stolen cargo (or cargo represented as stolen); or a driver contracted to haul cargo fails to deliver it, intending to do so.
offenses.notes: No penalty is listed for cargo under $1,500; ordinary theft may apply.

tiers.when: Total cargo value $1,500 to less than $10,000
Actor organized, supervised, financed, or managed others in the activity (applies to (c)(1)-(3))

offenses.heading: CARGO THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft of Petroleum Product or Oil and Gas Equipment
offenses.summary: Unlawfully appropriates a petroleum product (by taking, transporting, or tapping a pipeline or tank) or oil and gas equipment with intent to deprive the owner; or transports petroleum of unknown origin to a waste site; or buys from an unauthorized seller.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed this as a state jail felony. Current law starts at third degree (amended 2025).

tiers.when: Oil and gas equipment worth less than $10,000
Oil and gas equipment $10,000 to less than $100,000
Oil and gas equipment $100,000 or more

offenses.heading: THEFT OF PETROLEUM PRODUCT OR OIL AND GAS EQUIPMENT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Mail Theft
offenses.summary: Intentionally takes mail without the addressee's consent, intending to deprive the addressee of it or to steal a negotiable instrument (check, money order, etc.).

tiers.when: Mail contained identifying information and intent to commit identity fraud (32.51): fewer than 10 addressees
Negotiable instruments taken to commit a Chapter 32 fraud offense: 5 or fewer instruments
Same: more than 5 but fewer than 10
Identity-fraud tiers (d)(1)-(3), when an addressee was known to be elderly or disabled
Negotiable-instrument tiers (d-1)(1)-(3), when an addressee was known to be elderly or disabled

offenses.heading: MAIL THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unauthorized Possession of Catalytic Converter
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly possesses a catalytic converter that has been removed from a vehicle, without being a person authorized to possess one (such as a dealer, repair shop, recycler, or the vehicle owner with documentation).

tiers.when: Prior conviction under this section; conspiracy to steal or damage for a catalytic converter; or possessed a firearm

offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC CONVERTER

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unauthorized Possession of Certain Copper or Brass Material
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly possesses copper or brass material (as defined in the section) without being a person authorized to possess it.

tiers.when: Taken from a critical infrastructure facility; prior conviction under this section or a related copper/brass theft, mischief, or organized crime offense; related conspiracy or organized crime; or possessed a firearm

offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED POSSESSION OF CERTAIN COPPER OR BRASS MATERIAL

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Real Property Theft
offenses.summary: Without the owner's effective consent and with intent to deprive, brings about (or attempts) a transfer of real property, title, or an interest in it; or sells, transfers, or encumbers real property the actor has no right to (see the statute for (b)(2)).

tiers.when: Transfer under (b)(1), real property market value less than $300,000
Transfer under (b)(1), market value $300,000 or more
Sale or encumbrance under (b)(2), benefit received less than $30,000
Owner was elderly, disabled, or a nonprofit, or the property was a residence homestead

offenses.heading: REAL PROPERTY THEFT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Forgery
offenses.summary: Forges a writing (makes, alters, completes, issues, transfers, or possesses with intent to pass a writing that purports to be another's act or authorized when it is not) with intent to defraud or harm another.

tiers.when: Will, deed, mortgage, security agreement, credit card, check, debit authorization, contract, release, or other commercial instrument
Money, securities, stamps; a listed government record (37.01(2)(C)); or government-issued instruments, stocks, or bonds
Forged to obtain property or service: value less than $100
Committed against an elderly individual (65 or older) (except the (e-1)(6) tier)

offenses.heading: FORGERY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Criminal Simulation
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or harm, makes or alters an object so it appears more valuable because of age, rarity, source, or authorship; possesses such an object to sell or pass it; or authenticates it as genuine.
offenses.heading: CRIMINAL SIMULATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Trademark Counterfeiting
offenses.summary: Intentionally makes, displays, advertises, distributes, sells, or possesses with intent to sell a counterfeit mark, or goods or services the person knows (or should know) bear a counterfeit mark.
offenses.heading: TRADEMARK COUNTERFEITING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Stealing or Receiving Stolen Check or Similar Sight Order
offenses.summary: Steals an unsigned check or similar sight order, or, knowing it was stolen, receives one with intent to use, sell, or transfer it.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed this as a Class A misdemeanor, and its statute link held pasted text. Current law makes it a state jail felony (amended 2025).
offenses.heading: STEALING OR RECEIVING STOLEN CHECK OR SIMILAR SIGHT ORDER

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Credit Card or Debit Card Abuse
offenses.summary: With intent to obtain a benefit fraudulently, uses a credit or debit card knowing it was not issued to them and is used without consent, or is expired or revoked; uses a fictitious card; steals or knowingly receives a stolen card; buys or sells a card; or other listed card fraud.

tiers.when: Committed against an elderly individual (65 or older)

offenses.heading: CREDIT CARD OR DEBIT CARD ABUSE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Use or Possession of Credit Card or Debit Card Information
offenses.summary: With intent to harm or defraud, obtains, possesses, transfers, or uses a counterfeit credit or debit card, or another person's card number and expiration date or card data without consent.
offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT USE OR POSSESSION OF CREDIT CARD OR DEBIT CARD INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: False Statement to Obtain Property or Credit or in the Provision of Certain Services
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly makes a materially false or misleading written statement to obtain property or credit (including a mortgage loan), or in a paid real estate appraisal.

tiers.when: Value of property or credit less than $100

offenses.heading: FALSE STATEMENT TO OBTAIN PROPERTY OR CREDIT OR IN THE PROVISION OF CERTAIN SERVICES

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Hindering Secured Creditors
offenses.summary: With intent to hinder a secured creditor, a person who signed a security agreement, mortgage, or deed of trust destroys, removes, conceals, encumbers, or reduces the value of the property (b); or a debtor sells the secured property or keeps the proceeds with intent to appropriate them (e).

tiers.when: Selling secured property or keeping proceeds (e): same value ladder, less than $100 through $300,000 or more

offenses.heading: HINDERING SECURED CREDITORS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Transfer of a Motor Vehicle
offenses.summary: Takes possession of another's motor vehicle under an agreement to arrange its transfer to a third party, and: transfers it without the lienholder's or lessor's written authorization; transfers or disposes of it intending to defraud or harm the owner; or does not disclose where the vehicle is when the owner or lienholder asks.

tiers.when: Transfer or disposal (b)(1)-(3): vehicle worth less than $30,000
Not disclosing the vehicle's location on request (b)(4)

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT TRANSFER OF A MOTOR VEHICLE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Credit Card Transaction Record Laundering
offenses.summary: An authorized vendor, with intent to defraud, presents to a creditor a credit card record of a sale the vendor did not make (credit card "factoring"); or a person causes a vendor to do so.
offenses.heading: CREDIT CARD TRANSACTION RECORD LAUNDERING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Issuance of Bad Check or Similar Sight Order
offenses.summary: Issues or passes a check or similar sight order knowing the issuer does not have sufficient funds to pay it and all other outstanding checks.

tiers.when: Check was for court-ordered child support

offenses.heading: ISSUANCE OF BAD CHECK OR SIMILAR SIGHT ORDER

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Deceptive Business Practices
offenses.summary: In the course of business, commits a listed deceptive practice: false weights or measures, short-selling quantity, adulterated or mislabeled goods, passing off goods as another's, false or misleading advertising, bait-and-switch, and others.

tiers.when: Practices (b)(1)-(6), with criminal negligence and no prior conviction
Practices (b)(1)-(6), intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly, or with a prior Class B or C conviction under this section

offenses.heading: DECEPTIVE BUSINESS PRACTICES

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Commercial Bribery
offenses.summary: A fiduciary (agent, employee, trustee, lawyer, etc.) without the beneficiary's consent solicits or accepts a benefit to influence their conduct for the beneficiary; or a person offers or confers that benefit.
offenses.heading: COMMERCIAL BRIBERY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Rigging Publicly Exhibited Contest
offenses.summary: With intent to affect the outcome of a publicly exhibited contest, offers a benefit to or threatens a participant or official, or tampers with a person, animal, or thing against the rules; or solicits or accepts such a benefit.
offenses.heading: RIGGING PUBLICLY EXHIBITED CONTEST

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Illegal Recruitment of an Athlete
offenses.summary: Without the college's consent, solicits or accepts a benefit to influence enrolling at a college and playing intercollegiate athletics, or offers or confers such a benefit.
offenses.heading: ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT OF AN ATHLETE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Misapplication of Fiduciary Property or Property of Financial Institution
offenses.summary: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly misapplies property held as a fiduciary or property of a financial institution in a way that creates substantial risk of loss to the owner or beneficiary.

tiers.when: Committed against an elderly individual (65 or older) (tiers (c)(1)-(6))

offenses.heading: MISAPPLICATION OF FIDUCIARY PROPERTY OR PROPERTY OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Securing of Document Execution
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or harm, causes another to sign or execute a document affecting property, service, or a pecuniary interest without effective consent (a)(1); or causes a public servant to file a document from a fake court or "sovereign citizen" type entity (a)(2).

tiers.when: Signing or executing (a)(1): value less than $100
Filing a document from a fake court or entity (a)(2)
Committed against an elderly individual (65 or older), or involves the state Medicaid program

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT SECURING OF DOCUMENT EXECUTION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Destruction, Removal, or Concealment of Writing
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or harm, destroys, removes, conceals, alters, substitutes, or impairs a writing other than a governmental record (including switching price tags).

tiers.when: Writing is a will or codicil, or a deed, mortgage, or other document the law allows to be recorded
Price-tag switch: by the price difference, from less than $100 (Class C) to $300,000 or more (first degree)

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT DESTRUCTION, REMOVAL, OR CONCEALMENT OF WRITING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Simulating Legal Process
offenses.summary: Recklessly causes delivery of a document that simulates a summons, complaint, judgment, or other court process, intending to induce payment or make the person submit or act.
offenses.heading: SIMULATING LEGAL PROCESS

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Refusal to Execute Release of Fraudulent Lien or Claim
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or harm, holds or benefits from a fraudulent lien or claim on property and refuses to release it within 21 days of a written request.

tiers.when: Property owner is a person the actor knows is a public servant

offenses.heading: REFUSAL TO EXECUTE RELEASE OF FRAUDULENT LIEN OR CLAIM

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Deceptive Preparation and Marketing of Academic Product
offenses.summary: For profit, prepares, sells, or advertises an academic product (term paper, thesis, etc.) knowing it will be submitted as someone else's work.
offenses.heading: DECEPTIVE PREPARATION AND MARKETING OF ACADEMIC PRODUCT

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Use or Possession of Identifying Information
offenses.summary: With intent to harm or defraud, obtains, possesses, transfers, or uses identifying information of another person without consent, of a deceased person without legal authorization, or of a child younger than 18 (identity theft).

tiers.when: Committed against an elderly individual (65 or older), or used to help a sex offender evade registration (tiers (c)(1)-(3))

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT USE OR POSSESSION OF IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent, Substandard, or Fictitious Degree
offenses.summary: Uses or claims to hold a fraudulent, substandard, fictitious, or revoked college degree in advertising or to obtain a job, license, promotion, admission, or other benefit.
offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT, SUBSTANDARD, OR FICTITIOUS DEGREE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Exploitation of Child, Elderly Individual, or Disabled Individual
offenses.summary: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly causes the exploitation of a child, elderly individual, or disabled individual (illegal or improper use of their resources for personal gain).
offenses.heading: EXPLOITATION OF CHILD, ELDERLY INDIVIDUAL, OR DISABLED INDIVIDUAL

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent or Fictitious Military Record
offenses.summary: Uses or claims to hold a fraudulent, fictitious, or revoked military record (such as a DD-214 or award) in advertising or to obtain a benefit or preference.
offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT OR FICTITIOUS MILITARY RECORD

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Financial Abuse of Elderly Individual
offenses.summary: Knowingly engages in financial abuse of an elderly individual (65 or older): wrongfully taking, using, or keeping their property, including through a relationship of trust.
offenses.heading: FINANCIAL ABUSE OF ELDERLY INDIVIDUAL

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Use, Possession, or Tampering With Gift Card, Packaging, or Redemption Information
offenses.summary: With intent to harm or defraud: takes or keeps a gift card or its redemption information without consent; alters or tampers with a gift card or its packaging; uses a counterfeit or illegally obtained card or information; or traffics in them.
offenses.notes: One of four different sections numbered 32.56 enacted in 2025 (gift cards, mail keys, fake property documents, AI or phishing fraud).

tiers.when: Fewer than 5 unactivated, counterfeit, or compromised gift cards

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT USE, POSSESSION, OR TAMPERING WITH GIFT CARD, GIFT CARD PACKAGING, OR GIFT CARD DATA OR REDEMPTION INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unlawful Conduct Involving Mail Receptacle Key or Lock
offenses.summary: With intent to harm or defraud or to deprive someone of property, obtains, possesses, duplicates, transfers, or uses a postal key or lock for a mailbox or other mail receptacle.
offenses.notes: One of four different sections numbered 32.56 enacted in 2025.
offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL CONDUCT INVOLVING MAIL RECEPTACLE KEY OR LOCK

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: False, Fraudulent, or Fictitious Document Conveying Real Property Interest
offenses.summary: To enter or stay on real property, knowingly presents a false or fake lease, deed, or other document claiming to give an interest in the property (often used by squatters).
offenses.notes: One of four different sections numbered 32.56 enacted in 2025.
offenses.heading: FALSE, FRAUDULENT, OR FICTITIOUS DOCUMENT CONVEYING REAL PROPERTY INTEREST

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Financial Abuse Using Artificially Generated Media or Phishing
offenses.summary: Knowingly commits financial abuse using AI-generated media sent to another person, or by tricking someone into giving personal, financial, or identifying information through email, text, or other digital means (phishing).
offenses.notes: One of four different sections numbered 32.56 enacted in 2025.
offenses.heading: FINANCIAL ABUSE USING ARTIFICIALLY GENERATED MEDIA OR PHISHING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Fraudulent Sale, Rental, or Lease of Residential Real Property
offenses.summary: Knowingly lists, advertises, sells, rents, or leases residential real property without legal title or authority to do so.
offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT SALE, RENTAL, OR LEASE OF RESIDENTIAL REAL PROPERTY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Real Property Fraud
offenses.summary: Makes a materially false written statement to obtain real property; or with intent to defraud, causes someone to sign a document affecting real property, or causes a public servant to file a fake document about title, a lien, or a claim.

tiers.when: Property or interest worth less than $300,000
Property or interest worth $300,000 or more
Owner was elderly, disabled, or a nonprofit, or the property was a residence homestead

offenses.heading: REAL PROPERTY FRAUD

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Malicious Solicitation of Disaster Victim or for Disaster Response or Recovery
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or harm: solicits donations claiming they will be used for disaster response or recovery; solicits donations for someone else intending to keep them; charges a disaster victim for services after posing as a volunteer offering them free; or charges a disaster victim to search for or return a missing relative.

tiers.when: Same, and the actor faked a disaster-related designation (Government Code ch. 418, subch. L)
Charging a disaster victim to find or return a missing relative (b)(4)

offenses.heading: MALICIOUS SOLICITATION OF DISASTER VICTIM OR FOR DISASTER RESPONSE OR RECOVERY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Breach of Computer Security
offenses.summary: Knowingly accesses a computer, network, or system without the owner's effective consent (a); or does so with intent to defraud, harm, or alter or delete property, including accessing a government or business system against a clear prohibition or contract to get data (b-1).

tiers.when: Same, with two or more prior Chapter 33 convictions, or the system belongs to the government or a critical infrastructure facility
Access with intent to defraud or harm (b-1): aggregate amount less than $100
Same: $150,000 to less than $300,000; any amount under $300,000 if a government or critical infrastructure system; or obtains another's identifying information from one system
Same: $300,000 or more, or obtains identifying information by accessing more than one system

offenses.heading: BREACH OF COMPUTER SECURITY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Online Solicitation of a Minor
offenses.summary: A person 17 or older, with intent to commit a listed sex offense, communicates in a sexually explicit way with, or sends sexually explicit material to, a minor online or by text (b); or knowingly solicits a minor online to meet for sexual contact (c). A "minor" includes someone the actor believes is under 17.

tiers.when: Same, and the minor is (or is believed to be) younger than 14
During school hours, and the actor knew or should have known the minor was enrolled in school

offenses.heading: ONLINE SOLICITATION OF A MINOR

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Electronic Access Interference
offenses.summary: Intentionally interrupts or suspends access to a computer system or network without the owner's effective consent (other than a provider acting for a legitimate business purpose).
offenses.heading: ELECTRONIC ACCESS INTERFERENCE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Electronic Data Tampering
offenses.summary: Through deception and without a legitimate business purpose, intentionally alters data as it moves between computers, or introduces ransomware onto a computer, network, or system.

tiers.when: With intent to defraud or harm: amount less than $100 or cannot be determined
Knowingly restricted a victim's access to privileged information: less than $2,500
Same: $2,500 to less than $30,000, or a client or patient suffered harm
Same: $30,000 to less than $150,000, or a client or patient suffered bodily injury
Same: $150,000 or more, or a client or patient suffered serious bodily injury or death

offenses.heading: ELECTRONIC DATA TAMPERING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unlawful Decryption
offenses.summary: Intentionally decrypts encrypted private information through deception and without a legitimate business purpose.

tiers.when: With intent to defraud or harm: amount less than $100 or cannot be determined
Knowingly decrypted privileged information: less than $2,500
Same: $2,500 to less than $30,000, or a client or patient suffered harm
Same: $30,000 to less than $150,000, or a client or patient suffered bodily injury
Same: $150,000 or more, or a client or patient suffered serious bodily injury or death

offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL DECRYPTION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Tampering with Direct Recording Electronic Voting Machine
offenses.summary: Knowingly accesses part of a voting system that uses direct recording electronic voting machines and thereby prevents a lawful vote, changes a vote, prevents a vote from being counted, or causes an unlawful vote to be counted.
offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH DIRECT RECORDING ELECTRONIC VOTING MACHINE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Online Impersonation
offenses.summary: Without consent and with intent to harm, defraud, intimidate, or threaten, uses another's name or persona to create a web page or post messages on a social networking or other website (a); or sends an email or text using another's identifying information so the recipient believes they sent it, with intent to harm or defraud (b).

tiers.when: Message (b) sent with intent to get a response by emergency personnel

offenses.heading: ONLINE IMPERSONATION

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Unauthorized Use of Telecommunications Service
offenses.summary: An officer, owner, employee, agent, or contractor of a telecommunications provider knowingly and without authority uses or diverts telecommunications service for their own or another's benefit.

tiers.when: Less than $500, with a prior conviction under Chapter 33A
Less than $1,500, with two or more prior Chapter 33A convictions

offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED USE OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Manufacture, Possession, or Delivery of Unlawful Telecommunications Device
offenses.summary: Makes, possesses, delivers, offers, or advertises a counterfeit telecommunications device, or one meant to steal service or hide a call's origin or destination; or distributes plans or instructions to make one.
offenses.heading: MANUFACTURE, POSSESSION, OR DELIVERY OF UNLAWFUL TELECOMMUNICATIONS DEVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Theft of Telecommunications Service
offenses.summary: Knowingly obtains or tries to obtain telecommunications service to avoid paying for it by using an access device without authority, a counterfeit device, or a fraudulent scheme.

tiers.when: Less than $500, with a prior conviction under Chapter 33A
Less than $1,500, with two or more prior Chapter 33A convictions

offenses.heading: THEFT OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Publication of Telecommunications Access Device
offenses.summary: With criminal negligence publishes a telecommunications access device (or counterfeit one) designed to be used to steal telecommunications service.
offenses.heading: PUBLICATION OF TELECOMMUNICATIONS ACCESS DEVICE

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: False Caller Identification Information Display
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or cause harm, makes a call or uses any technology so that another person's phone displays false identity or number information (caller ID "spoofing").
offenses.heading: FALSE CALLER IDENTIFICATION INFORMATION DISPLAY

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Money Laundering
offenses.summary: Knowingly acquires, conceals, possesses, transfers, or transports proceeds of criminal activity; conducts or facilitates a transaction involving them; invests or receives them (or funds believed to be proceeds); or finances criminal activity.
offenses.notes: No penalty is listed for funds under $2,500.

tiers.when: Value of funds $2,500 to less than $30,000

offenses.heading: MONEY LAUNDERING

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Insurance Fraud
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud or deceive an insurer, prepares or presents a statement with false or misleading material information in support of a claim (a) or an application (a-1); or solicits, offers, pays, or receives a benefit in connection with goods or services billed to insurance (b).

tiers.when: Claim (a) or kickback (b): value of claim less than $100
$300,000 or more, or an act in the offense put a person at risk of death or serious bodily injury

offenses.heading: INSURANCE FRAUD

offenses.group: Title 7. Offenses Against Property
offenses.name: Health Care Fraud
offenses.summary: Knowingly makes false statements, conceals information, converts benefits, or commits other listed fraud to obtain unauthorized or excessive payments or benefits under a health care program such as Medicaid.

tiers.when: $2,500 to less than $30,000; offense under (a)(11); or value cannot be determined
$30,000 to less than $150,000, or more than 25 but fewer than 50 fraudulent claims
$150,000 to less than $300,000, or 50 or more fraudulent claims
Actor was a high managerial agent (except the (b)(7) tier)

offenses.heading: HEALTH CARE FRAUD

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Bribery
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly offers, confers, solicits, or accepts any benefit as consideration for a public servant's, party official's, or voter's decision, vote, or exercise of discretion; for a decision in a judicial or administrative proceeding; or for violating a legal duty.
offenses.heading: BRIBERY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Coercion of Public Servant or Voter
offenses.summary: By coercion, influences or tries to influence a public servant in a specific official act or to violate a known legal duty, or influences a voter not to vote or to vote a certain way.

tiers.when: The coercion is a threat to commit a felony

offenses.heading: COERCION OF PUBLIC SERVANT OR VOTER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Improper Influence
offenses.summary: Privately communicates with a public servant who decides an adjudicatory proceeding, intending to influence the outcome on grounds not authorized by law.
offenses.heading: IMPROPER INFLUENCE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Tampering with Witness
offenses.summary: With intent to influence a witness or prospective witness in an official proceeding, offers a benefit to or coerces them to testify falsely, withhold evidence, evade a subpoena, not appear, or drop or delay a prosecution; or a witness solicits or accepts a benefit to do so.

tiers.when: Base offense (proceeding is not a criminal prosecution)

tiers.level: Same category as the most serious offense charged
tiers.when: Proceeding is part of a criminal prosecution
Most serious offense charged is a capital felony

tiers.level: Greater of F3 or the most serious offense charged
Greater of F2 or the most serious offense charged
tiers.when: Family violence proceeding, and the defendant has a prior family-violence conviction

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH WITNESS

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Obstruction or Retaliation
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly harms or threatens to harm another by an unlawful act in retaliation for, or to prevent or delay, their service as a public servant, witness, prospective witness, informant, or crime reporter; or posts or sends a public servant's home address or phone number to cause harm in retaliation.

tiers.when: Victim was harmed or threatened because of service as a juror
Posting or disclosing a public servant's address or phone number (a-1) results in bodily injury to the public servant or a family or household member

offenses.heading: OBSTRUCTION OR RETALIATION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Acceptance of Honorarium
offenses.summary: A public servant solicits or accepts an honorarium for services they would not have been asked to provide but for their official position.
offenses.heading: ACCEPTANCE OF HONORARIUM

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Gift to Public Servant by Person Subject to His Jurisdiction
offenses.summary: A public servant in a regulatory, custodial, litigating, purchasing, or judicial role solicits or accepts a benefit from a person subject to their jurisdiction (regulated, in custody, in litigation, seeking a contract, or with a matter pending); also covers legislators and statewide officials and their staff.
offenses.heading: GIFT TO PUBLIC SERVANT BY PERSON SUBJECT TO HIS JURISDICTION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Offering Gift to Public Servant
offenses.summary: Offers, confers, or agrees to confer a benefit on a public servant that the person knows the public servant is prohibited by law from accepting.
offenses.heading: OFFERING GIFT TO PUBLIC SERVANT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Perjury
offenses.summary: With intent to deceive and knowing what the statement means, makes a false statement under oath (or swears to a false statement) when the statement is required or authorized by law to be under oath, or makes a false unsworn declaration.
offenses.heading: PERJURY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Aggravated Perjury
offenses.summary: Commits perjury, and the false statement is made during or in connection with an official proceeding and is material.
offenses.heading: AGGRAVATED PERJURY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: False Report to Peace Officer, Federal Special Investigator, Law Enforcement Employee, Corrections Officer, or Jailer
offenses.summary: With intent to deceive, knowingly makes a false statement material to a criminal investigation to a peace officer or federal special investigator conducting it, an authorized law enforcement employee, or a corrections officer or jailer.
offenses.heading: FALSE REPORT TO PEACE OFFICER, FEDERAL SPECIAL INVESTIGATOR, LAW ENFORCEMENT EMPLOYEE, CORRECTIONS OFFICER, OR JAILER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: False Report Regarding Missing Child or Missing Person
offenses.summary: With intent to deceive, knowingly files a false report of a missing child or missing person with law enforcement, or makes a false statement to law enforcement about a missing child or person.
aliases: False Report Regarding Missing Child or Missing Peron
offenses.heading: FALSE REPORT REGARDING MISSING CHILD OR MISSING PERSON

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Misrepresenting Child as Family Member at Port of Entry
offenses.summary: With intent to commit human trafficking, knowingly misrepresents a child as the person's family member to a peace officer or federal special investigator at a port of entry.
offenses.heading: MISREPRESENTING CHILD AS FAMILY MEMBER AT PORT OF ENTRY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Tampering with or Fabricating Physical Evidence
offenses.summary: Knowing an investigation or official proceeding is pending or in progress, alters, destroys, or conceals evidence, or makes or uses false evidence to affect it (a); knowing an offense was committed, alters, destroys, or conceals evidence (d)(1); or sees a corpse where a reasonable person would believe an offense occurred and fails to report it to police (d)(2).

tiers.when: The thing altered, destroyed, or concealed is a human corpse

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH OR FABRICATING PHYSICAL EVIDENCE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Tampering with Governmental Record
offenses.summary: Knowingly makes a false entry in or alteration of a governmental record; makes, presents, or uses a fake record as genuine; destroys, conceals, or impairs a governmental record; possesses or sells a record or blank form for unlawful use or knowing it was obtained unlawfully; or presents or uses a record knowing it is false.
offenses.notes: A fake or altered proof-of-insurance card shown to an officer is charged under subsection (d): presenting it is a Class B misdemeanor.

tiers.when: Base offense with intent to defraud or harm another
Public school test or report, TEA (PEIMS) data, or a license, certificate, permit, seal, or title issued by a government
Same, with intent to defraud or harm another
Forensic lab report on physical evidence in a criminal case
Certification or maintenance record of a forensic testing instrument
Search warrant issued by a magistrate
Record used to establish a student's residency for school enrollment
Appraisal filed with an appraisal review board by a person with a contingency interest
Ballot application with knowingly false information
Temporary vehicle tag (Transportation Code ch. 502 or 503)
Proof of motor vehicle liability insurance (insurance card, insurer certificate, or fake insurance document, 37.01(2)(D)): presenting or using it
Same insurance record: making, altering, destroying, possessing, or selling it
Same insurance record, with intent to defraud or harm another

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH GOVERNMENTAL RECORD

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Fraudulent Filing of Financing Statement
offenses.summary: Knowingly presents for filing (or causes to be filed) a financing statement the person knows is forged, contains a material false statement, or is groundless.

tiers.when: Forged, with two or more prior convictions under this section
False or groundless, with intent to defraud or harm another

offenses.heading: FRAUDULENT FILING OF FINANCING STATEMENT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Impersonating Public Servant
offenses.summary: Impersonates a public servant intending to make another submit to the pretended authority or rely on pretended official acts, or knowingly claims to perform the functions of a public servant or public office (including a judge or court) without legal authority.
offenses.heading: IMPERSONATING PUBLIC SERVANT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: False Identification as Peace Officer; Misrepresentation of Property
offenses.summary: Makes, gives another, or possesses a badge, ID card, insignia, emblem, or vehicle with a law enforcement agency's insignia identifying someone as a peace officer or reserve officer, knowing that person is not commissioned as shown; or intentionally or knowingly misrepresents an object or vehicle as law enforcement property.
offenses.heading: FALSE IDENTIFICATION AS PEACE OFFICER; MISREPRESENTATION OF PROPERTY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Record of a Fraudulent Court
offenses.summary: Makes, presents, or uses a document knowing it is not a record of a lawful court, intending that it be given the legal effect of a real court record.

tiers.when: Two or more prior convictions under this section

offenses.heading: RECORD OF A FRAUDULENT COURT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: False Statement Regarding Child Custody Determination Made in Foreign Country
offenses.summary: Knowingly makes (or causes) a false statement about a child custody determination made in a foreign country, during a hearing under the Family Code.
offenses.heading: FALSE STATEMENT REGARDING CHILD CUSTODY DETERMINATION MADE IN FOREIGN COUNTRY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Identify
offenses.summary: Intentionally refuses to give name, residence address, or date of birth to a peace officer who has lawfully arrested the person and asked (a); gives a false name, address, or date of birth to an officer who has lawfully arrested or detained the person, or who has good cause to believe they are a witness (b); or a lawfully detained driver who does not show a license refuses to give name, license number, address, or date of birth (b-1).
offenses.notes: A person who is only detained (not arrested) commits no offense by refusing to identify, unless they are a driver who fails to show a license (b-1, added 2023). Giving false information while detained is an offense.

tiers.when: Refusing after lawful arrest (a), or a detained driver refusing (b-1)
Refusing after arrest (a), while a fugitive from justice
Giving false information (b), while a fugitive from justice
Detained driver (b-1) who also gave a false or fictitious name

offenses.heading: FAILURE TO IDENTIFY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Resisting Arrest, Search, or Transportation
offenses.summary: Intentionally prevents or obstructs a person known to be a peace officer (or someone acting at an officer's direction) from making an arrest, search, or transport of the actor or another, by using force against the officer or another.
offenses.notes: It is no defense that the arrest or search was unlawful (subsection (b)).

tiers.when: Actor uses a deadly weapon to resist the arrest or search

offenses.heading: RESISTING ARREST, SEARCH, OR TRANSPORTATION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Evading Arrest or Detention
offenses.summary: Intentionally flees from a person the actor knows is a peace officer or federal special investigator attempting lawfully to arrest or detain them.
offenses.notes: CONFLICT FOR PROOFREADER: the 2011 Legislature passed two versions of subsection (b). Evading in a vehicle is commonly charged as a third degree felony under the S.B. 1416 version. Confirm with your prosecutor.

tiers.when: Uses a vehicle while in flight (S.B. 1416 version; the other version makes this a state jail felony with no prior, third degree with a prior; watercraft is included there)
Another person suffers serious bodily injury from the officer's attempt to apprehend
Actor uses a tire deflation device against the officer (S.B. 1416 version, (b)(2)(C))
Another person dies as a direct result of the officer's attempt to apprehend
Another person suffers serious bodily injury from the actor's use of a tire deflation device

offenses.heading: EVADING ARREST OR DETENTION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Hindering Apprehension or Prosecution
offenses.summary: With intent to hinder the arrest, prosecution, conviction, or punishment of another (or the arrest of someone with a warrant or capias, or a juvenile's detention or adjudication), harbors or conceals them, helps them avoid arrest or escape, or warns them of impending discovery or apprehension.

tiers.when: Actor knew the person was under arrest for, charged with, or convicted of a felony (including failure to register as a sex offender), or a juvenile alleged or adjudicated for felony-level conduct

offenses.heading: HINDERING APPREHENSION OR PROSECUTION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Escape
offenses.summary: Escapes from custody while under arrest, lawfully detained, charged, or convicted; in custody under a court order; in a secure juvenile detention facility; or in a juvenile probation officer's custody for violating a court order.

tiers.when: Actor is under arrest for, charged with, or convicted of a felony
Actor is confined in a secure correctional facility or law enforcement facility
Actor is committed to a secure Texas Juvenile Justice Department facility (not a halfway house)
Actor causes bodily injury to effect the escape
Actor causes serious bodily injury, or uses or threatens a deadly weapon, to effect the escape

offenses.heading: ESCAPE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Permitting or Facilitating Escape
offenses.summary: A correctional facility official or employee knowingly permits or facilitates an escape; or anyone knowingly causes or facilitates the escape of a person held for delinquency or involuntary mental-health or chemical-dependency commitment.

tiers.when: Person in custody was under arrest for, charged with, or convicted of a felony, or confined after a felony conviction in a non-secure facility
A deadly weapon was used or threatened, or the person was confined in a secure correctional facility after a felony conviction

offenses.heading: PERMITTING OR FACILITATING ESCAPE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Effect of Unlawful Custody
offenses.summary: Not an offense. It is no defense to escape or permitting escape that the custody was unlawful.
offenses.heading: EFFECT OF UNLAWFUL CUSTODY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Implements for Escape
offenses.summary: With intent to facilitate escape, brings into a correctional facility, or gives a person in custody or an inmate, a deadly weapon or anything useful for escape.

tiers.when: The item was a deadly weapon

offenses.heading: IMPLEMENTS FOR ESCAPE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Bail Jumping and Failure to Appear
offenses.summary: A person lawfully released from custody, with or without bail, on condition of later appearing, intentionally or knowingly fails to appear as required.

tiers.when: Underlying offense is punishable by fine only

offenses.heading: BAIL JUMPING AND FAILURE TO APPEAR

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Prohibited Substances and Items in Correctional or Civil Commitment Facility
offenses.summary: Provides (or possesses intending to provide) alcohol, drugs, a deadly weapon, a cell phone, money, or tobacco (where prohibited) to a person in a correctional or civil commitment facility; takes alcohol or drugs into or onto facility property; possesses them or a weapon in a facility; an inmate possesses a cell phone; or acquires or pays for a phone for an inmate.

tiers.when: Providing or taking alcohol or drugs into a correctional facility (a)(1), (b), (c), by an employee of the facility
Same, by an employee, and the drug causes the death of a person in custody
tiers.extra: 15 to 99 years or life; fine up to $250,000

offenses.heading: PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES AND ITEMS IN CORRECTIONAL OR CIVIL COMMITMENT FACILITY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Improper Contact with Victim
offenses.summary: While confined after being charged with or convicted of stalking or a sex offense requiring registration, contacts the victim or their family (directly or through someone else) without written, dated consent received by the facility director.

tiers.when: Actor is confined after a felony conviction for one of those offenses

offenses.heading: IMPROPER CONTACT WITH VICTIM

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Tampering with Electronic Monitoring Device
offenses.summary: A person required to wear a GPS or electronic monitor (bail, probation, parole, or monitoring program) knowingly removes or disables it, or helps another do so.

tiers.when: Person is in the parole super-intensive supervision program

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH ELECTRONIC MONITORING DEVICE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Unauthorized Absence from Community Corrections Facility, County Correctional Center, or Assignment Site
offenses.summary: A person required to serve time or treatment in a community corrections facility or county correctional center fails to report or leaves the facility or a community service site without approval.
offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ABSENCE FROM COMMUNITY CORRECTIONS FACILITY, COUNTY CORRECTIONAL CENTER, OR ASSIGNMENT SITE

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Contraband in Correctional Facility
offenses.summary: Provides contraband (as defined by the facility) to an inmate, brings it into a correctional facility, or possesses it while confined.

tiers.when: Committed by an employee or volunteer of the facility

offenses.heading: CONTRABAND IN CORRECTIONAL FACILITY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Operation of Unmanned Aircraft Over Correctional Facility or Detention Facility
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly flies a drone over a correctional or detention facility at 400 feet or lower, lets it touch the facility or anyone on it, or flies close enough to interfere with or disturb the facility.

tiers.when: Drone used to deliver or introduce contraband

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT OVER CORRECTIONAL FACILITY OR DETENTION FACILITY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Barratry and Solicitation of Professional Employment
offenses.summary: With intent to obtain an economic benefit, files an unauthorized suit or claim, or solicits clients (in person, by phone, or by social media or electronic message) or pays others to solicit clients ("barratry," ambulance chasing); finances or knowingly accepts work from such solicitation; or a licensed professional sends prohibited written solicitations (such as within 30 days of an accident).

tiers.when: Prohibited written solicitation by a licensed professional (d)
Same (d), with a prior conviction under (d)

offenses.heading: BARRATRY AND SOLICITATION OF PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYMENT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Falsely Holding Oneself Out as a Lawyer
offenses.summary: With intent to obtain an economic benefit, holds oneself out as a lawyer without being licensed and in good standing.
offenses.heading: FALSELY HOLDING ONESELF OUT AS A LAWYER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Unauthorized Practice of Law
offenses.summary: Without being a lawyer and for economic benefit, contracts to represent, or advises, someone on personal injury or property damage claims or settlements, or makes listed contingent-fee or counsel-selection contracts.
offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED PRACTICE OF LAW

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Hindering Proceedings by Disorderly Conduct
offenses.summary: Intentionally hinders an official proceeding by noise or violent or tumultuous behavior, or recklessly does so and continues after an official request to stop.
offenses.heading: HINDERING PROCEEDINGS BY DISORDERLY CONDUCT

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Taking or Attempting to Take Weapon from Peace Officer, Federal Special Investigator, Employee or Official of Correctional Facility, Parole Officer, Community Supervision and Corrections Department Officer, or Commissioned Security Officer
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly, and with force, takes or tries to take a firearm, nightstick, stun gun, or chemical spray from a peace officer, federal investigator, correctional employee, parole or probation officer, or commissioned security officer.
offenses.heading: TAKING OR ATTEMPTING TO TAKE WEAPON FROM PEACE OFFICER, FEDERAL SPECIAL INVESTIGATOR, EMPLOYEE OR OFFICIAL OF CORRECTIONAL FACILITY, PAROLE OFFICER, COMMUNITY SUPERVISION AND CORRECTIONS DEPARTMENT OFFICER, OR COMMISSIONED SECURITY OFFICER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Interference with Public Duties
offenses.summary: With criminal negligence interrupts, disrupts, impedes, or interferes with a peace officer performing a duty, EMS personnel, a firefighter at a fire, a law enforcement animal, emergency CB radio traffic, an animal control officer, public health or safety officials at a site, and others listed.
offenses.notes: It is a defense that the interruption was speech only (subsection (d)).
offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH PUBLIC DUTIES

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Interference with Police Service Animals
offenses.summary: Recklessly taunts, torments, or strikes a police service animal; throws something at it; interferes with it or its handler; releases it; enters its area; or injures, kills, or tries to injure or kill it.

tiers.when: Throwing an object or substance at it (b)(2)
Interfering with or obstructing the animal or handler, releasing it, or entering its area (b)(3)-(5)
Injuring it, or conduct likely to injure it (b)(6)-(7)
Killing it or conduct likely to kill it, or injury that permanently affects its ability to serve

offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH POLICE SERVICE ANIMALS

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Interference with Radio Frequency Licensed to Government Entity
offenses.summary: Without consent, intentionally interrupts, jams, or interferes with an FCC-licensed government radio frequency used by law enforcement, fire, or EMS.

tiers.when: Intent to facilitate another offense or to interfere with an emergency response

offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH RADIO FREQUENCY LICENSED TO GOVERNMENT ENTITY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Preventing Execution of Civil Process
