offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly, by words or physical action, prevents the execution of civil process.
offenses.heading: PREVENTING EXECUTION OF CIVIL PROCESS

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Stop or Report Sexual or Assaultive Offense Against Child
offenses.summary: Observes what a reasonable person would believe is a sexual or assaultive offense being committed (or about to be) against a child, and fails to assist the child or immediately report it to police, when the person could do so without risking serious bodily injury or death.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed this as a Class A misdemeanor limited to aggravated sexual assault. Current law (amended 2025) covers any sexual or assaultive offense against a child and is a third degree felony.
aliases: Failure to Stop or Report Aggravated Sexual Assault of Child
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO STOP OR REPORT SEXUAL OR ASSAULTIVE OFFENSE AGAINST CHILD

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Report Felony
offenses.summary: Observes a felony where a reasonable person would believe serious bodily injury or death may have resulted, and fails to immediately report it to police when it seems unreported and reporting would not endanger the person.
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT FELONY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Report Assault, Neglect, or Omission of Care in Certain Group Homes
offenses.summary: Has actual knowledge that a group home resident suffered bodily injury from assault, neglect, or an omission of care, and fails to report it to law enforcement or DFPS.
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT ASSAULT, NEGLECT, OR OMISSION OF CARE IN CERTAIN GROUP HOMES

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Use of Collision Report Information and Other Information for Pecuniary Gain
offenses.summary: Obtains collision report or similar information from DPS or another government entity and uses it (or has an agent or client use it) to directly solicit business for profit; or hires someone to obtain it for that use.
aliases: Use of Accident Report Information and Other Information for Pecuniary Gain
offenses.heading: USE OF COLLISION REPORT INFORMATION AND OTHER INFORMATION FOR PECUNIARY GAIN

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Provide Notice and Report of Death of Resident of Institution
offenses.summary: A superintendent or general manager of an institution fails, as required by the Code of Criminal Procedure, to give notice of a resident's death, submit a death report, or include known material facts in the report.
offenses.notes: A new version of subsection (a), citing CCP Article 49A.151-.152, takes effect April 1, 2027.
aliases: Failure to Provide Notice and Report of Death Resident of Institution
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO PROVIDE NOTICE AND REPORT OF DEATH OF RESIDENT OF INSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Concurrent Jurisdiction to Prosecute Offenses under This Chapter
offenses.summary: Not an offense. With the local prosecutor's consent, the Attorney General may also prosecute offenses under Chapter 39.
offenses.heading: CONCURRENT JURISDICTION TO PROSECUTE OFFENSES UNDER THIS CHAPTER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Abuse of Official Capacity
offenses.summary: A public servant, with intent to obtain a benefit or to harm or defraud another, intentionally or knowingly violates a law relating to their office or employment (a)(1), or misuses government property, services, personnel, or anything of value in their custody because of their position (a)(2).

tiers.when: Violating a law relating to the office (a)(1)
Misusing government property (a)(2): value of the use less than $100

offenses.heading: ABUSE OF OFFICIAL CAPACITY

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Official Oppression
offenses.summary: A public servant acting under color of office or employment intentionally subjects another to mistreatment, or to an arrest, detention, search, seizure, dispossession, assessment, or lien they know is unlawful; intentionally denies or impedes another's rights knowing it is unlawful; or intentionally subjects another to sexual harassment.

tiers.when: Intent to impair the accuracy of data reported to the Texas Education Agency (PEIMS)

offenses.heading: OFFICIAL OPPRESSION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Violations of the Civil Rights of Person in Custody; Improper Sexual Activity with Person in Custody or under Supervision
offenses.summary: A correctional or juvenile facility official, employee, contractor, or volunteer, or a peace officer, intentionally denies or impedes a person in custody in exercising a right knowing it is unlawful (a)(1), or engages in sexual contact or intercourse with a person in custody (a)(2). Subsection (f) covers sexual activity by probation, parole, and juvenile staff with a person under their agency's supervision.
offenses.notes: Two different 2021 versions of subsection (b) are in effect (H.B. 3157 and S.B. 312). Both are shown. Note that peace officers are covered for persons in custody.

tiers.when: Denying or impeding rights (a)(1) (S.B. 312 version; the other 2021 version makes this a Class A misdemeanor)
Sexual activity with a person in custody (a)(2)
Sexual activity with a person in Texas Juvenile Justice Department custody or a juvenile facility (S.B. 312 version)
Sexual activity with a juvenile offender in a correctional facility (S.B. 312 version)
Sexual activity with a person under supervision but not in custody (f)

offenses.heading: VIOLATIONS OF THE CIVIL RIGHTS OF PERSON IN CUSTODY; IMPROPER SEXUAL ACTIVITY WITH PERSON IN CUSTODY OR UNDER SUPERVISION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Improper Sexual Activity with Committed Person
offenses.summary: An officer, employee, contractor, or volunteer of the Texas Civil Commitment Office or a civil commitment facility intentionally engages in sexual contact or intercourse with a person committed to the facility.
offenses.heading: IMPROPER SEXUAL ACTIVITY WITH COMMITTED PERSON

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Report Death of Prisoner
offenses.summary: A person required by the Code of Criminal Procedure to investigate and report a death in custody fails to investigate, file the report, or include known facts; or a person required by Government Code 501.055 fails to give notice of, investigate, or report an inmate's death.
offenses.notes: A new version of subsection (a), citing CCP Article 49A.153, takes effect April 1, 2027.
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO REPORT DEATH OF PRISONER

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Misuse of Official Information
offenses.summary: A public servant uses non-public information from their position to acquire a financial interest or speculate, or coerces someone into not reporting it to law enforcement (a); a public servant discloses or uses non-public information for a nongovernmental purpose to benefit or to harm (b); or a person solicits or receives such information from a public servant to benefit or harm (c).
offenses.heading: MISUSE OF OFFICIAL INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 8. Offenses Against Public Administration
offenses.name: Failure to Comply with Immigration Detainer Request
offenses.summary: A sheriff, police chief, constable, or other person with primary authority over a jail, having custody of a person subject to an ICE immigration detainer request, knowingly fails to comply with it.
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH IMMIGRATION DETAINER REQUEST

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Disorderly Conduct
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly, in a public place (including a school campus): uses abusive or vulgar language or makes an offensive gesture that tends to incite an immediate breach of the peace; creates a noxious odor; abuses or threatens someone in an obviously offensive way; makes unreasonable noise (also near a private residence); fights; discharges a firearm (other than on a public road or shooting range); displays a firearm or deadly weapon in a manner calculated to alarm; discharges a firearm on or across a public road; exposes the anus or genitals recklessly; or for a lewd or unlawful purpose looks into a dwelling, hotel room, restroom, or dressing room ("peeping").
offenses.notes: For noise, speech, or picketing, the actor must first be ordered to move or disperse before arrest (42.04). Significant provocation is a defense to abusive or threatening conduct under (a)(4).

tiers.when: Discharging a firearm in a public place (a)(7), or displaying a firearm or deadly weapon in a manner calculated to alarm (a)(8)

offenses.heading: DISORDERLY CONDUCT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Riot
offenses.summary: Knowingly participates in a riot: an assembly of seven or more persons resulting in conduct that creates immediate danger of property damage or injury, substantially obstructs law enforcement or government, or by force deprives a person of a legal right.

tiers.level: Same as the highest-grade offense committed by any rioter
tiers.when: A higher-grade offense was committed by anyone in the riot in furtherance of its purpose or should have been anticipated

offenses.heading: RIOT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Obstructing Highway or Other Passageway
offenses.summary: Without legal privilege, intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly obstructs a highway, street, sidewalk, entrance, exit, or other passageway the public uses, or disobeys a reasonable order to move from a peace officer, firefighter, or person in control of the premises given to prevent obstruction or keep people away from a fire, riot, or other hazard.

tiers.when: Knowingly blocks an emergency vehicle running lights or siren, or obstructs access to a hospital or emergency care facility
Driving while engaging in a reckless driving exhibition (street takeover)
Reckless driving exhibition, with a prior conviction under (d), while intoxicated, or causing bodily injury

offenses.heading: OBSTRUCTING HIGHWAY OR OTHER PASSAGEWAY

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Defense When Conduct Consists of Speech or Other Expression
offenses.summary: Not an offense. If conduct under 42.01(a)(5) (unreasonable noise), 42.03 (obstructing a passageway), or 42.055 (funeral disruption) consists of speech, gathering to hear speech, or peaceful picketing, the person must be ordered to move, disperse, or fix the violation before arrest, unless they have already intentionally harmed the interests those laws protect.
offenses.heading: DEFENSE WHEN CONDUCT CONSISTS OF SPEECH OR OTHER EXPRESSION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Disrupting Meeting or Procession
offenses.summary: With intent to prevent or disrupt a lawful meeting, procession, or gathering (in person or virtual), obstructs or interferes with it by physical action, verbal utterance, or electronic disturbance (including hacking).
offenses.heading: DISRUPTING MEETING OR PROCESSION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Funeral Service Disruptions
offenses.summary: Pickets within 1,000 feet of a facility or cemetery being used for a funeral service, during the period from three hours before until three hours after the service.
offenses.heading: FUNERAL SERVICE DISRUPTIONS

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: False Alarm or Report
offenses.summary: Knowingly initiates or circulates a false or baseless report of a bombing, fire, offense, or other emergency that would ordinarily cause an emergency response, put someone in fear of serious bodily injury, or disrupt a building, public place, or vehicle.

tiers.when: False report involving a school or college, public communications, transportation, water, gas, power, or other public service

offenses.heading: FALSE ALARM OR REPORT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: False Report to Induce Emergency Response
offenses.summary: Knowingly makes (or causes) a false report of a crime or emergency to police, 9-1-1, or emergency agencies that causes an emergency response, while reckless about whether the response may injure someone ("swatting").

tiers.when: Two or more prior convictions under this section
False report of a crime, and someone suffered serious bodily injury or death from lawful conduct in the response

offenses.heading: FALSE REPORT TO INDUCE EMERGENCY RESPONSE

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Silent or Abusive Calls to 9-1-1 Service
offenses.summary: Calls or texts 9-1-1 when there is no emergency and knowingly or intentionally remains silent or makes abusive or harassing statements to the dispatcher; or knowingly lets another use the person's phone that way.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed this as a Class A misdemeanor. It is a Class B misdemeanor.
aliases: Silent or Abuse Calls to 9-1-1 Service
offenses.heading: SILENT OR ABUSIVE CALLS TO 9-1-1 SERVICE

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Interference with Emergency Request for Assistance
offenses.summary: Knowingly prevents or interferes with another's ability to call 9-1-1 or request emergency help, or recklessly renders a phone or device unusable that another would use to call for help.
offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH EMERGENCY REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Harassment
offenses.summary: With intent to harass, annoy, alarm, abuse, torment, or embarrass: initiates an obscene communication; threatens bodily injury or a felony against the person, family, household, or property; falsely reports a death or serious injury; makes repeated or anonymous calls, or fails to hang up; lets one's phone be used for harassment; sends repeated electronic messages; repeatedly posts online to cause emotional distress (except matters of public concern); tracks or follows the person or their vehicle without consent; or harasses from a temporary or disposable phone number.

tiers.when: Electronic harassment of a child under 18 intended to cause suicide or serious self-injury ("cyberbullying"), or after violating a cyberbullying TRO or injunction
Against a utility employee or agent performing a duty
Against a person the actor knows is a court employee
Against a court employee, with a prior conviction under this section
Against a person the actor knows is a judge
Against a judge, with a prior conviction under this section

offenses.heading: HARASSMENT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Stalking
offenses.summary: On more than one occasion, under one course of conduct directed at a specific person, knowingly engages in conduct (including harassment under 42.07) that the actor knows or should know the person will regard as threatening bodily injury, death, or an offense against them, their family or household, dating partner, or property; that causes them to be afraid or to feel harassed, terrified, intimidated, or alarmed; and that would cause a reasonable person similar fear or distress.

tiers.when: Prior stalking conviction (Texas, another state, tribal, territorial, or federal)

offenses.heading: STALKING

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Unlawful Disclosure of Residence Address or Telephone Number
offenses.summary: Posts on a public website or sends electronically the home address or phone number of a person, intending to cause harm or a threat of harm to them or their family or household ("doxxing").

tiers.when: Results in bodily injury to the person or a family or household member

offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL DISCLOSURE OF RESIDENCE ADDRESS OR TELEPHONE NUMBER

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Disclosure of Confidential Information Regarding Family Violence or Victims of Trafficking Shelter Center
offenses.summary: With intent to threaten the safety of any resident, discloses or publicizes the location or physical layout of a family violence shelter or victims-of-trafficking shelter.
offenses.heading: DISCLOSURE OF CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION REGARDING FAMILY VIOLENCE OR VICTIMS OF TRAFFICKING SHELTER CENTER

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Abuse of Corpse
offenses.summary: Without legal authority, knowingly disinters, disturbs, damages, or offensively treats a human corpse; conceals an illegally disinterred corpse; buys, sells, or traffics in a corpse; sends a corpse out of state; or vandalizes or offensively treats a grave or resting place.

tiers.when: Vandalizing or offensively treating a grave or resting place (a)(5)

offenses.heading: ABUSE OF CORPSE

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Cruelty to Livestock Animals
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly tortures a livestock animal; unreasonably fails to provide food, water, or care, or abandons it; transports or confines it cruelly; poisons another's livestock (other than cattle, horses, sheep, swine, or goats); causes it to fight; uses it as a live lure; trips a horse; or seriously overworks it.

tiers.when: Neglect, abandonment, cruel transport or confinement, or overwork ((a)(2)-(4), (9))
Same, with two prior convictions under 42.09 or 42.092 (in any combination)
Torture, poisoning, fighting, live lure, or horse tripping ((a)(1), (5)-(8))
Same, with two prior convictions under 42.09 or 42.092 (in any combination)

offenses.heading: CRUELTY TO LIVESTOCK ANIMALS

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Attack on Assistance Animal
offenses.summary: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly attacks, injures, or kills an assistance animal (such as a guide dog), or incites or permits the person's own animal to do so.
offenses.heading: ATTACK ON ASSISTANCE ANIMAL

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Cruelty to Nonlivestock Animals
offenses.summary: Intentionally, knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence: tortures, cruelly kills, or seriously injures an animal; without the owner's consent kills, poisons, or seriously or otherwise injures an animal; unreasonably fails to provide food, water, care, or shelter, or abandons it; transports or confines it cruelly; causes animals to fight (if either is not a dog); uses it as a live lure; or seriously overworks it.

tiers.when: Neglect, abandonment, cruel transport or confinement, bodily injury without consent, or overwork ((b)(3)-(6), (9))
Same, with two prior convictions under 42.09 or 42.092 (in any combination)
Torture, cruel killing, serious injury, or killing or poisoning without consent ((b)(1)-(2))
Same, with a prior conviction under (b)(1), (2), (7), or (8) or under 42.09
Animal fighting (not dog-on-dog) or live lure ((b)(7)-(8))
Same, with a prior conviction under this section or 42.09

offenses.heading: CRUELTY TO NONLIVESTOCK ANIMALS

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Dog Fighting
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly causes a dog to fight another dog; profits from or operates a dog-fighting facility; lets property be used for dog fighting; owns dog-fighting equipment or trains a dog for fighting; or attends a dog fight as a spectator.

tiers.when: Causing a fight, profiting or operating, or allowing property to be used ((a)(1)-(3))
Owning equipment, training a dog to fight, or attending as a spectator ((a)(4)-(6))

offenses.heading: DOG FIGHTING

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Cockfighting
offenses.summary: Knowingly causes a cockfight, profits from one, lets property be used for one, trains a cock to fight, deals in gaffs or slashers for cockfighting, or attends a cockfight as a spectator.

tiers.when: Causing a fight or sharing in the earnings ((b)(1)-(2))
Allowing property use, training, or dealing in implements ((b)(3)-(5))
Attending as a spectator, with a prior conviction for attending

offenses.heading: COCKFIGHTING

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Possession of Animal by Person Convicted of Animal Cruelty
offenses.summary: Possesses or controls an animal within five years after being convicted of animal cruelty (42.091, 42.092, or 42.10, or a similar out-of-state or federal offense).
offenses.heading: POSSESSION OF ANIMAL BY PERSON CONVICTED OF ANIMAL CRUELTY

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Destruction of Flag
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly damages, defaces, mutilates, or burns the flag of the United States or of Texas.
offenses.notes: Flag-burning laws like this one were held unconstitutional as applied to protest in Texas v. Johnson (1989) and are generally not enforceable.
offenses.heading: DESTRUCTION OF FLAG

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Discharge of Firearm in Certain Municipalities
offenses.summary: Recklessly discharges a firearm inside the city limits of a municipality with a population of 100,000 or more.
aliases: Discharge or Firearm in Certain Municipalities
offenses.heading: DISCHARGE OF FIREARM IN CERTAIN MUNICIPALITIES

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Use of Laser Pointers
offenses.summary: Knowingly points a laser pointer at a uniformed safety officer (peace officer, security guard, firefighter, EMS worker, or other uniformed officer).

tiers.when: Causes bodily injury to the officer
Causes serious bodily injury to the officer

offenses.heading: USE OF LASER POINTERS

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Illumination of Aircraft by Intense Light
offenses.summary: Intentionally points a laser or other light at an aircraft, with intensity sufficient to impair the operator's ability to control it.

tiers.when: The light actually impairs the operator's ability to control the aircraft

offenses.heading: ILLUMINATION OF AIRCRAFT BY INTENSE LIGHT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.chapter: Ch. 42 Disorderly Conduct and Related Offenses
offenses.name: Operation of Unmanned Aircraft Over Airport, Military Installation, or Spaceport
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly flies a drone over an airport, military installation, or spaceport; lets it touch the property or anyone on it; or flies it so it interferes with or disturbs operations.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT OVER AIRPORT, MILITARY INSTALLATION, OR SPACEPORT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Prostitution
offenses.summary: Knowingly offers or agrees to receive a fee from another to engage in sexual conduct.

tiers.when: One or two prior convictions for prostitution
Three or more prior convictions for prostitution

offenses.heading: PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Solicitation of Prostitution
offenses.summary: Knowingly offers or agrees to pay a fee to another person to engage in sexual conduct with that person or another (the buyer's offense).
offenses.notes: Buying sex has been a felony in Texas since 2021.

tiers.when: Prior conviction for solicitation of prostitution (or under former 43.02(b))
The other person is younger than 18, was represented as under 18, or was believed to be under 18
Committed on or within 1,000 feet of a school, or where a school function or UIL event was taking place

offenses.heading: SOLICITATION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Promotion of Prostitution
offenses.summary: Other than as the prostitute, knowingly receives money or property under an agreement to share the proceeds of prostitution, or solicits another to engage in sexual conduct with someone for pay (pimping).

tiers.when: Involves a person younger than 18 (age need not be known)

offenses.heading: PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Online Promotion of Prostitution
offenses.summary: Owns, manages, or operates an interactive computer service or content provider (website or app) with intent to promote or facilitate another person's prostitution.

tiers.when: Prior conviction under this section or 43.041
Involves a person younger than 18 engaging in prostitution

offenses.heading: ONLINE PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Continuous Promotion of Prostitution
offenses.summary: During a period of 30 or more days, engages two or more times in conduct that is promotion of prostitution (43.03).
offenses.heading: CONTINUOUS PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Aggravated Promotion of Prostitution
offenses.summary: Knowingly owns, invests in, finances, controls, supervises, or manages a prostitution enterprise that uses two or more prostitutes.
offenses.heading: AGGRAVATED PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Aggravated Online Promotion of Prostitution
offenses.summary: Owns, manages, or operates an interactive computer service or content provider with intent to promote or facilitate the prostitution of five or more persons.

tiers.when: Involves two or more persons younger than 18

offenses.heading: AGGRAVATED ONLINE PROMOTION OF PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Compelling Prostitution
offenses.summary: Knowingly causes another by force, threat, coercion, or fraud to commit prostitution, or causes by any means a child younger than 18 or a disabled individual to commit prostitution (knowledge of age or disability not required).
offenses.heading: COMPELLING PROSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Accomplice Witness; Testimony and Immunity
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A party to a prostitution offense may be required to give evidence or testify about it, and may be granted immunity for doing so.
offenses.heading: ACCOMPLICE WITNESS; TESTIMONY AND IMMUNITY

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Obscene Display or Distribution
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly displays or distributes an obscene photo, drawing, or other obscene material, reckless about whether someone present will be offended or alarmed.
offenses.heading: OBSCENE DISPLAY OR DISTRIBUTION

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Obscenity
offenses.summary: Knowing its content, wholesale promotes (or possesses to wholesale promote) obscene material or devices (a); or promotes or possesses to promote obscene material or devices, or produces or takes part in an obscene performance (c).

tiers.when: Material depicts sexual conduct by a child under 18, an image virtually indistinguishable from one, or an image altered to depict an identifiable child

offenses.heading: OBSCENITY

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Promotion or Possession of Child-Like Sex Doll
offenses.summary: Knowingly promotes, possesses with intent to promote, or possesses a child-like sex doll.
offenses.heading: PROMOTION OR POSSESSION OF CHILD-LIKE SEX DOLL

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Possession, Promotion, or Production of Certain Visual Material Appearing to Depict Child
offenses.summary: Knowingly possesses, accesses to view, or promotes obscene material that appears to depict a child under 18 in sexual conduct, whether a real child, cartoon, or AI-generated image; or uses an image of a real child to train an AI model to produce child pornography.

tiers.when: One prior conviction under this section or 43.23, 43.26, 43.261, or 43.262
Two or more such prior convictions

offenses.heading: POSSESSION, PROMOTION, OR PRODUCTION OF CERTAIN VISUAL MATERIAL APPEARING TO DEPICT CHILD

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Sale, Distribution, or Display of Harmful Material to Minor
offenses.summary: Knowing material is harmful to minors: sells, distributes, or exhibits it to a known minor; displays it recklessly where a minor may be present and offended; or uses a minor to do either.

tiers.when: Hiring or using a minor to do so (b)(3)

offenses.heading: SALE, DISTRIBUTION, OR DISPLAY OF HARMFUL MATERIAL TO MINOR

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Sexual Performance by a Child
offenses.summary: Knowingly employs, authorizes, or induces a child younger than 18 to engage in sexual conduct or a sexual performance, or a parent or guardian consents to it (b); or knowingly produces, directs, or promotes a performance that includes sexual conduct by a child (d).
offenses.heading: SEXUAL PERFORMANCE BY A CHILD

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Employment Harmful to Children
offenses.summary: Employs, authorizes, or induces a child to work in a sexually oriented commercial activity, or in a business that permits or requires a child to work nude or topless.

tiers.when: Child younger than 14 (age need not be known)

offenses.heading: EMPLOYMENT HARMFUL TO CHILDREN

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Possession or Promotion of Child Pornography
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly possesses or accesses to view material depicting a child under 18 in sexual conduct (a-1), or a computer-generated child (a-2); or promotes or possesses with intent to promote such material (e), (e-1).
offenses.notes: CONFLICT FOR PROOFREADER: this section was rewritten in 2025 (S.B. 1621) and other bills amended older subsections. Subsection (d) still refers to old Subsection (a); (c-4) is marked repealed; and there are two versions of (g). Confirm the current penalties with your prosecutor.

tiers.when: Possessing or viewing real-child material (a-1), base offense
Same, with one prior conviction under Chapter 43 or a sex-offender-registration offense, or 10 to fewer than 50 images
Same, with two or more such priors, 50 or more images, or depicts sexual assault of a child
Same, by a child-care, residential treatment, or youth shelter employee or a state-funded caregiver, or displayed in a school library
Depicts a child younger than 10 (second and third degree tiers), or minimum 15 years for the (c-1)(2) tier
Possessing or viewing computer-generated child material (a-2), base offense
Same, with one prior, or 10 to fewer than 50 images
Same, with two or more priors, or 50 or more images
Same, by a listed child-care employee or displayed in a school library
Promoting real-child material (e), base offense (one 2025 version; the other makes it first degree)
Promoting, with a prior conviction, 10 to fewer than 50 images, or any image of a child who appears under 10
Promoting 50 or more images, or images of sexual assault of a child
Promoting computer-generated child material (e-1), base offense
Same, with a prior, 10 or more images, or a child who appears under 10

offenses.heading: POSSESSION OR PROMOTION OF CHILD PORNOGRAPHY

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Electronic Transmission of Certain Visual Material Depicting Minor
offenses.summary: A minor intentionally or knowingly sends another minor sexually explicit images of a minor (including themselves) that a minor produced, or possesses such images of another minor ("sexting" between minors).
offenses.notes: A minor may be eligible for a defense or an education program; see subsections (e)-(f) and CCP Art. 45.0215.

tiers.when: Sending to harass, annoy, alarm, abuse, or embarrass; or one prior conviction under this section
Sending, with a prior harassment-type conviction or two or more prior convictions under this section
Possessing, with one prior conviction under this section
Possessing, with two or more prior convictions

offenses.heading: ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION OF CERTAIN VISUAL MATERIAL DEPICTING MINOR

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Possession or Promotion of Lewd Visual Material Depicting Child
offenses.summary: Knowingly possesses, accesses to view, or promotes material depicting the lewd exhibition of the genitals or pubic area of a child younger than 18 (clothed or not), that appeals to the prurient interest and lacks serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.

tiers.when: One prior conviction under this section or 43.26
Two or more such prior convictions

offenses.heading: POSSESSION OR PROMOTION OF LEWD VISUAL MATERIAL DEPICTING CHILD

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Duty to Report
offenses.summary: Not a separate offense. A business that develops or processes visual material and finds that it may be evidence of a Chapter 43 offense must report it to local law enforcement.
offenses.heading: DUTY TO REPORT

offenses.group: Title 9. Offenses Against Public Order and Decency
offenses.name: Certain Sexually Oriented Performances Prohibited
offenses.summary: Engages in a sexually oriented performance (paid or not) on public property where a child could reasonably be expected to see it, or in the presence of a person younger than 18.
offenses.notes: This 2023 law (S.B. 12) has been challenged in federal court. Check its current enforcement status with your prosecutor.
offenses.heading: CERTAIN SEXUALLY ORIENTED PERFORMANCES PROHIBITED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Unlawful Carrying Weapons
offenses.summary: Carries a handgun when under 21, or within five years of an assault, deadly conduct, terroristic threat, or disorderly-conduct-firearm conviction, while not on own premises or in or en route to own vehicle (a); carries a handgun in own vehicle in plain view (unless 21+ or licensed and holstered) or while engaged in criminal activity or prohibited from possessing a firearm (a-1); a minor under 18 carries a location-restricted knife off premises without a parent (a-4); intentionally displays a handgun in plain view in a public place (unless holstered) (a-5); carries a handgun while intoxicated off own property or vehicle (a-6); or carries a handgun while prohibited from possessing a firearm under 46.04 (a-7).
offenses.notes: Since 2021 (H.B. 1927), a person 21 or older who is not prohibited from possessing a firearm may carry a handgun without a license, if it is concealed or holstered.

tiers.when: Location-restricted knife by a person under 18 (a-4)
Carrying while prohibited (a-7) because of a felony conviction (46.04(a))
Carrying while prohibited (a-7) because of a family-violence assault conviction or protective order (46.04(b), (c))
Committed within 300 feet of a school, or at a school function or UIL event, and the actor knew it

offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL CARRYING WEAPONS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Places Weapons Prohibited
offenses.summary: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly possesses or goes with a firearm, location-restricted knife, club, or prohibited weapon: at a school or college (or its sponsored activity or vehicle); a polling place during voting; a court; a racetrack; an airport secured area; near an execution site on an execution day; a 51% alcohol business; a high school, college, or professional sporting event; a correctional or civil commitment facility; a hospital, nursing facility, or mental hospital; an amusement park; or an open government meeting with notice. Also covers license holders displaying handguns on college grounds and carrying where campuses prohibit it.
offenses.notes: Licensed carry exceptions, "effective notice" signs (30.06 / 30.07), and defenses are in subsections (b)-(f) and (h)-(i).

tiers.when: Location-restricted knife at a school or college (a)(1)
Sporting event, hospital or nursing facility, amusement park, government meeting ((a)(8), (10), (11), (13)), or college display or campus carry violations ((a-2)-(a-4))

offenses.heading: PLACES WEAPONS PROHIBITED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Unlawful Carrying of Handgun by License Holder
offenses.summary: A license holder carrying a handgun intentionally displays it in plain view in a public place (unless it is holstered, or holstered in a vehicle).
offenses.warning: The section history shows it was repealed by H.B. 4595 (2023), although the website still displays subsection (a). The same conduct is an offense under 46.02(a-5) (Class A misdemeanor). Proofreader: confirm before release.
offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL CARRYING OF HANDGUN BY LICENSE HOLDER

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Unlawful Possession of Firearm
offenses.summary: A convicted felon possesses a firearm within five years of release from confinement or supervision, or after that anywhere other than where they live (a); a criminal street gang member carries a handgun in a vehicle or watercraft (a-1); a person convicted of Class A family-violence assault possesses a firearm within five years of release (b); or a person subject to a protective order possesses a firearm (c).

tiers.when: Gang member with a handgun in a vehicle (a-1), family-violence conviction (b), or protective order (c)

offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF FIREARM

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Unlawful Possession of Metal or Body Armor by Felon
offenses.summary: A person convicted of a felony possesses metal or body armor.
offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF METAL OR BODY ARMOR BY FELON

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibited Weapons
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly possesses, manufactures, transports, repairs, or sells an unregistered explosive weapon or machine gun, armor-piercing ammunition, a chemical dispensing device, a zip gun, a tire deflation device, or an improvised explosive device.
offenses.notes: The current list does not include short-barrel firearms, firearm silencers, or knuckles; those were removed from this section in recent sessions.
offenses.heading: PROHIBITED WEAPONS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Unlawful Transfer of Certain Weapons
offenses.summary: Gives or sells a handgun to someone who intends to use it unlawfully; gives or sells a firearm, club, or location-restricted knife to a child under 18; sells a firearm or ammunition to an intoxicated person or to a felon within five years of release; transfers a handgun to (or receives one while) under an active protective order; or, while prohibited from having a firearm, lies on a firearm purchase form.

tiers.when: Selling or giving a handgun to a child under 18 (a)(2)
False statement on a firearm transfer form by a prohibited person (a)(7)

offenses.heading: UNLAWFUL TRANSFER OF CERTAIN WEAPONS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Interstate Purchase
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A Texas resident may buy firearms, ammunition, reloading components, and accessories in another state if not otherwise prohibited.
offenses.heading: INTERSTATE PURCHASE

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Hoax Bombs
offenses.summary: Knowingly makes, sells, buys, transports, or possesses a hoax bomb intending to make someone believe it is an explosive or to cause an emergency response.
offenses.heading: HOAX BOMBS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Components of Explosives
offenses.summary: Knowingly possesses components of an explosive weapon intending to combine them into an explosive weapon for use in a criminal endeavor.
offenses.heading: COMPONENTS OF EXPLOSIVES

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Deadly Weapon in Penal Institution
offenses.summary: While confined in a penal institution, intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly carries, possesses, or conceals a deadly weapon.
offenses.heading: DEADLY WEAPON IN PENAL INSTITUTION

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Penalty If Offense Committed Within Weapon-Free School Zone
offenses.summary: Not a separate offense. The punishment for a Chapter 46 weapons offense is raised one category if the actor knowingly committed it within 300 feet of a school, or where a school function or UIL event was taking place (with exceptions in (b)).
offenses.heading: PENALTY IF OFFENSE COMMITTED WITHIN WEAPON-FREE SCHOOL ZONE

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Maps as Evidence of Location or Area
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A city or county map approved as an official record of weapon-free school zones is admissible and is prima facie evidence of the zone boundaries.
offenses.heading: MAPS AS EVIDENCE OF LOCATION OR AREA

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Making a Firearm Accessible to a Child
offenses.summary: With criminal negligence, fails to secure a readily dischargeable firearm, or leaves it where a child (younger than 17) would gain access, and a child gains access to it.

tiers.when: The child discharges the firearm and causes death or serious bodily injury

offenses.heading: MAKING A FIREARM ACCESSIBLE TO A CHILD

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Firearm Smuggling
offenses.summary: Knowingly engages in the business (more than once, or for pay) of transporting or transferring firearms the person knows were acquired illegally.

tiers.when: Three or more firearms in a single criminal episode

offenses.heading: FIREARM SMUGGLING

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Gambling
offenses.summary: Bets on the result of a game, contest, or participant's performance; bets on a political nomination, appointment, or election; or plays and bets money or something of value at a game with cards, dice, balls, or another gambling device.
offenses.notes: Defenses for private social gambling (in a private place, no one profits, equal risk) are in subsection (b).
offenses.heading: GAMBLING

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Gambling Promotion
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly operates or profits from a gambling place, engages in bookmaking, holds bets for gain, sells chances on games or elections, or for gain sets up or sells tickets for a lottery.
offenses.heading: GAMBLING PROMOTION

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Keeping a Gambling Place
offenses.summary: Knowingly uses or lets another use property the person owns or controls (building, room, vehicle, boat, etc.) as a gambling place, or rents it expecting such use.
offenses.heading: KEEPING A GAMBLING PLACE

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Communicating Gambling Information
offenses.summary: With intent to further gambling, knowingly communicates information about bets or betting odds, or provides or maintains equipment to transmit it.
offenses.heading: COMMUNICATING GAMBLING INFORMATION

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Possession of Gambling Device, Equipment, or Paraphernalia
offenses.summary: With intent to further gambling, knowingly owns, makes, transfers, or possesses a gambling device or essential part, altered gambling equipment, or gambling paraphernalia.
offenses.heading: POSSESSION OF GAMBLING DEVICE, EQUIPMENT, OR PARAPHERNALIA

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Smoking Tobacco
offenses.summary: Possesses a burning tobacco product, smokes tobacco, or uses an e-cigarette in a public school facility, elevator, enclosed theater, library, museum, hospital, transit or intrastate bus, plane, or train that is a public place.
offenses.notes: Defense: no prominently displayed no-smoking notice (subsection (b)).
offenses.heading: SMOKING TOBACCO

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibitions Relating to Certain Cigarettes
offenses.summary: Knowingly acquires, holds, possesses, transports, or imports for sale or distribution in Texas cigarettes that do not meet federal requirements or that cannot lawfully be tax-stamped.
offenses.heading: PROHIBITIONS RELATING TO CERTAIN CIGARETTES

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibition of the Purchase and Sale of Human Organs
offenses.summary: Knowingly or intentionally offers to buy or sell, acquires, receives, sells, or transfers a human organ for valuable consideration.
offenses.notes: The original spreadsheet listed this as a Class A misdemeanor. It is a state jail felony (amended 2025).
offenses.heading: PROHIBITION OF THE PURCHASE AND SALE OF HUMAN ORGANS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibition on Purchase and Sale of Human Fetal Tissue
offenses.summary: Knowingly offers to buy or sell, acquires, receives, sells, or transfers human fetal tissue for economic benefit.
offenses.heading: PROHIBITION ON PURCHASE AND SALE OF HUMAN FETAL TISSUE

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibition on Purchase and Sale of Adult Stem Cells for Certain Investigational Treatments
offenses.summary: Knowingly offers to buy or sell, acquires, receives, sells, or transfers adult stem cells for valuable consideration for use in an investigational stem cell treatment.
offenses.heading: PROHIBITION ON PURCHASE AND SALE OF ADULT STEM CELLS FOR CERTAIN INVESTIGATIONAL TREATMENTS

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.name: Prohibited Camping
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly camps (sleeps, cooks, builds a fire, stores belongings for an extended time, etc.) in a public place without consent of the agency that manages it.
offenses.notes: Before or when issuing a citation, the officer must make a reasonable effort to tell the person of a lawful alternative place to camp and, if appropriate, contact local officials or a nonprofit for services (subsection (g)), unless there is an imminent threat to health or safety (subsection (h)).
offenses.heading: PROHIBITED CAMPING

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Public Intoxication
offenses.summary: Appears in a public place (including a TABC-licensed premises) while intoxicated to the degree that the person may endanger themselves or another.
offenses.notes: Public intoxication is not a lesser included offense of DWI (subsection (d)).

tiers.level: Punished as a minor's alcohol offense (ABC 106.071)

offenses.heading: PUBLIC INTOXICATION

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Possession of Alcoholic Beverage in Motor Vehicle
offenses.summary: Knowingly possesses an open container of alcohol in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public highway, whether the vehicle is moving, stopped, or parked. The passenger area does not include a locked glove box, the trunk, or the area behind the last upright seat if there is no trunk.
offenses.notes: Passengers in buses, taxis, limousines, or the living quarters of a motor home are excepted. The officer must issue a citation, not arrest, if the person signs a promise to appear (subsection (e)).
offenses.heading: POSSESSION OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE IN MOTOR VEHICLE

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Driving While Intoxicated
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating a motor vehicle in a public place. "Intoxicated" means not having normal use of mental or physical faculties because of alcohol, drugs, or any other substance, or having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more (49.01).
offenses.notes: NEW IN 2025 (S.B. 826): DWI in an active school crossing zone is a state jail felony. A deferred adjudication for DWI counts as a conviction for 49.09 enhancement (49.09(g)). Repeat offenders within five years must get an ignition interlock (49.09(h)).

tiers.when: Open container of alcohol in the driver's immediate possession
Blood, breath, or urine analysis showed 0.15 or more
Driving in a school crossing zone while the reduced school speed limit applies
One prior conviction of an offense relating to operating a motor vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft, or an amusement ride, while intoxicated (defined in 49.09(c)) (DWI 2nd)
Two prior intoxication-related convictions (DWI 3rd or more)
One prior conviction of intoxication manslaughter (Texas or a substantially similar out-of-state law)

offenses.heading: DRIVING WHILE INTOXICATED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Driving While Intoxicated with Child Passenger
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating a motor vehicle in a public place, and the vehicle is occupied by a passenger younger than 15.

tiers.when: Two prior intoxication-related convictions, or one prior intoxication manslaughter

offenses.heading: DRIVING WHILE INTOXICATED WITH CHILD PASSENGER

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Flying While Intoxicated
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating an aircraft.

tiers.when: One prior conviction of an offense relating to operating a motor vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft, or an amusement ride, while intoxicated (defined in 49.09(c))
Two prior intoxication-related convictions, or one prior intoxication manslaughter

offenses.heading: FLYING WHILE INTOXICATED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Boating While Intoxicated
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating a watercraft (boat, water skis, personal watercraft, etc.).

tiers.when: One prior conviction of an offense relating to operating a motor vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft, or an amusement ride, while intoxicated (defined in 49.09(c))
Two prior intoxication-related convictions, or one prior intoxication manslaughter

offenses.heading: BOATING WHILE INTOXICATED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Boating While Intoxicated with Child Passenger
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating a watercraft occupied by a passenger younger than 15.

tiers.when: Two prior intoxication-related convictions, or one prior intoxication manslaughter

offenses.heading: BOATING WHILE INTOXICATED WITH CHILD PASSENGER

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Assembling or Operating an Amusement Ride While Intoxicated
offenses.summary: Is intoxicated while operating an amusement ride or while assembling a mobile amusement ride.

tiers.when: Open container of alcohol in immediate possession
One prior conviction of an offense relating to operating a motor vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft, or an amusement ride, while intoxicated (defined in 49.09(c))
Two prior intoxication-related convictions, or one prior intoxication manslaughter

offenses.heading: ASSEMBLING OR OPERATING AN AMUSEMENT RIDE WHILE INTOXICATED

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Intoxication Assault
offenses.summary: By accident or mistake, while intoxicated and operating a motor vehicle in a public place (or an aircraft, watercraft, or amusement ride, or assembling a mobile amusement ride), by reason of that intoxication causes serious bodily injury to another.
offenses.notes: NEW IN 2025 (S.B. 745): intoxication assault of a peace officer or judge is a first degree felony.

tiers.when: Serious bodily injury to a firefighter or EMS personnel in the actual discharge of an official duty
Serious bodily injury to a peace officer or judge in the actual discharge of an official duty
Traumatic brain injury resulting in a persistent vegetative state

offenses.heading: INTOXICATION ASSAULT

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Intoxication Manslaughter
offenses.summary: While operating a motor vehicle in a public place (or an aircraft, watercraft, or amusement ride, or assembling a mobile amusement ride), is intoxicated and by reason of that intoxication causes the death of another by accident or mistake.
offenses.notes: CONFLICT FOR PROOFREADER: the 2025 Legislature passed two versions of 49.09(b-2). Both are shown. Confirm with your prosecutor.

tiers.when: Death of a peace officer, judge, firefighter, or EMS personnel on duty; or more than one death in the same transaction (S.B. 745 version)
Death of a peace officer, judge, firefighter, or EMS personnel on duty; or a prior intoxication-related conviction while the actor was in violation of Chapter 51 (H.B. 2017 version)

offenses.heading: INTOXICATION MANSLAUGHTER

offenses.group: Title 10. Offenses Against Public Health, Safety, and Morals
offenses.chapter: Ch. 49 Intoxication and Alcoholic Beverage Offenses
offenses.name: Enhanced Offenses and Penalties
offenses.summary: Not a separate offense. Raises the punishment for intoxication offenses: one prior intoxication-related conviction makes DWI, FWI, BWI, or amusement-ride intoxication a Class A misdemeanor (minimum 30 days); two priors, or one prior intoxication manslaughter, makes it a third degree felony; and it sets the higher levels for intoxication assault and manslaughter of officers and first responders. It also defines which prior offenses count and requires ignition interlocks for repeat offenders within five years.
offenses.heading: ENHANCED OFFENSES AND PENALTIES

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.name: Engaging in Organized Criminal Activity
offenses.summary: With intent to establish, maintain, or take part in a combination (three or more people collaborating in criminal activity) or its profits, or as a member of a criminal street gang or foreign terrorist organization, commits or conspires to commit a listed offense (including murder, robbery, burglary, theft, aggravated assault, Class A assault, deadly conduct, burglary of a vehicle, unauthorized use of a vehicle, drug delivery, prostitution promotion, weapons trafficking, human smuggling or trafficking, felony fraud, and street-racing or takeover offenses).
offenses.notes: Two 2025 versions of the list in subsection (a) exist (one adds possession with intent to deliver drugs and fentanyl; the other adds 43.235). Conspiracy to commit this offense is punished the same as the offense (subsection (c)).

tiers.level: One category higher than the most serious listed offense

tiers.when: Most serious listed offense is a Class A misdemeanor
Most serious offense is aggravated sexual assault of a child under 6, of a child under 14 with aggravating factors, or of a child under 17 with serious bodily injury, by an adult
Most serious offense is continuous smuggling punishable under 20.06(g)
Most serious offense is any other first degree felony

tiers.level: Same category as the most serious listed offense
tiers.when: Defendant proves at punishment a voluntary, complete withdrawal and a substantial effort to prevent the offense
A deadly weapon was used or exhibited (applies when the (b) level is second degree or lower)

offenses.heading: ENGAGING IN ORGANIZED CRIMINAL ACTIVITY

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.name: Violation of Court Order Enjoining Organized Criminal Activity
offenses.summary: Knowingly violates a temporary or permanent gang injunction (Civil Practice and Remedies Code 125.065).
offenses.heading: VIOLATION OF COURT ORDER ENJOINING ORGANIZED CRIMINAL ACTIVITY

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.name: Coercing, Inducing, or Soliciting Membership in a Criminal Street Gang or Foreign Terrorist Organization
offenses.summary: Knowingly causes, encourages, recruits, or solicits a person to join a criminal street gang or foreign terrorist organization that requires a Class A or felony offense for membership; or threatens or injures a child or the child's family to coerce the child to take part in gang activity.
aliases: Coercing, Inducing, or Soliciting Membership in a Criminal Street Gang
offenses.heading: COERCING, INDUCING, OR SOLICITING MEMBERSHIP IN A CRIMINAL STREET GANG OR FOREIGN TERRORIST ORGANIZATION

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.name: Directing Activities of Criminal Street Gangs or Foreign Terrorist Organizations
offenses.summary: As part of the identifiable leadership of a criminal street gang or foreign terrorist organization, knowingly finances, directs, or supervises members in committing a "3g" felony, a felony with a deadly weapon, or a top-tier drug delivery or possession offense.
aliases: Directing Activities of Criminal Street Gangs
offenses.heading: DIRECTING ACTIVITIES OF CRIMINAL STREET GANGS OR FOREIGN TERRORIST ORGANIZATIONS

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.name: Gang-Free Zones
offenses.summary: Not a separate offense. For listed gang-related offenses by an actor 17 or older, punishment is raised one category if committed within 1,000 feet of a school, college, youth center, playground, or residential treatment center; within 300 feet of a shopping mall, movie theater, public pool, or video arcade; or on a school bus. Does not apply if the offense is already a first degree felony under 71.02.
offenses.heading: GANG-FREE ZONES

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.chapter: Ch. 72 Racketeering and Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.name: Use of Proceeds Derived from Racketeering or Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.summary: Intentionally uses or invests proceeds knowingly derived from a pattern of racketeering or unlawful debt collection to acquire real property or an interest in it, or to establish or operate an enterprise.
offenses.heading: USE OF PROCEEDS DERIVED FROM RACKETEERING OR UNLAWFUL DEBT COLLECTION

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.chapter: Ch. 72 Racketeering and Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.name: Acquisition of Interest in Property or Control of Enterprise Through Racketeering or Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.summary: Through a pattern of racketeering or unlawful debt collection, knowingly acquires or keeps an interest in or control of an enterprise or real property.
offenses.heading: ACQUISITION OF INTEREST IN PROPERTY OR CONTROL OF ENTERPRISE THROUGH RACKETEERING OR UNLAWFUL DEBT COLLECTION

offenses.group: Title 11. Organized Crime
offenses.chapter: Ch. 72 Racketeering and Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.name: Participation in Enterprise Through Racketeering or Unlawful Debt Collection
offenses.summary: Being employed by or associated with an enterprise, knowingly conducts or participates in it through a pattern of racketeering or unlawful debt collection.
offenses.heading: PARTICIPATION IN ENTERPRISE THROUGH RACKETEERING OR UNLAWFUL DEBT COLLECTION

offenses.group: Title 12. Terrorism
offenses.name: Terrorism
offenses.summary: Commits or conspires to commit a listed violent offense (homicide, unlawful restraint, kidnapping, trafficking, aggravated assault, aggravated sexual assault, felony deadly conduct or terroristic threat, product tampering, arson, felony railroad interference, aggravated robbery, felony radio interference, or hoax bomb) with intent to intimidate or coerce the public, or to influence government by intimidation or coercion.

tiers.level: One category higher than the most serious listed offense

tiers.when: Most serious listed offense is a Class A misdemeanor
Most serious listed offense is a first degree felony

offenses.heading: TERRORISM

offenses.group: Title 12. Terrorism
offenses.name: Aiding in Commission of Terrorism
offenses.summary: Intentionally raises, collects, or provides material support or resources knowing or intending that they will be used to commit or aid terrorism (76.02).

tiers.level: Same degree as the terrorism offense aided

offenses.heading: AIDING IN COMMISSION OF TERRORISM

offenses.group: Title 12. Terrorism
offenses.name: Hindering Prosecution of Terrorism
offenses.summary: With intent to hinder the arrest or prosecution of another for terrorism or aiding terrorism, harbors or conceals them, helps them avoid arrest or escape, warns them, or tampers with evidence.

tiers.level: Same degree as the underlying terrorism offense

offenses.heading: HINDERING PROSECUTION OF TERRORISM

offenses.group: Title 12. Terrorism
offenses.name: Transnational Repression
offenses.summary: As an agent of a foreign government or foreign terrorist organization, commits or conspires to commit trafficking, assault, aggravated assault, harassment, stalking, or compelling prostitution, intending to make someone act for the foreign power, leave or stay confined in the U.S., or to discourage or retaliate for protected conduct.

tiers.level: One category higher than the most serious listed offense

tiers.when: Most serious listed offense is a first degree felony

offenses.heading: TRANSNATIONAL REPRESSION

offenses.group: Title 12. Terrorism
offenses.name: Unauthorized Enforcement of Foreign Law
offenses.summary: As an agent of a foreign government or foreign terrorist organization, without state or federal approval, prevents a person in Texas from violating foreign law, or investigates, monitors, or surveils them to prevent such violations.
offenses.heading: UNAUTHORIZED ENFORCEMENT OF FOREIGN LAW

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Altering Vehicle Identity (Serial Number / VIN)
offenses.summary: Stamps or places a serial number (VIN) on a vehicle or vehicle part with intent to change the vehicle's identity.
offenses.notes: Affirmative defense: a manufacturer employee acting in the course of employment, or a person acting for or under rules of TxDMV. Removing or altering serial numbers on other property is PC 31.11.
offenses.heading: PLACEMENT OF SERIAL NUMBER WITH INTENT TO CHANGE IDENTITY

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: False Name, False Information, and Forgery
offenses.summary: Knowingly provides false or incorrect information, or signs another's name without authority, on a title application, application for a certified copy of a title, assignment of title, lien release, or other document needed to transfer ownership of a motor vehicle.
offenses.heading: FALSE NAME, FALSE INFORMATION, AND FORGERY

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Expired Registration
offenses.summary: After the fifth working day following the expiration of a vehicle's registration, operates on a public highway a motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer whose plate has not been validated by a current registration insignia (sticker).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the registration is renewed within 20 working days (or before the first court date, whichever is later) and a reimbursement fee of up to $20 is paid. Defense: the county tax office was closed for a protracted period and the registration was expired 30 working days or less.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE WITH EXPIRED LICENSE PLATE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Falsification or Forgery
offenses.summary: Knowingly provides false or incorrect information, or signs another person's name without authority, on a statement or application required for vehicle registration (with listed exceptions).
offenses.notes: Penalty raised to a third degree felony by recent amendments (last amended 2025).
offenses.heading: FALSIFICATION OR FORGERY

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: General Penalty (Registration Chapter)
offenses.summary: Violating a provision of Chapter 502 with no other penalty is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $200 (except listed sections).
offenses.heading: GENERAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operating Unregistered Vehicle / Improper Registration
offenses.summary: Operates a motor vehicle that has not been registered, or is registered for the wrong class of vehicle, as required by law.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE UNDER IMPROPER REGISTRATION

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: No Registration Insignia Displayed
offenses.summary: Operates on a public highway a motor vehicle that does not properly display the current registration insignia (sticker), or a road tractor, motorcycle, trailer, or semitrailer without one (dealers operating as allowed by law excepted).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge for a motor vehicle if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance, or the defendant shows a valid sticker was issued and attached, and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE WITHOUT REGISTRATION INSIGNIA

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Wrong, Fictitious, or Altered Registration Insignia
offenses.summary: Attaches to or displays on a motor vehicle a registration sticker that belongs to a different vehicle, was issued under another law, is for a different registration period, or is fictitious.
offenses.notes: A charge for a sticker from another registration period may be dismissed if fixed before the first court appearance with a fee of up to $10.

tiers.when: Wrong vehicle, wrong law, or wrong period
Owner knowingly altered or made the identification marks illegible

offenses.heading: WRONG, FICTITIOUS, ALTERED, OR OBSCURED INSIGNIA

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Deceptively Similar Insignia
offenses.summary: Manufactures, sells, or possesses a registration sticker deceptively similar to the official one (one a reasonable person would think was issued by TxDMV), or copies one for sale.

tiers.when: Possessing, with a prior conviction for possessing

offenses.heading: DECEPTIVELY SIMILAR INSIGNIA

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.chapter: Ch. 503 Dealer's and Manufacturer's Vehicle License Plates
offenses.name: Criminal Penalty
offenses.summary: Violates a provision of the dealer and manufacturer license and plate chapter (Chapter 503), such as misuse of dealer or temporary tags.
offenses.notes: Paper temporary tags were replaced by temporary metal plates effective July 1, 2025 (H.B. 718, 2023). Fake temporary tags may also be charged as tampering with a governmental record (PC 37.10(c)(6), Class A).

tiers.when: Violation was willful or with conscious indifference to the law

offenses.heading: CRIMINAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: No License Plate / Missing Front Plate
offenses.summary: Operates on a public highway a motor vehicle that does not display two license plates assigned for the period and placed according to TxDMV rules (front and rear), or a road tractor, motorcycle, trailer, or semitrailer without its one plate.
offenses.notes: A charge for a missing plate on a motor vehicle may be dismissed if fixed before the first court appearance with a fee of up to $10. Dealers operating as allowed by law are excepted.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE WITHOUT LICENSE PLATE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Vehicle with Wrong License Plate
offenses.summary: Operates, or as owner permits another to operate, on a public highway a motor vehicle with a plate or registration sticker issued for a different vehicle.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE WITH WRONG LICENSE PLATE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Wrong, Fictitious, Altered, or Obscured License Plate
offenses.summary: Attaches to or displays on a motor vehicle a license plate that is issued for a different vehicle, issued under another law, for a different registration period, or fictitious; has blurring or reflective matter that significantly impairs reading the state name or plate number; has an unauthorized light, sticker, decal, or emblem that interferes with readability; or has a coating, cover, or other material that distorts angular visibility, obscures half or more of the state name, or covers the plate number or color. (Normal trailer hitches, toll tags, wheelchair carriers, towed trailers, and bike racks are excepted.)
offenses.notes: Charges under (a)(3), (5), (6), or (7) may be dismissed if fixed before the first court appearance, with a fee of up to $10 and proof the vehicle was registered.

tiers.when: Owner knowingly altered or made the plate illegible
Plate cover or material obscuring the number or color (a)(7)(C), first offense
Same, with two or more prior convictions

offenses.heading: WRONG, FICTITIOUS, ALTERED, OR OBSCURED LICENSE PLATE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: Deceptively Similar License Plate
offenses.summary: Manufactures, sells, or possesses a license plate deceptively similar to an official Texas plate, or copies one for sale (licensed producers excepted).

tiers.when: Possessing, with a prior conviction for possessing

offenses.heading: DECEPTIVELY SIMILAR LICENSE PLATE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: License Plate Flipper
offenses.summary: With criminal negligence buys or possesses (b), or makes, sells, or distributes (c), a device designed to switch between license plates or flip a plate to hide its number.
offenses.heading: LICENSE PLATE FLIPPER; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle A. Certificates of Title and Registration of Vehicles
offenses.name: General Penalty (License Plate Chapter)
offenses.summary: Violating a provision of Chapter 504 with no other penalty is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $5 to $200.
offenses.heading: GENERAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Driver's License Required
offenses.summary: A person may not drive a motor vehicle on a highway in Texas without a Texas driver's license unless exempted by the chapter (for example, new residents for 90 days with a valid license from their prior state (521.029), and nonresidents with a valid home-state license (521.030)). Driving without a license, or without the right class, is charged under 521.025.
offenses.heading: LICENSE REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: No Driver's License / Failure to Display License
offenses.summary: A person required to have a driver's license fails to have in their possession, while driving, the class of license appropriate for the vehicle, or fails to display it when demanded by a peace officer, magistrate, or court officer. An officer may stop and detain a driver to determine whether they have a license.
offenses.notes: Defense: the person produces in court a license issued to them, appropriate for the vehicle, that was valid at the time of the arrest (subsection (d)). New residents have 90 days to get a Texas license (521.029). A vehicle may be towed when the driver has no license (545.305).

tiers.when: Second conviction within one year of the first

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine $25 to $500 and/or 72 hours to 6 months jail
tiers.when: Third or later conviction within one year of the second
Driving without insurance (601.191) and caused or was at fault in a collision with serious bodily injury or death

offenses.heading: LICENSE TO BE CARRIED AND EXHIBITED ON DEMAND; CRIMINAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Notice of Change of Address or Name
offenses.summary: A license or ID holder who moves or changes their name fails to notify DPS within 30 days and apply for a duplicate license showing the current address.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defendant fixes it within 20 working days and pays a reimbursement fee of up to $20.

tiers.when: General driver's license penalty (no specific penalty)

offenses.heading: NOTICE OF CHANGE OF ADDRESS OR NAME

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Driver Record Monitoring Pilot Program
offenses.summary: A contractor in the DPS driver record monitoring program discloses information it received from DPS in a way that violates the contract.
offenses.heading: DRIVER RECORD MONITORING PILOT PROGRAM

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Electronically Readable Information
offenses.summary: Accesses or uses the electronically readable (magnetic stripe or barcode) information on a driver's license or ID, or compiles a database of it, except as allowed (such as verifying age or identity for listed purposes).
offenses.heading: ELECTRONICALLY READABLE INFORMATION

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Imposition of Special Restrictions and Endorsements
offenses.summary: Drives a motor vehicle in violation of a restriction on the person's license (such as corrective lenses or daytime only) or without a required endorsement.
offenses.heading: IMPOSITION OF SPECIAL RESTRICTIONS AND ENDORSEMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Learner License
offenses.summary: The person occupying the seat beside a learner-license driver sleeps, is intoxicated, or is doing something that prevents them from watching and responding to the driver.
offenses.notes: Defense: another qualified licensed adult also occupied the seat by the driver and was not in violation (subsection (h)).

tiers.when: General driver's license penalty (no specific penalty)

offenses.heading: LEARNER LICENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Criminal Offense
offenses.summary: A holder of an occupational (essential need) driver's license drives in violation of its restrictions (hours, routes, purpose, ignition interlock, etc.) or fails to have a certified copy of the court order in their possession.
offenses.heading: CRIMINAL OFFENSE; PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Surrender of License; Return
offenses.summary: Fails or refuses to surrender a suspended, revoked, or canceled license to DPS after DPS demands it.
offenses.heading: SURRENDER OF LICENSE; RETURN

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Fictitious or Altered License; Misuse of License
offenses.summary: Displays or possesses a driver's license or ID the person knows is fictitious or altered; lends their license or lets another use it; displays someone else's license as their own; has more than one valid license or ID; or gives a false name, false address, counterfeit document, or false statement in a license application.
offenses.heading: GENERAL VIOLATION

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Fake ID by Person Under 21
