offenses.summary: A person under 21 possesses, intending to represent that they are 21 or older, a document deceptively similar to a driver's license or ID (one a reasonable person would think was government-issued) that is not marked "NOT A GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT" in red on both sides.
offenses.notes: A peace officer may confiscate the document (subsection (c)). The court may order 8 hours of community service (12 with a prior offense).
offenses.heading: FICTITIOUS LICENSE OR CERTIFICATE

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: False Application
offenses.summary: Knowingly swears or affirms falsely to information required in an application for a driver's license or ID.
offenses.heading: FALSE APPLICATION

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Use of Illegal License or Certificate
offenses.summary: Intentionally or knowingly uses a license or ID obtained by fraud or false application to harm or defraud another.
offenses.heading: USE OF ILLEGAL LICENSE OR CERTIFICATE

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Delivery or Manufacture of Counterfeit Instrument
offenses.summary: Possesses with intent to sell or deliver (a), manufactures or produces for sale (b), or possesses with intent to use or pass (c) a forged or counterfeit driver's license, ID, or similar instrument not issued by an authorized agency.

tiers.when: Possession with intent to sell or deliver
Manufacturing or producing to sell or deliver
Possession with intent to use, circulate, or pass

offenses.heading: DELIVERY OR MANUFACTURE OF COUNTERFEIT INSTRUMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Conspiring to Manufacture Counterfeit License or Certificate
offenses.summary: Establishes, maintains, participates in, or conspires with a combination or criminal street gang (or shares its profits) to manufacture counterfeit licenses or IDs for sale or distribution.
offenses.heading: CONSPIRING TO MANUFACTURE COUNTERFEIT LICENSE OR CERTIFICATE

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Driving While License Invalid (DWLI)
offenses.summary: Drives a motor vehicle on a highway after the person's license was canceled (with no new license issued), while it is suspended or revoked, while it is expired if it expired during a suspension, or after renewal was denied; or drives while subject to an order prohibiting the person from obtaining a license.
offenses.notes: Since 2019, a person is not driving while license invalid merely because the license has expired (unless it expired during a suspension). Notice of the suspension is generally required; confirm proof requirements with your prosecutor. A vehicle may be towed (545.305).

tiers.when: License was previously suspended because of an intoxication-related driving offense
Driving without insurance and caused or was at fault in a collision with serious bodily injury or death

offenses.heading: DRIVING WHILE LICENSE INVALID

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: General Penalty (Driver's License Chapter)
offenses.summary: Violating any provision of Chapter 521 that has no specific penalty is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to $200.
offenses.heading: GENERAL CRIMINAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: No Commercial Driver's License
offenses.summary: Drives a commercial motor vehicle without a CDL of the proper class in immediate possession (or while disqualified or under an out-of-service order), or with only a commercial learner's permit without a qualified CDL holder supervising from the adjacent seat, unless otherwise authorized (522.015).
offenses.notes: Defense: producing in court a valid CDL (or permit and license) issued to the person that was valid at the time.

tiers.when: Prior conviction under this section within the preceding year

offenses.heading: LICENSE OR PERMIT REQUIRED; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle B. Driver's Licenses and Personal Identification Cards
offenses.name: Driving While Disqualified (Commercial Vehicle)
offenses.summary: Drives a commercial motor vehicle on a highway after being denied a license or permit, while disqualified, while the license expired during a disqualification, while under an order prohibiting a license, or while the driver, employer, or vehicle is under an out-of-service order.
offenses.notes: Lack of notice is an affirmative defense, except for automatic disqualifications that follow a conviction. Notice mailed to the last known address is presumed.

tiers.when: Prior conviction, or also driving without insurance
Without insurance and at fault in a collision with serious bodily injury or death

offenses.heading: DRIVING WHILE DISQUALIFIED PROHIBITED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: General Offense (Rules of the Road)
offenses.summary: Not a separate charge. A person commits an offense by doing anything the rules of the road (Transportation Code Subtitle C, chapters 541-551) prohibit, or failing to do anything they require. Unless another penalty is provided, the offense is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $1 to $200 (542.401).
offenses.heading: GENERAL OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Offense by Person Owning or Controlling Vehicle
offenses.summary: A vehicle owner, or a person who employs or directs a driver, requires or knowingly permits the driver to operate the vehicle in violation of law.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OFFENSE BY PERSON OWNING OR CONTROLLING VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Inchoate Offense
offenses.summary: Not a separate charge. Attempting or conspiring to commit a traffic offense, or knowingly permitting another to commit one, is the same offense.
offenses.heading: INCHOATE OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: General Penalty (Traffic Offenses)
offenses.summary: A traffic misdemeanor with no other stated penalty is punishable by a fine of $1 to $200. Court costs and a $50 state traffic fine (542.4031) are added.
offenses.heading: GENERAL PENALTY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Work Zone Double Fines
offenses.summary: If a traffic offense (other than an inspection, pedestrian, child seat, or seat belt offense) is committed in a construction or maintenance work zone when workers are present, and the citation says workers were present, the minimum and maximum fines double. For speeding, the zone must be marked with a speed limit sign.
offenses.heading: FINE FOR OFFENSE IN CONSTRUCTION OR MAINTENANCE WORK ZONE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Yield Causing Injury
offenses.summary: If a failure to yield the right-of-way causes a collision: fine $500 to $2,000 if someone other than the driver suffered bodily injury; $1,000 to $4,000 if someone suffered serious bodily injury.
offenses.heading: PENALTIES FOR FAILURE TO YIELD RIGHT-OF-WAY OFFENSE RESULTING IN COLLISION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Comply With Lawful Order of Police Officer
offenses.summary: Willfully fails or refuses to comply with a lawful order or direction of a police officer, a school crossing guard performing crossing duties, or an escort flagger for an oversize or overweight load.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OBEDIENCE REQUIRED TO POLICE OFFICERS, SCHOOL CROSSING GUARDS, AND ESCORT FLAGGERS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Placing and Maintaining Traffic-Control Device
offenses.summary: Not an offense. TxDOT places traffic-control devices on state highways and local authorities on their own roads, following the state sign manual; a local authority may not place devices on a TxDOT highway without permission. Unauthorized signs are covered by 544.006.
offenses.heading: PLACING AND MAINTAINING TRAFFIC-CONTROL DEVICE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Disregard of Traffic-Control Device
offenses.summary: A driver fails to comply with an applicable official traffic-control device (sign, signal, or marking), unless directed otherwise by an officer or flagger or driving an authorized emergency vehicle under its exceptions.
offenses.notes: A device-based violation cannot be enforced if the device was not in proper position and sufficiently legible to an ordinarily observant person (subsection (b)). Fines double in an active construction or maintenance work zone when the citation notes workers were present (542.404).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: COMPLIANCE WITH TRAFFIC-CONTROL DEVICE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Interference with Traffic-Control Device or Railroad Sign or Signal
offenses.summary: Without lawful authority alters, damages, knocks down, or removes (or attempts to) an official traffic-control device or railroad sign or signal, or any part of one.
offenses.notes: Damage may also be criminal mischief (PC 28.03), which has higher penalties.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH TRAFFIC-CONTROL DEVICE OR RAILROAD SIGN OR SIGNAL

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Traffic-Control Signal Preemption Device
offenses.summary: Uses, sells, buys, or possesses for use or sale a device designed to change traffic signals (signal preemption device), except emergency services and transit vehicles. Possession is presumed to be for use or sale.
offenses.heading: TRAFFIC-CONTROL SIGNAL PREEMPTION DEVICE; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Display of Unauthorized Signs, Signals, or Markings
offenses.summary: Places or displays, on or in view of a highway, an unauthorized sign, signal, or marking that imitates an official device, attempts to direct traffic, or hides or interferes with an official device; places a traffic sign with advertising on a highway; or places a flashing light or sign within 1,000 feet of an intersection without a permit.
aliases: Display of Unauthorized Signs, Signals or Markings
Display Traffic Sign or Signal with Advertising
Flashing Light or Sign within 1000ft of Intersection
Place or Maintain Unauthorized Sign or Device

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DISPLAY OF UNAUTHORIZED SIGNS, SIGNALS, OR MARKINGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Traffic-Control Signals (Red Light, Green, Arrows)
offenses.summary: Rules for drivers at traffic signals. On a circular green, the driver may proceed but must yield to vehicles lawfully in the intersection and to pedestrians in an adjacent crosswalk. On a green arrow, the driver may enter cautiously in the arrow's direction and yield to pedestrians and other lawful traffic. On a steady red, the driver must stop at the stop line (or before the crosswalk, or the intersection) and remain stopped unless turning right (or left from one one-way street onto another) where permitted, after stopping and yielding.
offenses.notes: A steady yellow warns that the green is ending or a red is coming. A signal that is dark (no indication showing), other than a freeway ramp meter or pedestrian hybrid beacon, must be treated as a stop sign (subsection (i)). Right turns on red may be prohibited by posted signs. Last amended 2025 (S.B. 2039). Fines double in an active construction or maintenance work zone when the citation notes workers were present (542.404).
aliases: Disregarded Sole Green Turn Signal Arrow
Fail to Stop at Proper Place (at Traffic Light)
Fail to Stop at Proper Place (not at Intersection)
Fail to Yield ROW on Green Arrow Signal
Fail to Yield ROW on Green Signal
Fail to Yield ROW to Pedestrian at Singal Intersection

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TRAFFIC-CONTROL SIGNALS IN GENERAL

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Flashing Signals
offenses.summary: At a flashing red signal, the driver must stop at the stop line (or before the crosswalk or intersection) and then proceed as at a stop sign. At a flashing yellow, the driver may proceed only with caution. Does not apply at railroad crossings.
aliases: Disregarded Flashing Red Signal (at Stop Sign, Etc.)
Fail to Stop at Proper Place (Flashing Red Signal)

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: FLASHING SIGNALS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Lane-Direction-Control Signals
offenses.summary: Where lane-direction-control signals are over individual lanes, a vehicle may travel in a lane under a green signal but may not enter or travel in a lane under a red signal.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: LANE-DIRECTION-CONTROL SIGNALS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 544 Traffic Signs, Signals, and Markings
offenses.name: Stop Signs and Yield Signs
offenses.summary: At a stop sign (unless directed by an officer or signal), and at a yield sign when safety requires, the driver must stop at the clearly marked stop line; if none, before the crosswalk on the near side; if neither, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver can see approaching traffic.
offenses.notes: Right-of-way after stopping is in 545.151 and 545.153. Fines double in an active construction or maintenance work zone when the citation notes workers were present (542.404).
aliases: Fail to Stop - Designated Point - at Stop Sign
Fail to Stop - Designated Point - at Yield Sign

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: STOP SIGNS AND YIELD SIGNS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Right Side of Roadway
offenses.summary: On a roadway wide enough, drives on the right half unless passing, avoiding an obstruction (yielding to oncoming traffic), on a three-lane road, or on a one-way road. A vehicle slower than normal traffic must use the right lane or stay near the right edge unless passing or preparing to turn left. On a two-way road with four or more lanes, may not drive left of center except where a device allows, around an obstruction, or to turn left into or out of a driveway.
aliases: Fail to Yield ROW on Left at Obstruction
Slower Vehicle Failed to Keep Right
Wrong Side of Road - Not Passing
Wrong Side, 4 or More Lane, Two-Way Roadway

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON RIGHT SIDE OF ROADWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving Past Vehicle Moving in Opposite Direction
offenses.summary: When meeting an oncoming vehicle, the driver must keep to the right and, on a road with one lane each way, give the other driver at least half the main traveled roadway, or as much as possible.
aliases: Failed to Give One-Half of Roadway (Meeting Oncoming)
Failed to Pass Met Vehicle to Right

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING PAST VEHICLE MOVING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing to the Left; Return; Being Passed
offenses.summary: A driver passing on the left must pass at a safe distance and not return to the right until safely clear. A driver being passed must, on audible signal, move or stay to the right and may not speed up until passed (except where passing on the right is allowed).
aliases: Failed to Give Way when Overtaken

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING TO THE LEFT; RETURN; BEING PASSED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing to the Left: Safe Distance
offenses.summary: A driver may not go left of center to pass unless that is authorized and the left side is clearly visible and free of oncoming traffic far enough to pass safely; and must return to the proper lane before coming within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle, or otherwise as soon as practicable.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING TO THE LEFT: SAFE DISTANCE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing in a No-Passing Zone
offenses.summary: A driver must obey no-passing zone signs and markings that are in place and clearly visible, and may not drive left of the roadway in a no-passing zone or left of no-passing striping, except to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
aliases: Passing to the Left: Passing Zones

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING TO THE LEFT: PASSING ZONES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving to Left of Center of Roadway: Limitations Other than Passing
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive left of center within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing in a city (or a marked one outside a city), within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, or tunnel, or while waiting for a state ferry. Does not apply on one-way roads or when turning left into or out of an alley or driveway.
aliases: Driving to the Left Center of Roadway:  Other than Passing
Driving to the Left Center of Roadway: Limitations Other than Passing
Driving to the Left Center of Roadway: Other than Passing
Drove on Wrong Side Road Approaching Railroad Grade Crossing
Drove on Wrong Side - Railroad Crossing
Drove on Wrong Side of Approaching Bridge
Drove on Wrong Side Road Approaching Intersection
Drove on Wrong Side Road Awaiting Access to Ferry

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING TO LEFT OF CENTER OF ROADWAY: LIMITATIONS OTHER THAN PASSING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing to the Right
offenses.summary: A driver may pass on the right only when it is safe and the other vehicle is turning left, on a road with two or more unobstructed lanes each way, or on a one-way road wide enough for two lanes; and may not leave the main traveled roadway to pass on the right except as 545.058 allows.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING TO THE RIGHT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Improved Shoulder
offenses.summary: A driver may use the right improved shoulder only when necessary and safe, and only to stop, stand, or park; to accelerate onto or decelerate before a right turn off the roadway; to pass a vehicle that is slowing, stopped, disabled, or turning left; to let a faster vehicle pass; when a device permits; or to avoid a collision. The left shoulder of a divided or controlled-access highway may be used only by a disabled vehicle that cannot reach the right, when a device permits, or to avoid a collision.
offenses.notes: Limits do not apply to emergency vehicles responding to calls, police patrols, bicycles, or slow-moving vehicles.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON IMPROVED SHOULDER

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: One-Way Roadways and Rotary Traffic Islands
offenses.summary: On a roadway designated and signed for one-way traffic, the driver must travel only in the indicated direction; around a rotary traffic island, only to the right of the island.
aliases: Drove to Left of Rotary Traffic Island
Drove Wrong Way on One-Way Roadway

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: ONE-WAY ROADWAYS AND ROTARY TRAFFIC ISLANDS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Maintain Single Lane
offenses.summary: On a roadway divided into two or more clearly marked lanes, a driver must drive as nearly as practical entirely within a single lane and may not move from the lane unless it can be done safely. On a three-lane two-way road, the center lane may be used only to pass when clear, to prepare for a left turn, or where a device designates it.
offenses.notes: Courts have held that a brief, safe drift over a lane line may not by itself violate this section; the movement must also be unsafe. Confirm current case law with your prosecutor.
aliases: Driving on Roadway Laned for Traffic
Drove Center Lane (Not Passing, Not Turning Left)
Drove in Center Lane (Not Passing/Making Left Turn)
Drove Wrong Way in Designated Lane
Fail to Drive in Single Lane
Failed to Drive in Single Lane
Failed to Use Designated Lane (Slow or Direction)

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON ROADWAY LANED FOR TRAFFIC

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Motorcycles on Roadway Laned for Traffic
offenses.summary: A motorcycle is entitled to the full use of a lane, and other vehicles may not deprive it of that. Two motorcycles may ride side by side in one lane, but not more than two abreast; a motorcyclist may not ride between lanes of traffic moving in the same direction ("lane splitting") or pass a vehicle in the same lane (police on duty excepted).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTORCYCLES ON ROADWAY LANED FOR TRAFFIC

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Multiple-Lane Roadway
offenses.summary: On a one-way road with three or more lanes, a driver entering a lane from the right must yield to a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON MULTIPLE-LANE ROADWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Following Too Closely
offenses.summary: A driver following another vehicle must keep an assured clear distance so they can stop safely without colliding or veering into another vehicle, object, or person, considering speed, traffic, and road conditions. Trucks and vehicles towing outside business or residence districts, and caravans or motorcades, must leave room for passing vehicles to merge in.
offenses.notes: Fines double in an active work zone (542.404).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: FOLLOWING DISTANCE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Divided Highway
offenses.summary: On a divided highway, the driver must use the right-hand roadway unless directed otherwise, and may not drive over, across, or in the median, barrier, or dividing section except through an opening or at an established crossover or intersection.
aliases: Drove on Wrong Side Divided Highway
Drove on Wrong Side of Divided Highway

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON DIVIDED HIGHWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Restricted Access
offenses.summary: A driver may not enter or leave a limited-access or controlled-access roadway (freeway) except at an established entrance or exit.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: RESTRICTED ACCESS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: State and Local Regulation of Limited-Access or Controlled-Access Highways
offenses.summary: Not an offense by itself. The Texas Transportation Commission (state highways) or a local authority (by ordinance) may prohibit parades, funeral processions, pedestrians, bicycles, electric bicycles, small motorcycles (250 cc or less), and nonmotorized traffic on freeways, with signs posted. Violating a posted prohibition is enforced as disregarding a traffic-control device (544.004).
aliases: Prohibited Motor Vehicle on Controlled Access Highway
offenses.heading: STATE AND LOCAL REGULATION OF LIMITED-ACCESS OR CONTROLLED-ACCESS HIGHWAYS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing a Stopped School Bus
offenses.summary: Approaching from either direction a school bus stopped on the highway to load or unload students with its visual signals operating, the driver must stop before reaching the bus and may not proceed until the bus moves, the bus driver signals to proceed, or the signals turn off. Not required on a highway with separate roadways (divided by a median or barrier, not just a turn lane) for a bus on the other roadway.
offenses.notes: Driver's license may be suspended up to six months on a second or later conviction.

tiers.when: Second or later offense within five years
Causes serious bodily injury to another
Prior conviction for causing serious bodily injury under (c)(2)

offenses.heading: PASSING A SCHOOL BUS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Turning at Intersection
offenses.summary: To turn right, approach and turn as close as practicable to the right curb or edge. To turn left, approach in the far-left lane available and finish in a lane lawfully available for that direction; on a two-way road, turn to the left of the center of the intersection where practicable.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TURNING AT INTERSECTION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Turning on Curve or Crest of Grade
offenses.summary: A driver may not make a U-turn approaching a curve or the crest of a hill if the vehicle cannot be seen by other drivers approaching from either direction within 500 feet.
aliases: Made U-Turn on Curve or Hill

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TURNING ON CURVE OR CREST OF GRADE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Safely Turning
offenses.summary: A driver may not turn into a private road or driveway, turn from a direct course, or move right or left on a roadway unless the movement can be made safely.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SAFELY TURNING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Signal Turn or Lane Change
offenses.summary: A driver must signal an intention to turn, change lanes, or start from a parked position, and when turning must signal continuously for at least the last 100 feet before the turn. Turn signals may not be used as a "courtesy" or "go ahead and pass" signal, and only one side may not be lit on a parked or disabled vehicle.
aliases: Fail to Signal with Turn Indicator
Failed to Signal Required Distance Before Turning

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SIGNALING TURNS; USE OF TURN SIGNALS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Signaling Stops
offenses.summary: A driver may not stop or suddenly slow down without first giving a stop signal to the driver behind when there is an opportunity to do so.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SIGNALING STOPS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Signals by Hand and Arm or by Signal Lamp
offenses.summary: Turn and stop signals must be given by hand and arm or by approved signal lamps; lamps are required if the vehicle's body or load is more than 2 feet left of the steering post, or the vehicle or combination extends more than 14 feet behind it.
aliases: Fail to Give Hand Signals When Required
Improper Turn or Stop Hand Signal

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SIGNALS BY HAND AND ARM OR BY SIGNAL LAMP

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Method of Giving Hand and Arm Signals
offenses.summary: Hand signals are given from the left side: arm straight out for a left turn, arm up for a right turn (a cyclist may instead extend the right arm), and arm down to stop or slow.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: METHOD OF GIVING HAND AND ARM SIGNALS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Vehicle Approaching or Entering Intersection
offenses.summary: At an intersection, a driver must stop and yield as directed by a stop or yield sign, or when a signal is dark, and then proceed only when safe. A driver on a one- or two-lane road approaching an uncontrolled intersection with a divided or three-plus-lane road, or on an unpaved road approaching a paved road, must stop and yield to hazard-close vehicles. At other uncontrolled intersections, yield to a vehicle already in the intersection or approaching from the right.
aliases: Fail to Yield at Stop Intersection
Fail to Yield at Yield Intersection
Fail to Yield ROW at Open Intersection (specify type)

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE APPROACHING OR ENTERING INTERSECTION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Yield Right-of-Way Turning Left
offenses.summary: A driver turning left at an intersection or into an alley, private road, or driveway must yield to oncoming vehicles that are in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE TURNING LEFT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Yield at Stop or Yield Sign
offenses.summary: After stopping at a stop sign, the driver must yield to vehicles in the intersection or approaching closely enough to be an immediate hazard. At a yield sign, the driver must slow to a reasonable speed and yield the same way; a collision after driving past a yield sign without stopping is prima facie evidence of failure to yield.
aliases: Vehicle Entering Stop or Yield Intersection
Fail to Yield to Vehicle in Intersection

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE ENTERING STOP OR YIELD INTERSECTION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Vehicle Entering or Leaving Limited-Access or Controlled-Access Highway
offenses.summary: A driver on a freeway access or frontage (feeder) road must yield to vehicles exiting the freeway onto it or leaving it to enter the freeway.
aliases: Fail to Yield to Vehicle Leaving Highway

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE ENTERING OR LEAVING LIMITED-ACCESS OR CONTROLLED-ACCESS HIGHWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Yield Leaving Private Drive
offenses.summary: A driver about to enter or cross a highway from an alley, building, or private road or driveway must yield to vehicles approaching on the highway.
aliases: Vehicle Entering Highway from Private Road or Driveway
Fail to Yield Right of Way from Private Road
Fail to Yield ROW Leaving (Private Drive, Alley, Building)

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE ENTERING HIGHWAY FROM PRIVATE ROAD OR DRIVEWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Yield to Emergency Vehicle
offenses.summary: On the immediate approach of an emergency vehicle using lights and siren (or a police vehicle using either), a medical examiner vehicle, or a justice of the peace vehicle using authorized signals, the driver must yield, immediately pull over parallel to the right edge or curb clear of any intersection, and stop until it passes, unless directed otherwise by police.
aliases: Vehicle Approached by Authorized Emergency Vehicle
Fail to Yield ROW to Emergency Vehicle

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: VEHICLE APPROACHED BY AUTHORIZED EMERGENCY VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Move Over or Slow Down
offenses.summary: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with lights on, a stopped tow truck with lights, a TxDOT, construction, utility, toll, or parking-enforcement vehicle using warning lights, a stopped garbage or recycling truck, or an animal-control vehicle removing an animal, the driver must vacate the lane closest to it (on a road with two or more lanes in that direction) or slow to 20 mph below the posted limit (or to 5 mph when the limit is under 25 mph).
offenses.notes: Garbage trucks and parking-enforcement vehicles were added in recent sessions (last amended 2025). The actor may also be prosecuted under any other applicable law. License may be suspended up to six months with a prior conviction.

tiers.when: Second or later offense within five years
Results in bodily injury to another
Second or later offense resulting in bodily injury

offenses.heading: PASSING CERTAIN VEHICLES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing Streetcar to Left
offenses.summary: A driver may not pass on the left of a streetcar moving in the same direction (even if temporarily stopped) unless directed by police, on a one-way street, or where the tracks prevent it; when lawfully passing a stopped streetcar on the left, must slow down and yield to pedestrians.
aliases: Passed Streetcar on Left Without Reducing Speed/Caution

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING STREETCAR TO LEFT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Passing Streetcar to Right
offenses.summary: A driver passing on the right of a streetcar stopped for passengers must stop at least five feet behind its nearest door and wait until passengers are aboard or safely off the street, unless a safety zone has been established.
aliases: Fail to Stop for Streetcar-or Stop At Wrong
Fail to Stop for Streetcar-or Stop At Wrong Location

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PASSING STREETCAR TO RIGHT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Streetcar Tracks
offenses.summary: A driver on streetcar tracks ahead of a streetcar must move off the track when signaled; may not drive on or cross the track in an intersection in front of a crossing streetcar; and may not turn in front of a streetcar being passed so as to impede it.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON STREETCAR TRACKS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Failure to Stop at Railroad Crossing / Driving Around Crossing Gate
offenses.summary: Approaching a railroad crossing, the driver must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail when a signal warns of a train, a gate is lowered or a flagger warns, a close approaching train sounds a signal and is an immediate hazard, a train is plainly visible and hazardously close, or a sign or signal requires it; and must remain stopped until it is safe. At crossbuck-only crossings, yield to trains and slow to a reasonable speed. Driving around, under, or through a crossing gate or barrier that is closed, closing, or opening is an offense.
offenses.notes: A visible train in hazardous proximity is prima facie evidence it was not safe to proceed. Last amended 2025.
aliases: Obedience to Signal Indicate Approach of Train or Other On-Track Equipment
Disregarded Railroad Crossing Gate or Flagman (15-50ft)
offenses.heading: OBEDIENCE TO SIGNAL INDICATING APPROACH OF TRAIN OR OTHER ON-TRACK EQUIPMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: All Vehicles to Stop at Certain Railroad Grade Crossings
offenses.summary: At a railroad crossing designated particularly dangerous and marked with a stop sign or other device requiring a stop, every driver must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail and then proceed only with due care.
aliases: All Vehicle to Stop at Certain Railroad Grade Crossings
Fail to Stop at Marked Railroad Crossing
Failed to Stop at Marked Railroad Crossing
Heavy Equipment Disregarded Signal of Approaching Train
offenses.heading: ALL VEHICLES TO STOP AT CERTAIN RAILROAD GRADE CROSSINGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Buses to Stop at All Railroad Grade Crossings
offenses.summary: A driver of a motor bus carrying passengers for hire must stop 15 to 50 feet from a railroad crossing, look and listen both ways, proceed only when safe, and not shift gears while crossing (not required in business or residence districts or when directed by police or a signal).
offenses.heading: BUSES TO STOP AT ALL RAILROAD GRADE CROSSINGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: School Buses to Stop at All Railroad Grade Crossings
offenses.summary: A school bus driver must stop 15 to 50 feet from every railroad track at a grade crossing, look and listen both ways, proceed only when safe, and not shift gears while crossing (except at crossings signed "tracks out of service" or "exempt").

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SCHOOL BUSES TO STOP AT ALL RAILROAD GRADE CROSSINGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Vehicles Carrying Explosive Substances or Flammable Liquids
offenses.summary: A vehicle whose principal cargo is explosives or flammable liquids must slow to 20 mph or less within 200 feet of a railroad crossing and look and listen both ways; in a city it must stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail (with exceptions for police or flagger direction, inactive flashing signals, and exempt or industrial tracks).
offenses.heading: VEHICLES CARRYING EXPLOSIVE SUBSTANCES OR FLAMMABLE LIQUIDS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Moving Heavy Equipment at Railroad Grade Crossings
offenses.summary: Slow or low-clearance heavy equipment (crawler tractors, shovels, rollers, etc.) may not cross a railroad track without first notifying the railroad and giving it time to protect the crossing; must stop 15 to 50 feet away and cross only when safe; and may not cross when a train approach warning is given.
offenses.heading: MOVING HEAVY EQUIPMENT AT RAILROAD GRADE CROSSINGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Emerging from an Alley, Driveway, or Building
offenses.summary: A driver coming out of an alley, driveway, or building in a business or residence district must stop before crossing the sidewalk area, yield to pedestrians and sidewalk users, and yield to approaching vehicles when entering the roadway.
aliases: Emerging from an Alley, Driveway, or Buidling

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Failure to yield caused a collision with bodily injury / serious bodily injury to another

offenses.heading: EMERGING FROM AN ALLEY, DRIVEWAY, OR BUILDING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Stopping, Standing, or Parking Outside a Business or Residence District
offenses.summary: Outside a business or residence district, a driver may not stop, park, or leave a vehicle standing on the main traveled part of a highway unless it is impracticable to get off the roadway, the remaining width is open for traffic, and the vehicle is visible for 200 feet each way. Does not apply to an unavoidably disabled vehicle, a waste collection vehicle at work, or a tow truck performing towing duties.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: STOPPING, STANDING, OR PARKING OUTSIDE A BUSINESS OR RESIDENCE DISTRICT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Stopping, Standing, or Parking in Prohibited Places
offenses.summary: A driver may not stop, stand, or park: double-parked; on a sidewalk; in an intersection or crosswalk; next to a safety zone; where it would obstruct traffic at an excavation; on a bridge, elevated structure, or in a tunnel; on railroad tracks; or where signs prohibit stopping. May not stand or park (except momentarily to load or unload passengers) in front of a driveway, within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or signal at the roadside, near a marked fire station entrance, or where signs prohibit standing. May not park (except to load or unload) within 50 feet of a railroad crossing or where signs prohibit parking.
offenses.notes: Exceptions apply to avoid conflict with other traffic or when directed by police or a traffic-control device. Bicycles may be parked on a sidewalk if they do not impede pedestrians. Cities may adopt their own parking rules, usually enforced by ordinance.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: STOPPING, STANDING, OR PARKING PROHIBITED IN CERTAIN PLACES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Additional Parking Regulations
offenses.summary: When stopping or parking on a two-way road, the right wheels must be parallel to and within 18 inches of the right curb or edge; on a one-way road, parallel in the direction of traffic with the right or left wheels within 18 inches of that curb or edge (unless local ordinance or authorized angle parking applies).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL PARKING REGULATIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Moving the Vehicle of Another; Unlawful Parking
offenses.summary: A person may not move a vehicle not lawfully under their control into a prohibited parking place, or away from the curb an unlawful distance.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: MOVING THE VEHICLE OF ANOTHER; UNLAWFUL PARKING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Authority to Remove (Tow) Vehicles
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A peace officer may remove, or require the removal of, a vehicle from a highway if it is unattended and obstructing traffic on a bridge, viaduct, causeway, or tunnel; unlawfully parked blocking a private driveway; reported or identified as stolen; believed abandoned more than 48 hours; disabled and the owner is incapacitated, absent, or does not choose a tow company; operated by a person the officer arrests and must take into custody, or by a person driving without a license (521.021), driving while license invalid (521.457), without insurance (601.191), or a minor driving without a license (729.002); or, in the officer's opinion, a hazard or an obstruction to government functions, or because of a catastrophe or emergency.
offenses.heading: AUTHORIZED REMOVAL OF CERTAIN MOTOR VEHICLES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Overnight Parking of Commercial Motor Vehicle in or Near Residential Subdivision
offenses.summary: From 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., parks or leaves parked a commercial motor vehicle (including truck tractors and semitrailers) on a county or city street in, or adjacent to and within 1,000 feet of a residence, school, church, or park in, a residential subdivision (in a county over 220,000) where signs prohibiting overnight commercial parking are posted, unless it is there only to deliver or do work.
offenses.heading: OVERNIGHT PARKING OF COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE IN OR NEAR RESIDENTIAL SUBDIVISION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Speed Not Reasonable and Prudent / Failure to Control Speed
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions and actual and potential hazards, and must control speed as necessary to avoid colliding with any person or vehicle lawfully on or entering the highway. The driver must slow down approaching and crossing intersections and railroad crossings, on curves and hill crests, on narrow or winding roads, and when special hazards exist (pedestrians, weather, road conditions).
offenses.notes: Fines double in an active work zone when posted (542.404).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: MAXIMUM SPEED REQUIREMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Speeding (Prima Facie Speed Limits)
offenses.summary: Driving faster than the limit is prima facie evidence the speed is unreasonable and unlawful. Unless posted otherwise: 30 mph on streets in an urban district and 15 mph in alleys; 70 mph on numbered state or U.S. highways outside urban districts (including farm-to-market roads); 60 mph on other roads outside urban districts; 15 mph on beaches; lower limits for school buses. Posted limits set under 545.353-545.356 replace these.
offenses.notes: An "urban district" is an area with business or residential buildings less than 100 feet apart for at least a quarter mile along the highway. Speeding less than 10% over the limit outside a school zone is not counted as a moving violation for some purposes (542.304). Fines double in an active work zone when posted (542.404).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PRIMA FACIE SPEED LIMITS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Authority of Texas Transportation Commission to Alter Speed Limits
offenses.summary: Not an offense. The Texas Transportation Commission may set different speed limits (up to 75 mph, or higher on specified highways) after an engineering and traffic investigation; the limit takes effect when signs are posted. Counties (545.355) and cities (545.356) have similar authority on their roads.
offenses.heading: AUTHORITY OF TEXAS TRANSPORTATION COMMISSION TO ALTER SPEED LIMITS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Special Speed Limitations
offenses.summary: Special limits: a moped or small motorcycle (250 cc or less) may not exceed 35 mph at night unless its headlamp lights 300 feet ahead; solid-rubber-tired vehicles may not exceed 10 mph; posted bridge and elevated-structure limits must be obeyed; and unregistered agricultural chemical applicators may not exceed 30 mph.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SPECIAL SPEED LIMITATIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Impeding Traffic (Minimum Speed)
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive so slowly as to impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic, except when necessary for safety or to comply with law, and may not drive below a posted minimum speed limit except as necessary for safety.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: MINIMUM SPEED REGULATIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Reckless Driving
offenses.summary: Drives a vehicle in willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property. Applies on highways and other public places, and in business parking lots and private access ways open to customers.
offenses.notes: Street "takeovers" and reckless driving exhibitions may also be charged under PC 42.03 (Class A or state jail felony).
aliases: Wilful or wanton disregard for the safety of person or property

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine up to $200 and/or up to 30 days jail

offenses.heading: RECKLESS DRIVING; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Moving a Parked Vehicle
offenses.summary: A driver may not start moving a stopped, standing, or parked vehicle unless it can be done safely.
aliases: Unsafe Start from Parked, Stopped or Standing Position

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: MOVING A PARKED VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving Through Safety Zone
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive through or in a safety zone.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING THROUGH SAFETY ZONE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Unattended Motor Vehicle
offenses.summary: A driver may not leave a vehicle unattended without stopping the engine, locking the ignition, removing the key, setting the parking brake, and, on a grade, turning the front wheels to the curb (remote-start vehicles that need the key present to drive are excepted from the first three).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: UNATTENDED MOTOR VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Driving on Mountain Highway
offenses.summary: A driver going through a defile, canyon, or on a mountain highway must keep the vehicle under control and as near the right edge as possible, and must sound the horn when approaching a curve that blocks the view for 200 feet.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVING ON MOUNTAIN HIGHWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Coasting
offenses.summary: A driver going downhill may not coast in neutral; a truck, tractor, or bus driver going downhill may not coast with the clutch disengaged.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: COASTING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Following or Obstructing Fire Apparatus or Ambulance
offenses.summary: Unless on official business, a driver may not follow within 500 feet of a fire apparatus responding to an alarm or an ambulance flashing red lights, or drive or park in the block where fire apparatus has stopped at an alarm; and may not drive or park so as to interfere with an ambulance summoned to an emergency.
aliases: May not follow closer than 500 feet responding to alarm

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: FOLLOWING OR OBSTRUCTING FIRE APPARATUS OR AMBULANCE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Crossing Fire Hose
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive over an unprotected fire hose on a street or driveway intended for use at a fire without the fire commander's consent.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: CROSSING FIRE HOSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Drawbars and Trailer Hitches; Saddle-Mount Towing
offenses.summary: A towing connection must be strong enough for the load and no more than 15 feet long (except for poles, pipe, and similar loads); a chain, rope, or cable connection must display a white flag at least 12 inches square; and no more than three vehicles may be towed by triple saddle-mount.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRAWBARS AND TRAILER HITCHES; SADDLE-MOUNT TOWING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Towing Safety Chains
offenses.summary: A passenger car or light truck may not tow a trailer, semitrailer, house trailer, or another motor vehicle without approved safety chains properly attached (agricultural trailers and federally regulated motor carriers excepted).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TOWING SAFETY CHAINS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Use of Rest Area
offenses.summary: Stays at a TxDOT rest area, picnic area, roadside park, or scenic overlook longer than 24 hours, or puts up a tent or structure there, after notice by posted sign, or fails to leave or remove it within eight hours after a peace officer orally gives notice.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: USE OF REST AREA: OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Child Passenger Safety Seat
offenses.summary: Drives a passenger vehicle (car, light truck, SUV, van for 15 or fewer, truck) transporting a child younger than 8, unless the child is taller than 4 feet 9 inches, without keeping the child secured in a child safety seat according to the manufacturer's instructions.
offenses.notes: Defense: emergency or law enforcement purpose. Does not apply to vehicles carrying passengers for hire, or when all seating positions with seat belts or safety seats are occupied. A first-time defendant who was not cited for anything else, had no seat, and was not in a collision can have the charge dismissed by later getting an appropriate seat (545.4121).
offenses.heading: CHILD PASSENGER SAFETY SEAT SYSTEMS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Seat Belt Violations
offenses.summary: A person 15 or older riding in any seat with a seat belt in a moving passenger vehicle is not secured by the belt, or a school bus driver is not belted (a); a driver allows a child under 17 (who is not required to be in a child seat) to ride unbelted in a seat with a belt (b), or in a passenger van seating 15 or fewer (b-1).
offenses.notes: Defenses include a physician's written statement of a medical reason, and certain postal, newspaper, utility meter, farm, and waste-collection duties requiring frequent entry and exit.
aliases: Child (15-17years of age) Not Secured By Safety Belt (Front Passenger)

tiers.when: Person 15 or older not wearing a belt (a)
Driver allowing an unbelted child under 17 (b)

offenses.heading: SAFETY BELTS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Child Riding in Open Bed
offenses.summary: Drives an open-bed pickup or open flatbed truck, or tows an open flatbed trailer, while a child younger than 18 is in the bed.
offenses.notes: Defenses: parade or emergency; moving farmworkers between fields on rural roads; on a beach; the household's only vehicle; or a permitted hayride.
aliases: Operate Vehicle with <18years of age in Open Bed
offenses.heading: RIDING IN OPEN BEDS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Riding in or on Boat or Personal Watercraft Drawn by Vehicle
offenses.summary: Drives a motor vehicle on a highway or street while a child younger than 18 is in a boat or personal watercraft being towed by it (defenses: parade, emergency, or on a beach).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: RIDING IN OR ON BOAT OR PERSONAL WATERCRAFT DRAWN BY VEHICLE; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Backing a Vehicle
offenses.summary: A driver may not back a vehicle unless it can be done safely without interfering with other traffic, and may not back on the shoulder or roadway of a freeway (limited-access or controlled-access highway).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: BACKING A VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Riding on Motorcycle or Moped
offenses.summary: A motorcycle or moped rider must sit on the permanent seat; may carry a passenger only if the motorcycle is designed for two and has passenger footrests and handholds, with the passenger on a proper seat; and may not carry a passenger younger than 5 (except in a sidecar).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)
Carrying a passenger younger than 5 (not in a sidecar)

offenses.heading: RIDING ON MOTORCYCLE OR MOPED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Certain Motorcycles
offenses.summary: A person may not operate an enclosed-cab, three-wheeled motorcycle of the type described in 521.001(a)(6-a)(C)(vii) on a highway with a posted speed limit over 45 mph (except to cross it at an intersection).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF CERTAIN MOTORCYCLES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Obstruction of Operator's View or Driving Mechanism
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive when the load or more than three people in the front seat obstruct the driver's front or side view or interfere with control; a passenger may not ride in a position that does so.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OBSTRUCTION OF OPERATOR'S VIEW OR DRIVING MECHANISM

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Opening Vehicle Doors
offenses.summary: A person may not open a vehicle door on the traffic side unless it can be done safely without interfering with traffic, or leave it open longer than needed to load or unload a passenger.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPENING VEHICLE DOORS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Riding in House Trailer
offenses.summary: A person may not ride in a house trailer while it is being moved.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: RIDING IN HOUSE TRAILER

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Person Riding in Trailer or Semitrailer Drawn by Truck, Road Tractor, or Truck Tractor
offenses.summary: Drives a truck, road tractor, or truck tractor while a person is riding in the trailer or semitrailer it is towing.
offenses.notes: Defenses: parade, emergency, moving farmworkers, permitted hayride, the driver did not know, or the person was in a part of the trailer designed for living.
offenses.heading: PERSON RIDING IN TRAILER OR SEMITRAILER DRAWN BY TRUCK, ROAD TRACTOR, OR TRUCK TRACTOR

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Racing on Highway
offenses.summary: Participates in any manner in a race, speed competition or contest, drag race or acceleration contest, endurance test, or exhibition of speed or acceleration (or attempt at a speed record) on a highway.
offenses.notes: The officer must have the vehicle towed to a licensed storage facility (or held as evidence), and the owner must pay the fees before release (subsection (i)). Participation in racing is also a predicate for organized criminal activity (PC 71.02).
aliases: Person may not participate in a vehicle race

tiers.when: One prior conviction under this section
Driver was intoxicated or had an open container
Two prior convictions under this section
An individual suffered bodily injury as a result
An individual suffered serious bodily injury or death as a result

offenses.heading: RACING ON HIGHWAY; IMPOUNDMENT OF A VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Interference with Peace Officer Investigation of Highway Racing or Reckless Driving Exhibition
offenses.summary: Uses the person's body, a car, or a barricade to knowingly impede or interfere with a peace officer's investigation of street racing or a reckless driving exhibition.
offenses.heading: INTERFERENCE WITH PEACE OFFICER INVESTIGATION OF HIGHWAY RACING OR RECKLESS DRIVING EXHIBITION; CRIMINAL OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude Police Officer
offenses.summary: Willfully fails or refuses to stop, flees, or attempts to elude a pursuing police vehicle after a visual or audible signal to stop. The officer must be in uniform with a prominently displayed badge, and the vehicle must bear law enforcement insignia; the signal may be by hand, voice, light, or siren.
offenses.notes: Intentionally fleeing an officer known to be attempting a lawful arrest or detention in a vehicle is usually charged as evading arrest (PC 38.04), a felony.
aliases: Operating a motor vehicle and willfully fails to stop or flees.

tiers.when: Recklessly places another in imminent danger of serious bodily injury (presumed if the driver was intoxicated)

offenses.heading: FLEEING OR ATTEMPTING TO ELUDE POLICE OFFICER; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Crossing Sidewalk or Hike and Bike Trail
offenses.summary: A person may not drive a motor vehicle on a sidewalk, sidewalk area, or hike and bike trail except on a permanent or authorized temporary driveway (trail maintenance excepted).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: CROSSING SIDEWALK OR HIKE AND BIKE TRAIL

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Crossing Property
offenses.summary: A driver may not cross a sidewalk or drive through a driveway, parking lot, or business or residential entrance without stopping, and may not cut through a sidewalk, driveway, parking lot, or entrance at an intersection to turn from one highway onto another.
aliases: Cut Across Driveway to Make Turn

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: CROSSING PROPERTY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Restrictions on Drivers Under 18
offenses.summary: A driver under 18 may not use a wireless communication device (handheld or hands-free) while driving except in an emergency. A driver under 18 also may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. (unless for work, a school-related activity, or a medical emergency) or with more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member, unless accompanied as required for a learner license. A moped may be driven at night within sight of a parent. Similar limits apply to restricted motorcycle licenses under 17 during the first 12 months.
offenses.notes: A peace officer may not stop a vehicle or detain a driver solely to check for a violation of this section (subsection (e)).
aliases: Operation of Vehicle by Person Under 18 Years of Age

tiers.when: Phone use, with a prior conviction
General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE BY PERSON UNDER 18 YEARS OF AGE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Wireless Device Use in School Crossing Zone or Bus With Minor
offenses.summary: A driver may not use a wireless communication device while driving through a school crossing zone unless stopped or using a hands-free device; and a school bus or passenger bus driver may not use one while a minor passenger is aboard unless the bus is stopped (two-way-radio-style use for driving duties excepted).
offenses.notes: Affirmative defenses: an emergency call, or the required school zone sign was not posted (unless the city has a citywide ban with signs at its limits).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: USE OF WIRELESS COMMUNICATION DEVICE IN A SCHOOL CROSSING ZONE OR WHILE OPERATING A BUS WITH A MINOR PASSENGER; LOCAL AUTHORITY SIGN REQUIREMENTS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Texting While Driving (Electronic Messaging)
offenses.summary: Uses a portable wireless device to read, write, or send an electronic message while operating a motor vehicle unless the vehicle is stopped. The conduct must occur in the presence or view of a peace officer or be proved by other evidence.
offenses.notes: Affirmative defenses: hands-free use, GPS navigation, reporting crime or emergencies or using a traffic app, reading a message reasonably believed to be an emergency, a device affixed to the vehicle for work dispatch, or playing music. An officer may not take or inspect the phone unless otherwise authorized by law (subsection (i)). This section preempts local texting ordinances.
aliases: Use of Portable Wireless Communication Device for Electronic Messaging

tiers.when: Caused the death or serious bodily injury of another person
tiers.extra: Fine up to $4,000; up to 1 year jail

offenses.heading: USE OF PORTABLE WIRELESS COMMUNICATION DEVICE FOR ELECTRONIC MESSAGING; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Use of Wireless Communication Device on School Property
offenses.summary: A driver may not use a wireless communication device on the property of a public elementary, middle, junior high, or high school with a designated school crossing zone while the reduced school speed limit is in effect, unless stopped or using a hands-free device.
offenses.notes: Affirmative defense: an emergency call to police, fire, EMS, a hospital, clinic, doctor, or someone giving first aid.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: USE OF WIRELESS COMMUNICATION DEVICE ON SCHOOL PROPERTY; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of School Bus
offenses.summary: A person may not drive a school bus with the door open or with more passengers than its design capacity, and the driver must not let passengers stand, sit on the floor, or sit anywhere not designed as a seat.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF SCHOOL BUS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Vehicle with Insufficient Undercarriage Clearance
offenses.summary: A driver may not drive on or across a railroad grade crossing unless the vehicle has sufficient undercarriage clearance.
offenses.heading: OPERATION OF VEHICLE WITH INSUFFICIENT UNDERCARRIAGE CLEARANCE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Collision With Pedestrian or Vulnerable Road User in Crosswalk
offenses.summary: With criminal negligence, operates a motor vehicle within the area of a crosswalk and causes bodily injury to a pedestrian or a person on a bicycle, motor-assisted scooter, electric personal assistive mobility device, neighborhood electric vehicle, or golf cart.
offenses.notes: Affirmative defense: the injured person was violating a rule about walking or operating in the crosswalk or roadway. Added in 2023.
aliases: Motor Vehicle Accident Involving Pedestrian or Other Vulnerable Road User Within Area of Crosswalk
offenses.heading: MOTOR VEHICLE COLLISION INVOLVING PEDESTRIAN OR OTHER VULNERABLE ROAD USER WITHIN AREA OF CROSSWALK; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Miniature Vehicle
offenses.summary: A miniature vehicle (as defined in 502.001) may be operated on a public highway only if it is registered and titled and is capable of complying with traffic laws.
offenses.notes: Added in 2025.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MINIATURE VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 545 Operation and Movement of Vehicles
offenses.name: Automated Motor Vehicle Operation
offenses.summary: Operates an automated (self-driving, Level 4 or 5) motor vehicle to carry property or passengers commercially without a human driver, without Texas DMV authorization and an emergency-interaction plan filed with DPS. Each day is a separate offense.
offenses.notes: When an automated driving system is engaged it is the "operator," and citations go to the owner or authorization holder (545.454). Rewritten in 2025.
offenses.heading: AUTOMATED MOTOR VEHICLE OPERATION; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Vehicle Equipment Violations (General Offense)
offenses.summary: Operates or moves, or as the owner knowingly permits another to operate or move, a vehicle that is unsafe so as to endanger a person, is not equipped as Chapter 547 requires, or is equipped in a way the chapter prohibits; or knowingly operates a vehicle with equipment found noncompliant in a DPS compliance proceeding.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
offenses.heading: GENERAL OFFENSES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Offense Relating to Violation of Special-Use Provisions
offenses.summary: Uses a slow-moving-vehicle emblem on anything other than a slow-moving vehicle, or operates a vehicle marked "school bus" that is not used primarily to transport students to or from school or school activities.
offenses.heading: OFFENSE RELATING TO VIOLATION OF SPECIAL-USE PROVISIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Duty to Display Lights (No Headlights)
offenses.summary: Required lamps must be lit at night and whenever visibility is too poor to see a person or vehicle 1,000 feet ahead; at least one lighted lamp must show on each side of the front; and no more than four headlamps or bright auxiliary lamps may be lit on the front at once.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Drove Without Lights - When Required (1000ft visibility)
More Than 4 Driving Lamps Lighted (must be less than 300 candlepower)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: DUTY TO DISPLAY LIGHTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Color Requirements
offenses.summary: Rear lighting devices and reflectors must be red; rear signal devices may be red, amber, or yellow (unless the chapter provides otherwise).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Wrong Color Signal Device (must be red, amber, yellow)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: COLOR REQUIREMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Restrictions on Use of Lights (Red, Blue, Flashing Lights)
offenses.summary: Lights brighter than 300 candlepower (other than headlamps, spotlamps, and similar) must be aimed so the bright beam hits the road within 75 feet. Only police vehicles may display a red light visible from directly in front. No vehicle may have red, white, or blue beacon, flashing, or alternating lights unless specifically authorized. Alternately flashing warning lights are allowed only on school buses, emergency vehicles, marked church buses, and tow trucks under the stated conditions. Security patrol vehicles may use only green, amber, or white lights. A lamp counts as "equipped" even if temporary or not turned on.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Improper Use of Lighting - hwy. equip. (red/white/blue alternating)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: RESTRICTIONS ON USE OF LIGHTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Led Ground Effect Lighting Equipment on Motorcycle or Moped
offenses.summary: A motorcycle or moped with LED underglow (ground effect) lighting may display only a non-flashing amber or white light.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Must be non-flashing amber, or white light

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: LED GROUND EFFECT LIGHTING EQUIPMENT ON MOTORCYCLE OR MOPED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Headlamps Required
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle must have at least two headlamps, at least one on each side of the front, mounted 24 to 54 inches high.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: HEADLAMPS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Taillamps and License Plate Light Required
offenses.summary: Most vehicles must have at least two red taillamps (one on pre-1960 cars) mounted 15 to 72 inches high, visible 1,000 feet to the rear, plus a white light that makes the rear license plate legible from 50 feet. Taillamps and the plate lamp must be on whenever headlamps are on.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: TAILLAMPS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
