offenses.name: Stoplamps Required
offenses.summary: Most vehicles must have at least two stoplamps (one on pre-1960 cars) on the rear, emitting red or amber light visible 300 feet away in sunlight when the brakes are applied. A high-mounted stoplamp counts toward compliance under 547.3215.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles). Last amended 2025.

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: STOPLAMPS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Turn Signal Lamps Required
offenses.summary: Motor vehicles and trailers must have electric turn signal lamps flashing to the front and rear on the side of the turn (white or amber in front, red or amber in back), except some pre-1960 vehicles under 80 inches wide.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: TURN SIGNAL LAMPS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Reflectors Required
offenses.summary: Motor vehicles and trailers must have at least two red rear reflectors, 15 to 60 inches high, visible at night from 100 to 600 feet in low-beam headlights.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: REFLECTORS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Spotlamps Permitted
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle may have no more than two spotlamps, aimed so the bright beam does not hit the windshield, windows, mirrors, or occupants of another vehicle.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: SPOTLAMPS PERMITTED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Fog Lamps Permitted
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle may have no more than two fog lamps, mounted 12 to 30 inches high on the front and aimed low as specified.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: FOG LAMPS PERMITTED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Auxiliary Passing Lamps Permitted
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle may have no more than two auxiliary passing lamps, mounted 24 to 42 inches high on the front.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Improper Use of Auxiliary Passing Lamps

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: AUXILIARY PASSING LAMPS PERMITTED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Auxiliary Driving Lamps Permitted
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle may have no more than two auxiliary driving lamps, mounted 16 to 42 inches high on the front.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Improper Use of Auxiliary Driving Lamps

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: AUXILIARY DRIVING LAMPS PERMITTED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Other Lamps Permitted
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle may also have up to two side cowl or fender lamps and up to two running-board courtesy lamps (amber or white, without glare), and backup lamps (amber or white, lit only when not moving forward).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: OTHER LAMPS PERMITTED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Multiple-Beam Headlamps Required
offenses.summary: Headlamps (except on motorcycles and mopeds) must have high and low beams the driver can select. High beam must reveal a person or vehicle 450 feet ahead; low beam 150 feet ahead, aimed to avoid glare.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: MULTIPLE-BEAM LIGHTING EQUIPMENT REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Additional Lighting Equipment Requirements
offenses.summary: Buses, trucks, and trailers 80 inches wide or more need front and rear clearance lamps, side marker lamps, reflectors, and hazard lamps; buses and trucks 30 feet or longer need hazard lamps; and long trailers need additional side markers and reflectors.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Reflector(s) on Side-At or Near Front, Rear, Centrally (specify)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL LIGHTING EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Color Requirements
offenses.summary: Clearance, identification, and side marker lamps and reflectors on the front, front sides, or center must be amber; those on the rear or rear sides must be red.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: COLOR REQUIREMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Mounting Requirements
offenses.summary: Sets mounting heights and positions for reflectors (24 to 60 inches) and clearance lamps on large vehicles.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: MOUNTING REQUIREMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Visibility Requirements
offenses.summary: Clearance, identification, and side marker lamps on large vehicles must be visible from 50 to 500 feet, and reflectors from 100 to 600 feet at night in headlights.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Clearance Lights Not Visible Sufficient Distance
Identification Lamps Not Visible Sufficient Distance
Side Marker Lamps Not Visible Sufficient Distance

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: VISIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Lighting or Flags on Projecting Loads
offenses.summary: A load extending at least 4 feet beyond the rear of the bed must display at night two red lamps visible 500 feet to the rear, two red reflectors marking its width, and two red side lamps marking the overhang; at other times, red flags at least 12 inches square must mark the extremities of any load extending beyond the sides or more than 4 feet to the rear.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Lamps (or Reflectors) on Projecting Load at Night

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: LIGHTING EQUIPMENT ON PROJECTING LOADS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Lighting Requirements on Parked Vehicles
offenses.summary: A vehicle (other than a small motorcycle or moped) parked or stopped on a roadway or shoulder at night must display a lamp showing white or amber 1,000 feet to the front and red 1,000 feet to the rear on the traffic side, unless lawfully parked where there is enough light to see 1,000 feet. Headlamps on a parked vehicle must be dimmed.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Parked With Head Lamps Not Dimmed

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: LIGHTING REQUIREMENTS ON PARKED VEHICLES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Brakes Required
offenses.summary: Motor vehicles, trailers, and combinations must have brakes complying with the chapter; trailers 4,500 pounds or less (or up to 15,000 pounds drawn at 30 mph or less) do not need brakes.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Brakes Not Maintained In Good Working Order
Brakes Not on All Wheels When Required
No Automatic Brake Application on Breakaway Trailer

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: BRAKES REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Operation and Maintenance of Brakes
offenses.summary: Required brakes must operate on every wheel, with listed exceptions (special mobile equipment, vehicles towed as commodities, some trailers and multi-axle trucks), and must be maintained in good working order.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Single Control to Operate All Brakes

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF BRAKES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Parking Brakes Required
offenses.summary: Vehicles required to have brakes (other than motorcycles and mopeds) must have parking brakes that hold the vehicle on any grade and load and keep working despite power loss.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Parking Brakes (or Defective Parking Brakes

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: PARKING BRAKES REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Emergency Brakes Required
offenses.summary: A vehicle towing a vehicle with air or vacuum brakes must have the required emergency means of applying the towed vehicle's brakes.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Emergency Brake Operation (Air or Vacuum Brakes)
Tractor Brakes Not Protected (in Case of Breakaway)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: EMERGENCY BRAKES REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Brake Reservoir or Reserve Capacity Required
offenses.summary: Air-braked buses, trucks, and truck-tractors must have an adequate air reservoir with a drain; vacuum-braked trucks must have adequate reserve capacity; and trailers with air or vacuum brakes must have their own reservoir.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Inadequate Reservoir Safeguard (Air or Vacuum Brakes Specify)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: BRAKE RESERVOIR OR RESERVE CAPACITY REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Brake Warning Devices Required
offenses.summary: Air-braked buses, trucks, and truck-tractors must have a low-air-pressure warning and a pressure gauge visible to the driver; vacuum-braked vehicles must have a low-vacuum warning.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: No Warning Devices on Brakes Other Than Gauges (Air/Vacuum)
No Warning Signal or Defective Warning Signal for Air Brakes
No Warning Signal or Defective Warning Signal for Vacuum Brakes

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: BRAKE WARNING DEVICES REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Brake Performance Requirements
offenses.summary: Service brakes must meet stopping standards: for example, a passenger vehicle must stop from 20 mph within 25 feet; motorcycles and light single-unit vehicles within 30 feet; heavier vehicles within 40 to 50 feet.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS FOR BRAKES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Horn Required; Sirens Prohibited
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle must have a working horn audible at 200 feet, used only when necessary for safety; no vehicle may have or use a siren, whistle, or bell unless it is an authorized emergency vehicle (or a commercial vehicle theft alarm); and no warning device may be unreasonably loud or harsh.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Unauthorized Use of Siren, Bell, or Whistle

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: AUDIBLE WARNING DEVICES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Visible Warning Devices Required
offenses.summary: Trucks, buses, truck-tractors, and vehicles towing house trailers outside urban districts or on divided highways must carry two red flags (day) and three flares, fusees, red lanterns, or reflective triangles (night); explosive cargo vehicles may not carry flame devices.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Warning Devices Not Installed, or Defective

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: VISIBLE WARNING DEVICES REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Display of Hazard Lamps
offenses.summary: A truck, bus, truck-tractor, or trailer at least 80 inches wide or 30 feet long that stops on a roadway or shoulder must immediately turn on its hazard lamps, unless lawfully parked in an urban district, stopping for passengers, avoiding traffic, obeying an officer or device, or displaying other required warning devices.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Warning Devices Not Displayed (Flags, Fuses, Flares, Reflectors)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: DISPLAY OF HAZARD LAMPS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Offense Relating to Warning Devices
offenses.summary: Removes, damages, destroys, misplaces, or extinguishes a required warning device (flags, flares, reflectors) while it is being displayed as required (the vehicle owner, their agent, and peace officers excepted).
offenses.heading: OFFENSE RELATING TO WARNING DEVICES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Safety Belts Required
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle must have front seat belts if belt anchorages were original equipment (or if an assembled vehicle has anchorages).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Safety belt removed from original manufacture requirements

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: SAFETY BELTS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Mirrors Required
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle (including one towing another vehicle) must have a mirror that gives the driver a view of the highway at least 200 feet to the rear.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: MIRRORS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Windshield Wipers Required
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle must have working windshield wipers controlled by the driver.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: WINDSHIELD WIPERS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Muffler Required / Excessive Noise
offenses.summary: A motor vehicle must have a muffler in good working condition that prevents excessive or unusual noise; muffler cutouts and bypasses are prohibited.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: MUFFLER REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Emission Systems Required
offenses.summary: A vehicle's engine must be equipped and adjusted to prevent excessive smoke or fumes; post-1967 vehicles must have crankcase emission controls and maintain and use their exhaust emission systems (which may not be removed or disabled). Operating, or knowingly permitting operation of, a vehicle that emits visible smoke for 10 seconds or longer (or smoke that hangs in the air 10 seconds or longer) is an offense, except when downshifting is needed to keep momentum.
aliases: Removed Original Equipment Exhaust Emission System
offenses.heading: EMISSION SYSTEMS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Safety Guards or Flaps Required
offenses.summary: Road tractors, trucks, trailers, and truck-tractor and semitrailer combinations with at least four tires (or two super singles) on the rearmost axle must have mud flaps hanging behind the rear wheels within 8 inches of the road (not truck-tractors alone or pole trailers).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: SAFETY GUARDS OR FLAPS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Fire Extinguisher Required
offenses.summary: A school bus or a vehicle carrying passengers for hire must carry at least a one-quart chemical fire extinguisher in good condition, ready for use.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: FIRE EXTINGUISHER REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Safety Glazing Material Required
offenses.summary: New passenger vehicles (including buses) must have approved safety glass in doors, windows, and windshields; replacement glass must be safety glazing; and campers made after 1972 must have safety glazing.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: SAFETY GLAZING MATERIAL REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Use of Certain Video Equipment and Television Receivers
offenses.summary: A video screen (TV, DVD, or similar) may not be visible from the driver's seat unless the vehicle is in park or the parking brake is set (exceptions include navigation, safety, and law enforcement equipment).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: USE OF CERTAIN VIDEO EQUIPMENT AND TELEVISION RECEIVERS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Restrictions on Use and Sale of Tires
offenses.summary: Tire restrictions: solid rubber tires need rubber above the flange; metal tires may not touch the road (small farm wagons excepted); studs, cleats, or spikes that project beyond the tread are prohibited unless they do not damage the road or are reasonable tire chains used for safety. Selling or offering for sale a regrooved passenger car tire is a separate offense (e).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way
Selling or offering a regrooved passenger car tire

offenses.heading: RESTRICTIONS ON USE AND SALE OF TIRES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Window Tint and Obstructed View
offenses.summary: Operates a motor vehicle with an object or material on the windshield or side or rear windows that obstructs or reduces the driver's clear view, or places tint or other color-altering material on them, unless allowed by the exceptions. Main exceptions: a windshield strip above the AS-1 line or within 5 inches of the top (25% light transmission or more, 25% reflectance or less, not red, blue, or amber); front side windows and wing vents with tint that, combined with the glass, lets through 25% of light or more with 25% reflectance or less; side windows behind the driver (any tint); the rear window if the vehicle has outside mirrors on both sides; factory or manufacturer-spec glass; out-of-state vehicles; required stickers; vehicles for hire; law enforcement vehicles; and commercial motor vehicles.
offenses.notes: Defense: the driver or a passenger must be shielded from the sun for a medical reason (subsection (e)). DPS allows a 3% tolerance on the 25% standard. A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Affix Color/Light Altering Material to Windshield/Window

tiers.when: Driver: obstructed view or illegal tint (a)
Tint business installing tint without the required label (547.609)

offenses.heading: RESTRICTIONS ON WINDOWS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Restrictions on Airbags
offenses.summary: Knowingly installs (or claims to install) an airbag but installs none or a counterfeit one; makes or sells a counterfeit airbag; alters an airbag so it no longer meets federal standards; represents a counterfeit airbag as genuine; or causes or helps another to do so.
aliases: Airbags - Make/Sell Counterfeit IN ALT Result Death
Airbags - Make/Sell Counterfeit INT ALT PREV CONV
Airbags - Make/Sell counterfeit INT ALT Result BI

tiers.when: An individual suffered bodily injury as a result
The offense resulted in a death

offenses.heading: RESTRICTIONS ON AIRBAGS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Radar Interference Devices
offenses.summary: Uses, attempts to use, installs, or operates a radar or laser jamming device in a motor vehicle the person drives (police on duty excepted), or buys, sells, or offers one for that use. Ham and CB radios are not included.
offenses.heading: RADAR INTERFERENCE DEVICES; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Motorcycle and Moped Footrests and Handholds Required
offenses.summary: A motorcycle or moped designed for a passenger must have passenger footrests and handholds (autocycles excepted).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: MOTORCYCLE AND MOPED FOOTRESTS AND HANDHOLDS REQUIRED

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Additional Equipment Requirements for School Buses and Other Buses Used to Transport Schoolchildren
offenses.summary: A school bus must have a convex front mirror and four alternately flashing red warning lamps visible 500 feet in sunlight, and may have rooftop warning lamps, stop arms, and other listed equipment. Last amended 2025.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Bus Driver Failed to Activate Warning Signal/Equipment
Bus Not Equipped With Convex Mirrors

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR SCHOOL BUSES AND OTHER BUSES USED TO TRANSPORT SCHOOLCHILDREN

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Additional Equipment Requirements for Other Buses
offenses.summary: A public transit bus acquired after September 1, 1997, must have rear flashing amber hazard lamps (used when unloading anyone under 18) and a rear sign reading "Caution--children may be exiting."
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR OTHER BUSES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Additional Equipment Requirements for Slow-Moving Vehicles
offenses.summary: A slow-moving vehicle (25 mph or less) must display a clean, reflective slow-moving-vehicle emblem on the rear, base down (except in marked construction zones).
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Emblem Not In Clean (or Reflective) Condition

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR SLOW-MOVING VEHICLES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Lighting Equipment
offenses.summary: A motorcycle or moped must have one or two headlamps (24 to 54 inches high), at least one taillamp, a license plate lamp, a stoplamp, and a rear red reflector; motorcycles over 250 cc need high and low beams.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).
aliases: Defective Head Lamp on Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle)
No Head Lamp(s) on Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle)
No or Defective Multiple-Beam Road lighting Equipment on Motorcycle
No Reflector(s) on Rear of Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle)
No Stop Lamp on Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle
Tail Lamp Improperly Located on Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle
Tail Lamp Improperly Located on Motorcycle (or Motor-Driven Cycle)

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: LIGHTING EQUIPMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Brake Equipment
offenses.summary: Motorcycle and moped brake rules: sidecar wheels and (for mopeds and motorcycles of 250 cc or less) front wheels need no brakes if the vehicle meets the stopping standards of 547.408.
offenses.notes: A court may dismiss the charge if the defect is fixed before the first court appearance and a reimbursement fee of up to $10 is paid (547.004(c); not for commercial motor vehicles).

tiers.when: Operating a vehicle not equipped as required, or equipped in a prohibited way

offenses.heading: BRAKE EQUIPMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Offense Generally
offenses.summary: Inspection fraud by an inspector, station, or other person: submitting or issuing an inspection report in violation of the rules or without inspecting the vehicle; passing a vehicle that was not repaired or is missing required items; falsely telling an owner repairs are needed; misrepresenting application information; refusing to let the owner choose who repairs; overcharging; or selling customer information.
offenses.notes: A TxDMV/DPS designated representative may also issue a notice to appear (subsection (c)).

tiers.when: All cases, unless the chapter specifies otherwise

offenses.heading: OFFENSE GENERALLY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Fictitious or Counterfeit Inspection Report or Insurance Document
offenses.summary: Presents to a government official an inspection report or insurance document the person knows is counterfeit, altered, fictitious, issued for another vehicle, or improperly issued, or knowingly fails to comply with an emissions inspection requirement (a); makes or possesses for sale a counterfeit inspection report or insurance document, or the equipment to make one (b); or, as owner, knowingly allows the vehicle to be registered with an improper inspection report (c).

tiers.when: Presenting a counterfeit or improper document, or not complying with emissions requirements (a), or owner allowing improper registration (c)
Making or possessing counterfeit documents for sale, or the equipment to make them (b)
Same (b), with intent to defraud or harm another
Presenting a fictitious vehicle inspection report (a)(1)

offenses.heading: FICTITIOUS OR COUNTERFEIT INSPECTION CERTIFICATE OR INSURANCE DOCUMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Penalty for Certain Violations
offenses.summary: Operates or moves a motor vehicle, trailer, semitrailer, pole trailer, or mobile home equipped in violation of the inspection chapter or its rules.
offenses.heading: PENALTY FOR CERTAIN VIOLATIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Operating a Vehicle without Complying with Inspection Requirements as Certified; Offense; Dismissal of Charge
offenses.summary: Operates a vehicle registered with a certification that it would meet inspection requirements (548.256(b)) when it does not comply with the applicable inspection requirements (commercial safety inspection or emissions testing). An officer may require the inspection report if the registration record flags the vehicle for verification.
offenses.notes: Defense: a passing inspection report was in effect. The court must dismiss if the defect is fixed within 20 working days of the citation (or before the first court date) and within 40 working days of the deadline, with a fee of up to $20. Safety inspections for non-commercial vehicles were eliminated January 1, 2025 (H.B. 3297, 2023); emissions testing still applies in designated counties, including El Paso County.
offenses.heading: OPERATING A VEHICLE WITHOUT COMPLYING WITH INSPECTION REQUIREMENTS AS CERTIFIED; OFFENSE; DISMISSAL OF CHARGE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Stop and Render Aid (Collision Involving Injury or Death)
offenses.summary: The driver of a vehicle involved in a collision that results, or is reasonably likely to result, in injury or death fails to immediately stop at or as close as possible to the scene (or immediately return to it), determine whether anyone is involved and needs aid, and remain until complying with 550.023 (give name, address, registration, and insurer; show license on request; and give reasonable assistance, including arranging transport to medical care).
offenses.notes: Applies on highways and other public places, and on business parking lots and access ways open to customers (not private residential property or pay parking lots) (550.001). Knowledge that a collision occurred is generally required; confirm proof issues with your prosecutor.
terms: fail to stop and render aid

tiers.when: Collision resulted in serious bodily injury

tiers.level: Up to 5 years TDCJ or up to 1 year county jail, and/or fine up to $5,000

offenses.heading: COLLISION INVOLVING PERSONAL INJURY OR DEATH

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Stop and Give Information (Collision Damaging Attended Vehicle)
offenses.summary: The driver of a vehicle in a collision that damages only a vehicle that is driven or attended fails to immediately stop at or near the scene without obstructing traffic more than necessary (or return to it) and remain until complying with 550.023. On a metropolitan freeway, if every vehicle can be normally and safely driven, each driver must move to a safe location off the main lanes to exchange information (b).
offenses.notes: Applies on highways and other public places, and on business parking lots and access ways open to customers (not private residential property or pay parking lots) (550.001).
terms: fail to stop and give information

tiers.when: Damage to all vehicles less than $200
Damage to all vehicles $200 or more
Failing to move drivable vehicles off a metropolitan freeway (b)

offenses.heading: COLLISION INVOLVING DAMAGE TO VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Duty to Give Information and Render Aid
offenses.summary: Not a separate charge (failing to comply is punished under 550.021 or 550.022). After a collision with injury, death, or damage to an attended vehicle, the driver must give their name and address, the vehicle's registration number, and their liability insurer to anyone injured and to the other drivers, occupants, or attendants; show their driver's license if requested and available; and give injured persons reasonable assistance, including transporting or arranging transport to a doctor or hospital if treatment is apparently needed or requested.
offenses.heading: DUTY TO GIVE INFORMATION AND RENDER AID

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Notify Owner of Unattended Vehicle (Striking Unattended Vehicle)
offenses.summary: A driver who collides with and damages an unattended vehicle fails to immediately stop and either locate the owner or operator and give the striking driver's and owner's names and addresses, or leave a conspicuous written note with that information and a statement of the circumstances.
offenses.notes: Applies on highways and other public places, and on business parking lots and access ways open to customers (not private residential property or pay parking lots) (550.001).

tiers.when: Damage to all vehicles less than $200
Damage to all vehicles $200 or more

offenses.heading: DUTY ON STRIKING UNATTENDED VEHICLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Failure to Report Striking Structure, Fixture, or Landscaping
offenses.summary: A driver in a collision damaging only a structure next to a highway, or a fixture or landscaping legally on or next to it, fails to take reasonable steps to locate and notify the owner of the collision, the driver's name and address, and the vehicle registration number, or fails to show their license on request.

tiers.when: Damage to all fixtures and landscaping less than $200

offenses.heading: DUTY ON STRIKING STRUCTURE, FIXTURE, OR HIGHWAY LANDSCAPING

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Immediate Report of Collision
offenses.summary: The driver in a collision causing injury, death, or damage making a vehicle unable to be normally and safely driven fails to immediately report it by the quickest means to the city police (in a city or within 100 feet of one), or otherwise to the sheriff or nearest DPS office.
offenses.heading: IMMEDIATE REPORT OF COLLISION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Peace Officer Investigation of Collisions on Any Property
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A peace officer notified of a collision with injury, death, or apparent property damage of $1,000 or more may investigate and file charges wherever it occurred, except privately owned residential parking areas and pay parking lots.
offenses.heading: INVESTIGATION BY PEACE OFFICER

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.name: Officer's Collision Report (CR-3)
offenses.summary: Not an offense. An officer who investigates a collision resulting in injury, death, or apparent damage to any one person's property of $1,000 or more must make a written report and file it electronically with TxDOT within 10 days. Only the reporting officer may change a material fact in the report, except by a signed written supplement (550.068).
offenses.heading: OFFICER'S COLLISION REPORT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Rights and Duties
offenses.summary: A bicyclist has the same rights and duties as a driver of a vehicle (unless the chapter changes them or they cannot apply to a bicycle). A parent or guardian may not knowingly permit a child or ward to violate the traffic laws. These rules also apply to mopeds and electric bicycles (551.002).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: RIGHTS AND DUTIES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: General Operation
offenses.summary: A bicyclist must ride on a permanent, regular seat; may not carry more people than the bicycle is designed for; may not carry anything that keeps them from having at least one hand on the handlebars; and no one on a bicycle, skates, sled, or toy vehicle may hitch onto a moving vehicle.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: GENERAL OPERATION

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation on Roadway
offenses.summary: A bicyclist moving slower than traffic must ride as near as practicable to the right curb or edge, except when passing, preparing to turn left, avoiding hazards or obstacles, or in an outside lane less than 14 feet wide with no bike lane or too narrow to share safely. On a one-way road with two or more lanes, they may ride near the left edge. Cyclists may ride two abreast in a single lane if they do not impede the normal flow of traffic, but not more than two abreast.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION ON ROADWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Safety Equipment
offenses.summary: A bicycle must have a brake that can skid a wheel on dry pavement. At night it must have a white front lamp visible 500 feet ahead and either an approved red rear reflector (visible 50 to 300 feet in high beams) or a red rear lamp visible 500 feet.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SAFETY EQUIPMENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Regulation of Bicycles by Department or Local Authority
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Electric bicycles may not be banned from highways used mainly by motor vehicles or from places where regular bicycles are allowed (except natural-surface trails). TxDOT or a local authority may prohibit bicycles on sidewalks and set speed limits on bike paths.
offenses.heading: REGULATION OF BICYCLES BY DEPARTMENT OR LOCAL AUTHORITY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation of Electric Bicycle
offenses.summary: An electric bicycle's motor must stop when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes; a person under 15 may not operate (but may ride as a passenger on) a Class 3 electric bicycle (as defined in 664.001). E-bikes are exempt from vehicle registration, licensing, and insurance requirements.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF ELECTRIC BICYCLE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation on Roadway
offenses.summary: A self-balancing electric personal assistive mobility device (such as a Segway) may be used on a street with a speed limit of 30 mph or less only to cross at a crosswalk, where no sidewalk is available, or when directed by a device or officer, riding near the right edge; it may be used on bike paths and sidewalks (551.203). Bicycle rules otherwise apply.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION ON ROADWAY

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation on Roadways
offenses.summary: A neighborhood electric vehicle (low-speed vehicle, top speed 35 mph) may be operated only on streets with a posted limit of 45 mph or less (it may cross faster roads at intersections), and never faster than the posted limit or 35 mph. Local governments and TxDOT may prohibit them for safety.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION ON ROADWAYS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Motor-Assisted Scooter Operation
offenses.summary: A motor-assisted scooter (stand-up or seated scooter with a motor of 40 cc or less, able to be human-powered) may be operated only on streets with a posted limit of 35 mph or less (it may cross faster roads at intersections), and on bike paths and sidewalks, unless a city, county, or TxDOT prohibits it. Bicycle rules apply; motor vehicle rules do not. Pocket bikes and minimotorbikes may not be ridden on any road, bike path, or sidewalk (551.353).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION ON ROADWAYS OR SIDEWALKS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Registration Not Authorized; License Plates
offenses.summary: A golf cart may be operated on a highway (where 551.403 or 551.404 allows it) only if it displays a golf cart license plate issued by TxDMV; golf carts cannot otherwise be registered for highway use. The plate does not expire and does not transfer to a new owner.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: REGISTRATION NOT AUTHORIZED; LICENSE PLATES

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 551 Operation of Bicycles and Mopeds, Golf Carts, and Other Low-Powered Vehicles
offenses.name: Operation Authorized in Certain Areas
offenses.summary: Golf carts may be operated in master planned communities and residential subdivisions with approved plats, on beaches open to vehicles, or on roads with a posted limit of 35 mph or less in the daytime within five miles of where the cart is usually parked, going to or from a golf course. In a qualifying master planned community, no golf cart plate is needed on roads of 35 mph or less (including crossing faster roads at intersections). Cities, and some counties, may allow more (551.404), and must require lamps, reflectors, parking brake, and mirrors (551.4041).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: OPERATION AUTHORIZED IN CERTAIN AREAS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Traffic Control Signals
offenses.summary: A pedestrian or sidewalk user facing a green signal may cross within a crosswalk (unless the only green is a turn arrow); facing a steady red or yellow signal, they may not enter the roadway.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TRAFFIC CONTROL SIGNALS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Pedestrian or Sidewalk User Right-of-Way If Control Signal Present
offenses.summary: At a pedestrian "Walk" signal, pedestrians and sidewalk users may cross and drivers must stop and yield to them. A pedestrian may not start crossing on "Don't Walk" or "Wait"; one already crossing must continue to a sidewalk or safety island.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PEDESTRIAN OR SIDEWALK USER RIGHT-OF-WAY IF CONTROL SIGNAL PRESENT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Failure to Yield to Pedestrian in Crosswalk
offenses.summary: Where no traffic signal is operating, a driver must stop and yield to a pedestrian crossing in a crosswalk who is on the driver's half of the roadway or approaching so closely from the other half as to be in danger. A driver may not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. A pedestrian may not suddenly step into a crosswalk in the path of a vehicle too close to stop.
offenses.notes: Crosswalk injuries caused by criminal negligence may also be charged under 545.428 (Class A or state jail felony).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine up to $500 and 30 hours community service
tiers.when: Failure to yield caused a collision with serious bodily injury or death to a visually impaired or disabled person

offenses.heading: PEDESTRIAN RIGHT-OF-WAY AT CROSSWALK

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Sidewalk User Right-of-Way at Crosswalk
offenses.summary: Where no signal is operating, a driver must stop and yield to a sidewalk user (such as a person on a scooter or mobility device) crossing in a crosswalk on the driver's half or approaching closely. A sidewalk user may not dart into a crosswalk too close to stop, or enter it faster than reasonable (over 8 mph is prima facie unreasonable). Drivers may not pass a vehicle stopped for a sidewalk user.
offenses.notes: Added in 2025 (S.B. 2039), along with 552.0036 (sidewalk users must stop at stop signs before entering crosswalks and yield).

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SIDEWALK USER RIGHT-OF-WAY AT CROSSWALK

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Sidewalk User Right-of-Way at Stop Sign
offenses.summary: A sidewalk user approaching an intersection with a stop sign must stop before entering the crosswalk and then yield to any vehicle in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SIDEWALK USER RIGHT-OF-WAY AT STOP SIGN

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Pedestrian to Keep to Right
offenses.summary: A pedestrian must use the right half of a crosswalk when possible.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: PEDESTRIAN TO KEEP TO RIGHT

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Pedestrian Crossing Outside Crosswalk (Jaywalking)
offenses.summary: A pedestrian crossing a roadway other than in a marked crosswalk or an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, or where a pedestrian tunnel or overpass is provided, must yield to vehicles. Between adjacent intersections with operating traffic signals, a pedestrian may cross only in a marked crosswalk. Diagonal crossing is allowed only where a device authorizes it.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: CROSSING AT POINT OTHER THAN CROSSWALK

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Walking in Roadway Where Sidewalk Provided
offenses.summary: A pedestrian may not walk along and on a roadway if an accessible sidewalk is provided; where there is none, they must walk on the left side or shoulder facing traffic unless it is obstructed or unsafe. A driver entering or leaving an alley, building, or driveway must stop and yield to pedestrians on a sidewalk crossing it.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: USE OF SIDEWALK

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Solicitation by Pedestrian in Roadway
offenses.summary: A person may not stand in a roadway to solicit a ride, contribution, employment, or business from vehicle occupants (charitable solicitation allowed only with local authorization), or stand on or near a highway to solicit watching or guarding of parked vehicles.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: SOLICITATION BY PEDESTRIANS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Drivers to Exercise Due Care
offenses.summary: Every driver must exercise due care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian on a roadway, sound the horn when necessary, and take proper precautions on seeing a child or an obviously confused or incapacitated person on the roadway.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: DRIVERS TO EXERCISE DUE CARE

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Blind Pedestrians
offenses.summary: Only a totally or partially blind person may carry a white cane on a public street. A driver approaching an intersection or crosswalk where a pedestrian with a white cane or assistance animal is crossing must take necessary precautions and come to a full stop if that is the only way to avoid injury or danger.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine up to $500 and 30 hours community service
tiers.when: Collision caused serious bodily injury or death to a blind person

offenses.heading: BLIND PEDESTRIANS

offenses.group: Subtitle C. Rules of the Road
offenses.chapter: Ch. 552 Pedestrians and Other Sidewalk Users
offenses.name: Train Occupying Crossing
offenses.summary: A pedestrian may not move in front of, under, between, or through the cars of a moving or stopped train occupying a railroad crossing.

tiers.when: General traffic penalty (no specific penalty in this section)

offenses.heading: TRAIN OCCUPYING CROSSING

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: General Penalty (Financial Responsibility Act)
offenses.summary: Violating any provision of Chapter 601 with no specific penalty is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $500 and/or up to 90 days in jail.
offenses.heading: VIOLATION OF CHAPTER; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Financial Responsibility (Insurance) Required
offenses.summary: A person may not operate a motor vehicle in Texas unless financial responsibility is established for it through a liability insurance policy meeting state minimums, a surety bond, a cash or securities deposit with the comptroller or county judge, or self-insurance. Driving without it is charged under 601.191.
offenses.heading: REQUIREMENT OF FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Evidence of Financial Responsibility (Proof of Insurance)
offenses.summary: On request, a driver must show a peace officer, or anyone involved in a collision with them, evidence of financial responsibility: the policy or a copy, a standard proof-of-insurance card, an image on a phone provided by the insurer, an insurance binder, or a surety bond, deposit, or self-insurance certificate. A driver who cannot show it is presumed to be uninsured, unless the officer verifies coverage through the state insurance verification program (TexasSure).
offenses.heading: EVIDENCE OF FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: No Insurance (Failure to Maintain Financial Responsibility)
offenses.summary: Operates a motor vehicle without financial responsibility (liability insurance or another approved form) established for it.
offenses.notes: The citation must indicate the officer could not verify coverage through the verification program (subsection (e)). It is a defense if the defendant produces in court proof that was valid at the time (601.193). A second conviction can lead to license suspension unless proof is kept on file with DPS for two years. Driving without insurance also raises driving while license invalid (521.457) and no license (521.025), and a vehicle may be towed (545.305).

tiers.when: First offense (the court may reduce the fine if the defendant cannot pay)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE IN VIOLATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE LIABILITY INSURANCE REQUIREMENT; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Defense: Financial Responsibility in Effect at Time of Alleged Offense
offenses.summary: Not an offense. It is a defense to no-insurance charges (601.191, 601.195) if the person produces in court a proof-of-insurance document that was valid when the offense allegedly occurred; once the court verifies it, the charge must be dismissed.
offenses.heading: DEFENSE: FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY IN EFFECT AT TIME OF ALLEGED OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Operation of Motor Vehicle in Violation of Requirement to Establish Financial Responsibility
offenses.summary: A person required to establish financial responsibility after a suspension or conviction (Subchapters F or K, usually by filing an SR-22) does not maintain the required evidence, and during that period drives a vehicle they own on a highway or knowingly lets an unauthorized person drive it.

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine up to $500 and/or up to 6 months jail

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE IN VIOLATION OF REQUIREMENT TO ESTABLISH FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Operation of Motor Vehicle in Violation of Suspension
offenses.summary: During a period when the person's vehicle registration is suspended under this chapter, knowingly permits a motor vehicle they own to be operated on a highway.
offenses.notes: Affirmative defense: the person had not received notice of the suspension (presumed if mailed or emailed to the address on record).

tiers.level: Misdemeanor: fine $100 to $500 and 72 hours to 6 months jail

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE IN VIOLATION OF SUSPENSION; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle D. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility
offenses.chapter: Ch. 601 Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act
offenses.name: Failure to Return Driver's License or Vehicle Registration
offenses.summary: Willfully fails to send a suspended driver's license or vehicle registration to DPS as required by 601.372.
offenses.heading: FAILURE TO RETURN DRIVER'S LICENSE OR VEHICLE REGISTRATION; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle G. Motorcycles and Electric Bicycles
offenses.chapter: Ch. 661 Protective Headgear for Motorcycle Operators and Passengers
offenses.name: No Motorcycle Helmet
offenses.summary: Operates or rides as a passenger on a motorcycle on a public street or highway without approved protective headgear, or carries a passenger who is not wearing it.
offenses.notes: Exception: the rider is at least 21 and has completed an approved motorcycle safety course or has health insurance covering motorcycle collision injuries. An officer may not cite a rider 21 or older who shows such proof, and may not stop or detain a rider solely to check for it (subsections (c), (c-1)).
offenses.heading: OFFENSES RELATING TO NOT WEARING PROTECTIVE HEADGEAR

offenses.group: Subtitle H. Parking, Towing, and Storage of Vehicles
offenses.name: Illegal Parking in Disabled Space
offenses.summary: Parks or stands a vehicle in a space designated for persons with disabilities (by a political subdivision, or on private property where the city or county has applied this section): with disabled plates or a placard but without authorization under 681.006-681.008 (a); or without disabled plates or a placard (b). Also: blocking an access aisle, curb ramp, or other accessibility improvement (c); lending a placard to someone who misuses it (d); and a non-disabled person using disabled plates or a placard to avoid parking fees or time limits (l). The registered owner is presumed to be the person who parked the vehicle.
offenses.notes: A space without a compliant identification sign may only get a warning, not a citation (subsection (f-2)). Two versions of subsections (h)-(j) were enacted in 2009 and differ in the fine and service hours. Reduced penalties apply when the vehicle has certain veteran plates without a placard (subsections (m)-(o)).

tiers.level: Fine $500 or $550 to $800 and 10 hours community service
tiers.when: One prior conviction (two 2009 versions of the fine range)

tiers.level: Fine $550 to $800 and 20 to 30 hours community service
Fine $800 to $1,100 and 30 or 50 hours community service

offenses.heading: OFFENSES; PRESUMPTION

offenses.group: Subtitle H. Parking, Towing, and Storage of Vehicles
offenses.name: Manufacture, Sale, Possession, or Use of Counterfeit or Altered Placard
offenses.summary: Without TxDMV authorization, manufactures, sells, or possesses a placard deceptively similar to a disabled parking placard, or alters a genuine placard (a); or knowingly parks a vehicle displaying a counterfeit or altered placard in a disabled space (b).

tiers.when: Parking with a counterfeit or altered placard (b)

offenses.heading: MANUFACTURE, SALE, POSSESSION, OR USE OF COUNTERFEIT OR ALTERED PLACARD

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Implied Consent
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A person arrested for an offense arising out of operating a motor vehicle in a public place, or a watercraft, while intoxicated, or for a minor driving under the influence (Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.041), is deemed to have consented to give one or more breath or blood specimens to test for alcohol concentration or drugs. They may also consent to another type of specimen.
offenses.heading: CONSENT TO TAKING OF SPECIMEN

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Taking a Specimen; Mandatory Blood
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A breath or blood specimen may be taken after arrest at the request of an officer with reasonable grounds to believe the person operated a motor vehicle in a public place, or a watercraft, while intoxicated, or violated ABC 106.041. If the person refuses, the officer MUST require a specimen when the person was the operator in a collision the officer reasonably believes resulted from the offense and someone died, will die, or suffered serious bodily injury (blood required); when someone other than the person suffered bodily injury and was taken to a hospital; when the arrest is for DWI with a child passenger (49.045) or BWI with a child passenger (49.061); or when the officer has reliable information that the person has a prior intoxication assault, intoxication manslaughter, or child-passenger conviction or probation, or two or more prior DWI-type convictions or probations. The officer designates the type of specimen. Under (e), the officer may NOT require a specimen unless the officer obtains a warrant or has probable cause that exigent circumstances exist.
offenses.warning: A mandatory specimen without a warrant or genuine exigency violates the Fourth Amendment (State v. Villarreal, Tex. Crim. App. 2014; Missouri v. McNeely, 2013). Get a warrant.
offenses.heading: TAKING OF SPECIMEN

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: No Specimen After Refusal (Except Mandatory Cases)
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Except for the mandatory specimen cases in 724.012(a-1) and (b), a specimen may not be taken if the person refuses the specimen the officer designated. The officer's alternative is to apply for a search warrant.
offenses.heading: PROHIBITION ON TAKING SPECIMEN IF PERSON REFUSES; EXCEPTION

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: DIC-24 Statutory Warning
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Before requesting a specimen, the officer must tell the person orally and in writing that: (1) a refusal may be admissible in a later prosecution; (2) refusing means their license will be automatically suspended for at least 180 days, whether or not they are prosecuted; (3) if they refuse, the officer may apply for a warrant for a specimen; (4) if they are 21 or older and the result shows an alcohol concentration at the Chapter 49 level, the license will be suspended for at least 90 days; (5) if they are under 21 with any detectable alcohol, the license will be suspended for at least 60 days even if they submit (with possibly lesser criminal penalties if below the Chapter 49 level); (6) a Texas resident without a license will be denied a license on the same terms; (7) they may request a hearing on the suspension or denial within 15 days of receiving notice; and (8) a blood specimen will be kept and preserved under CCP 38.50. If the person consents, the officer asks them to sign a statement of consent.
offenses.heading: INFORMATION PROVIDED BY OFFICER BEFORE REQUESTING SPECIMEN; STATEMENT OF CONSENT

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Who May Draw Blood
offenses.summary: Not an offense. Only a physician, qualified technician, registered nurse, licensed vocational nurse, or an EMT-intermediate or paramedic authorized by their medical director under a protocol may take a blood specimen at an officer's request or order. It must be taken in a sanitary place. A person or facility drawing blood according to recognized medical procedures is immune from civil liability (except for negligence); drawing from a person who objects or resists is not in itself negligence.
offenses.heading: TAKING OF BLOOD SPECIMEN

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Defendant's Independent Blood Test
offenses.summary: Not an offense. A person who gives a specimen at an officer's request may, within a reasonable time not to exceed two hours after arrest, have a physician, qualified technician, chemist, or registered nurse of their choosing take an additional blood specimen, and must be given a reasonable opportunity to contact one. The officer is not required to transport them for it, failure to get the test does not keep the state's result out, and the officer and agency are not liable.
offenses.heading: ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS BY REQUEST

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Refusal Statement
offenses.summary: Not an offense. If a person refuses to give a specimen, the officer must ask them to sign a statement that the officer requested a specimen, the person was told the consequences of refusing, and the person refused.
offenses.heading: STATEMENT REQUESTED ON REFUSAL

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.name: Specimen Results Admissible
offenses.summary: Not an offense. In a trial for a Chapter 49 offense involving a motor vehicle or watercraft, or a minor DUI under ABC 106.041, evidence of alcohol concentration or drugs shown by analysis of blood, breath, urine, or another bodily substance taken at an officer's request or order is admissible.
offenses.heading: ADMISSIBILITY IN CRIMINAL PROCEEDING OF SPECIMEN ANALYSIS

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.chapter: Ch. 727 Modification of, Tampering with, and Equipment of Motor Vehicles
offenses.name: Tampering With Odometer
offenses.summary: With intent to defraud, disconnects or resets an odometer to reduce the mileage shown (trip odometers excepted).

tiers.level: Up to 2 years county jail and/or fine up to $1,000
30 days to 2 years county jail and fine up to $2,000

offenses.heading: TAMPERING WITH ODOMETER; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.chapter: Ch. 728 Sale or Transfer of Motor Vehicles and Master Keys
offenses.name: Sale of Master Key for Motor Vehicle Ignitions
offenses.summary: Sells or offers to sell a master key knowingly designed to fit the ignition switch of more than one motor vehicle.
offenses.heading: SALE OF MASTER KEY FOR MOTOR VEHICLE IGNITIONS

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.chapter: Ch. 729 Operation of Motor Vehicle by Minor
offenses.name: Traffic Violation by Minor Under 17
offenses.summary: A person younger than 17 drives on a public road, city street or alley, or public beach in violation of a traffic law (registration, driver's license (other than DWLI), rules of the road, insurance, size and weight, helmet, or disabled parking laws).
offenses.notes: Lets justice and municipal courts handle a juvenile's fine-only traffic offenses. Offenses carrying jail time (such as leaving the scene under 550.021-.025 and DWLI) are excluded and are handled as juvenile conduct.

tiers.level: Same fine or sanction as the underlying traffic law (no jail)

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE BY MINOR IN VIOLATION OF TRAFFIC LAWS; OFFENSE

offenses.group: Subtitle J. Miscellaneous Provisions
offenses.chapter: Ch. 729 Operation of Motor Vehicle by Minor
offenses.name: Minor Driving Without License
offenses.summary: A person younger than 17 drives a motor vehicle on a public road, city street or alley, or public beach without a driver's license authorizing them to do so.
offenses.notes: A vehicle driven by a minor without a license may be towed (545.305).

tiers.level: Same as no driver's license for an adult (521.025), without confinement

offenses.heading: OPERATION OF MOTOR VEHICLE BY MINOR WITHOUT LICENSE

cases.name: Terry v. Ohio
cases.facts: An officer watched men repeatedly walk past and peer into a store window, suspected a robbery was being planned, stopped them, and patted them down, finding guns.
cases.held: An officer may briefly stop a person on reasonable suspicion, based on specific and articulable facts, that criminal activity is afoot. If the officer also reasonably believes the person is armed and dangerous, the officer may pat down outer clothing for weapons.
cases.patrol: Reasonable suspicion for the stop and a separate armed-and-dangerous belief for the frisk. Articulate both in your report.

cases.name: Delaware v. Prouse
cases.facts: An officer stopped a car at random, with no traffic violation or suspicion, just to check the license and registration.
cases.held: Random, suspicionless stops of motorists to check licenses and registration violate the Fourth Amendment.
cases.patrol: Every traffic stop needs reasonable suspicion or probable cause of a violation (or a lawful checkpoint).

cases.name: Whren v. United States
cases.facts: Vice officers stopped a truck for traffic violations, though their real interest was drugs, and saw cocaine in plain view.
cases.held: A traffic stop supported by probable cause of a traffic violation is reasonable regardless of the officer's actual motive.
cases.patrol: "Pretext" stops are lawful under the Fourth Amendment if there is a real violation. Racial profiling is still prohibited by Texas law (CCP 2B.0052).

cases.name: Pennsylvania v. Mimms
cases.facts: During a stop for an expired tag, the officer ordered the driver out of the car and saw a bulge, which turned out to be a gun.
cases.held: Once a vehicle is lawfully stopped, the officer may order the driver out of the car for safety without any additional suspicion.
cases.patrol: You may always order the driver out on a lawful stop.

cases.name: Maryland v. Wilson
cases.facts: An officer ordered a nervous passenger out of a stopped car, and crack cocaine fell to the ground.
cases.held: The Mimms rule extends to passengers: an officer may order passengers out of a lawfully stopped vehicle.
cases.patrol: Passengers may be ordered out (or kept in) during the stop.

cases.name: Brendlin v. California
cases.facts: A passenger was found to have a warrant after a stop that had no lawful basis.
cases.held: A passenger is seized during a traffic stop, just like the driver, and may challenge the legality of the stop.
cases.patrol: A bad stop taints evidence against passengers too.

cases.name: Rodriguez v. United States
cases.facts: After issuing a warning for driving on the shoulder, an officer held the driver seven or eight more minutes for a K-9 sniff.
cases.held: A stop may last no longer than needed to handle its mission (the violation, plus ordinary checks of license, warrants, registration, and insurance). Extending it for a dog sniff or other unrelated investigation without reasonable suspicion violates the Fourth Amendment, even if the delay is short.
cases.patrol: Once the traffic mission is done (or should have been), release the driver unless you have independent reasonable suspicion. Do not slow-walk the citation.

cases.name: Illinois v. Caballes
cases.facts: While one trooper wrote a speeding warning, a second walked a drug dog around the car.
cases.held: A dog sniff during a lawful traffic stop that does not prolong it is not a search.
cases.patrol: A sniff is fine while the stop is still legitimately in progress (see Rodriguez for the limit).

cases.name: Illinois v. Wardlow
cases.facts: A man in a high-narcotics area saw officers and fled; officers caught him and found a gun.
cases.held: Unprovoked headlong flight on seeing police, in a high-crime area, together supported reasonable suspicion for a stop.
cases.patrol: Flight plus location can be enough; neither alone is ideal. Document both.

cases.name: Florida v. J.L.
cases.facts: An anonymous caller said a young man in a plaid shirt at a bus stop had a gun. Officers found him and frisked him.
cases.held: A bare anonymous tip that a person is carrying a gun, with no predictive information or indicia of reliability, does not justify a stop and frisk.
cases.patrol: Corroborate anonymous tips with your own observations before detaining.

cases.name: Navarette v. California
cases.facts: A 911 caller reported that a specific truck had just run her off the road. Officers found and stopped it about 18 minutes later.
cases.held: A 911 call reporting a contemporaneous, eyewitness account of dangerous driving had enough reliability to give reasonable suspicion of drunk driving.
cases.patrol: Detailed, firsthand 911 reports of dangerous driving can justify a stop without seeing a violation yourself.

cases.name: Heien v. North Carolina
cases.facts: An officer stopped a car with one broken brake light, believing that was a violation; the state court later held one working light was enough.
cases.held: A reasonable mistake of law can supply reasonable suspicion for a stop. The mistake must be objectively reasonable, such as a genuinely ambiguous statute.
cases.patrol: Know the traffic code. This protects only reasonable mistakes about unclear laws, not ignorance of clear ones.

cases.name: Kansas v. Glover
cases.facts: A plate check showed the registered owner's license was revoked, and the deputy stopped the truck without seeing who was driving.
cases.held: Absent information that the owner is not the driver (for example, a driver who clearly does not match the owner's description), it is reasonable to infer the owner is driving, so the stop was lawful.
cases.patrol: An owner-suspended return supports a stop unless you see something that rules the owner out.

cases.name: Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial District Court of Nevada
cases.facts: A man detained on reasonable suspicion refused 11 times to identify himself and was convicted under Nevada's stop-and-identify law.
cases.held: A state law requiring a lawfully detained suspect to state their name does not violate the Fourth or Fifth Amendment.
cases.patrol: Texas is different: under Penal Code 38.02 a person must give name, address, and date of birth only after a lawful arrest. Giving false information while lawfully detained is an offense.
cases.note: Texas has no general stop-and-identify requirement for detained persons.

cases.name: Florida v. Bostick
cases.facts: Officers boarded a bus, approached a passenger, and asked to search his bag.
cases.held: The test for a seizure is whether a reasonable person would feel free to decline the officers' requests or otherwise end the encounter, considering all the circumstances.
cases.patrol: Consensual encounters require no suspicion, but your words and actions must not convey that compliance is required.

cases.name: Michigan v. Long
cases.facts: Deputies found a driver who had swerved into a ditch and saw a knife on the floorboard; they searched the passenger area for weapons and found marijuana.
cases.held: Officers may search the passenger compartment, limited to places a weapon could be, if they reasonably believe the suspect is dangerous and may gain immediate control of a weapon.
cases.patrol: A "vehicle frisk" needs the same armed-and-dangerous belief as a person frisk.

cases.name: Arizona v. Johnson
cases.facts: During a stop for a registration violation, an officer frisked a passenger wearing gang colors and found a gun.
cases.held: During a lawful traffic stop, an officer may frisk a driver or passenger reasonably suspected of being armed and dangerous, without separate suspicion of other criminal activity.
cases.patrol: You do not need suspicion that the passenger committed a crime to frisk, only that they are armed and dangerous.

cases.name: Minnesota v. Dickerson
cases.facts: During a frisk, an officer felt a small lump in a pocket that was not a weapon, then squeezed and manipulated it to determine it was crack cocaine.
cases.held: An officer may seize contraband felt during a lawful pat-down if its identity is immediately apparent ("plain feel"). Continued manipulation after concluding it is not a weapon exceeds the frisk.
cases.patrol: Once you know it is not a weapon, stop. Seize it only if it is immediately apparent as contraband.

cases.name: Carroll v. United States
cases.facts: Prohibition agents stopped and searched a car they had probable cause to believe was carrying liquor.
cases.held: Because vehicles are mobile, officers with probable cause that a vehicle contains contraband may search it without a warrant (the automobile exception).
cases.patrol: Probable cause plus a vehicle readily mobile on the road equals a lawful warrantless search.

cases.name: California v. Acevedo
